atoms.claim: 在治疗情境中谈论自己本身就是一种益处，因为人们独自思考时容易在想法和感受中迷失。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Talking about yourself in this context is a benefit in and of itself, because in general when people are left on their own to figure things out they tend to go astray in their thoughts and feelings.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 心理治疗中的亲近他人
atoms.canonical_name_en: getting closer to others in psychotherapy
atoms.claim: 心理治疗还涉及让他人进入自己的生活，敢于信任他人并建立联结，让他人变得重要。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: But psychotherapy involves even more. It also deals with getting closer to other people—letting others into one’s life, that is, daring to trust others and make bonds with others, letting others become significant in one’s life.

atoms.claim: MBT治疗包括每周一次个体和团体治疗，持续18个月，并制定问题表述、危机计划、角色责任、目标以及机构整合。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗结构明确，有助于患者理解治疗框架
atoms.evidence_excerpt: After agreeing a treatment contract for individual and group MBT once per week for 18 months, each person works with a clinician to achieve the following: 1 Mentalization-based problem formulation 2 Crisis plans 3 Agreement on roles and responsibilities 4 Understanding and agreeing immediate and long-term goals 5 Integration between agencies if they are currently involved, for example, work rehabilitation, probation, and social services.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了MBT治疗结构

atoms.claim: MBT项目中患者之间不允许发展亲密关系，若发生则至少一人需离开并另寻治疗。
therapeutic_implications: 维护治疗边界，防止治疗复杂化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Intimate relationships between patients attending the MBT program are not permitted, and if such a relationship should develop then at least one of the individuals will have to leave and seek therapy elsewhere.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了亲密关系禁令

atoms.claim: MBT治疗师采用心智化立场，即对他人心智、经验、想法和感受保持好奇，持“不知”态度，尝试多种可能性。
therapeutic_implications: 促进患者发展自己的解决方案
atoms.evidence_excerpt: the mentalizing stance means being curious about other people’s minds, about their experiences, thoughts, and feelings—a “not-knowing” attitude in which one attempts to find out by trying many different alternatives.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了心智化立场

atoms.claim: MBT是一种协作努力，治疗师寻求让患者参与进来。
therapeutic_implications: 强调治疗师与患者的合作
atoms.evidence_excerpt: MBT is a collaborative effort in which the clinicians seek to get the patients to come along
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了协作努力

atoms.claim: 要求参与者尝试用心理化立场（探索性、好奇、开放于其他理解等）来理解这些事件。
therapeutic_implications: 鼓励采用探索性、好奇、开放的态度
atoms.evidence_excerpt: That they try to understand more about these events using a mentalizing stance—exploratory, curious, open to alternative understandings, etc.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用原文。

atoms.claim: 要求其他团体成员通过心理化立场参与探索自己和他人的问题。
therapeutic_implications: 团体成员相互支持心理化过程
atoms.evidence_excerpt: That other group members participate in this process by exploring their own problems and those of others through a mentalizing stance.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用原文。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 团体事件的心理化探索
atoms.claim: 要求所有人一起尝试以同样的方式探索团体中发生的事件。
therapeutic_implications: 将心理化应用于团体互动
atoms.evidence_excerpt: That everyone together tries to find out about events in the group in the same way.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用原文。

atoms.claim: 要求参与者尝试与团体、团体成员和临床医生建立联结。
therapeutic_implications: 促进治疗联盟和团体凝聚力
atoms.evidence_excerpt: That they try to bond to the group, its members, and the clinicians.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用原文。

atoms.claim: MBT的目标是增强亲密关系中的心理化能力。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗聚焦于改善关系中的心理化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Aim of MBT—to enhance mentalizing ability in close relationships
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用原文总结部分。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 小组活动：讨论治疗关系中的困难
atoms.canonical_name_en: Group activity: Discuss difficulties in therapy relationship
atoms.claim: 小组活动要求成员讨论与个体临床医生、小组临床医生以及其他小组成员形成治疗关系时可能遇到的困难。
clinical_signals: 患者表达对形成依恋关系的常见反对意见，如认为关系痛苦且无意义、注定失败、人们会背叛或让人失望、依恋涉及关心他人、无法信任他人
therapeutic_implications: 激活广泛的依恋主题，讨论可能变得混乱，小组领导者可在一段时间后通过分别讨论与个体临床医生、小组临床医生和其他小组成员的关系来帮助结构化讨论
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Group activity: Discuss the difficulties you think you may run up against when you form a therapy relationship with: 1  The individual clinician 2  The group clinician 3  The other group members.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了小组活动的内容和目的。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 依恋方面的常见反对意见
atoms.canonical_name_en: Common objections to forming affiliative relationships
atoms.claim: 患者对形成依恋关系的常见反对意见包括：认为关系痛苦且无意义（因为知道很快会分离）、注定失败、人们会背叛或让人失望、依恋涉及关心他人、无法信任他人。
clinical_signals: 患者表达上述反对意见
therapeutic_implications: 这些反对意见是小组讨论中需要处理的依恋主题
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Common objections to forming affiliative relationships include: ◆ Belief that it is both painful and meaningless when you know that you will soon be separated from the other person ◆ They are doomed to failure ◆ People will always betray you/let you down ◆ Attachment involves caring about another person ◆ You cannot trust people.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确列出了常见反对意见。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 对与所有个体建立依恋的质疑
atoms.canonical_name_en: Questioning whether it is possible to bond with all individuals
atoms.claim: 其他人可能质疑是否可能与列出的所有个体建立依恋，因为一个人需要喜欢与之建立依恋的人，而患者可能不喜欢临床医生或其他小组成员。
clinical_signals: 患者质疑与所有治疗关系对象建立依恋的可能性
therapeutic_implications: 需要讨论喜欢与依恋的关系
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Others may question whether it is possible to bond with all the individuals listed: after all, one needs to like the people one bonds with, and one may not like the clinicians or other group members.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了患者的质疑。

atoms.claim: 依恋可能导致想要更多，例如希望在困难时联系临床医生。
clinical_signals: 患者表达在困难时联系临床医生的愿望
therapeutic_implications: 需要讨论依恋带来的额外需求
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Still others may raise the issue that attachment can lead to wanting more, such as a wish to contact the clinician whenever things are difficult.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了依恋可能带来的需求。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 与不透露私生活的临床医生建立依恋的困难
atoms.canonical_name_en: Difficulty bonding with clinician who does not share private life
atoms.claim: 患者可能提出如何与不透露自己私生活的临床医生建立依恋的问题。
clinical_signals: 患者对临床医生不透露私生活感到困惑
therapeutic_implications: 需要讨论治疗关系中自我暴露的边界
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The question of how you can bond with someone who doesn’t say anything about his/her own private life may also be raised.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了患者的疑问。

atoms.claim: 澄清误解和敏感的内心感受是MBT的核心要素。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗中应主动澄清误解和敏感感受
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Clarifying misunderstandings and sensitive interpersonal feelings is a central element of MBT.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确陈述澄清误解是核心要素。

atoms.claim: 对临床医生和他人的个人反应往往有“地下”倾向，即未被言说。
therapeutic_implications: 需要将地下感受明确化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Personal reactions to clinicians and other people often have a tendency to “go underground.”
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确描述个人反应有地下倾向。

atoms.claim: 未满足需求的经验是扩展治疗理解的丰富教学领域，治疗师应花时间探索。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应花时间探索未满足需求的经验
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The experience of one’s needs and wishes not being met is a very important and rich pedagogic area to expand understanding of therapy, so the group leader may spend some time on this.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确建议花时间探索。

atoms.claim: 焦虑和抑郁症状常与依恋过程相关，是寻求治疗的主要动机。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗需处理与依恋过程相关的焦虑和抑郁
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In this and the next session we will deal with anxiety and depression to the extent that they are related to attachment process.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确将焦虑抑郁与依恋过程关联。

atoms.claim: 许多参与者可能表示他们天生焦虑，且恐惧来源未知，这使得他们更难处理问题。
therapeutic_implications: 在团体中讨论并探索恐惧来源
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Many of the participants may say that they are intrinsically anxious and the source of their fear is unknown. This makes it much more difficult for them to address the problem.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 恐慌发作的生理心理特征
atoms.claim: 恐惧强度可能过大，导致个体的身心过程无法妥善处理；自主神经系统可能超负荷，引发恐慌发作，其特征包括心率加快、呼吸困难、头晕、害怕晕倒、死亡、发疯或失控等。
clinical_signals: 害怕晕倒/死亡/发疯/失控
therapeutic_implications: 在团体中讨论恐慌发作体验
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The intensity of fear can be so strong that the person’s physical and mental processes may not handle it properly. The autonomic nervous system can become overloaded, causing the individual to experience a panic attack; this is characterized by increased heart rate, difficulty breathing, dizziness, and fear of fainting, dying, going mad, or simply losing control, etc.

atoms.claim: 焦虑障碍的治疗涉及控制性暴露，暴露必须带来掌控和控制的体验，而非挫败。
therapeutic_implications: 暴露治疗应确保患者体验到掌控和控制
暴露治疗不应让患者感到挫败
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Treatment of anxiety disorders involves controlled exposure. Simply exposing the person to the situation that triggers their anxiety is usually not enough in itself. It is necessary for the exposure to be done in a manner that implies an experience of mastery and control, not defeat.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 焦虑的最佳解药是另一个能安抚的人
atoms.canonical_name_en: the best remedy for anxiety is a calming other person
atoms.claim: 焦虑的最佳解药是一个能安抚的他人。
therapeutic_implications: 在焦虑情境中，与可信赖的人在一起有助于缓解焦虑
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The fact remains, however, that the best remedy for anxiety is a calming other person.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 不理想的安抚互动导致儿童独自应对恐惧
atoms.canonical_name_en: non-ideal soothing interaction leads child to handle fear alone
atoms.claim: 当安抚互动不理想时，儿童可能认为恐惧必须独自处理，甚至隐藏恐惧体验。
therapeutic_implications: 需要修复早期不理想的安抚互动带来的影响
atoms.evidence_excerpt: However, this interaction will not always be ideal, for different reasons (as we discussed in Module 6), and this can leave the child continuing to feel frightened or feeling that it is useless or even worse than useless to approach others, leading to the conclusion that fear has to be handled by oneself alone, or even that one has to hide one’s experience of fear.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 可信赖的人的存在降低焦虑并帮助放松
atoms.canonical_name_en: presence of trusted person reduces anxiety and helps relaxation
atoms.claim: 可信赖的人的存在能降低焦虑，帮助个体放松和管理症状。
therapeutic_implications: 在暴露治疗中，治疗师作为可信赖的人提供支持
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The presence of the trusted person reduces anxiety and they can help the individual to relax and manage their symptoms.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 成功完成暴露任务带来掌控感
atoms.canonical_name_en: successful completion of exposure task gives experience of mastery
atoms.claim: 在可信赖的人陪伴下完成暴露任务，给焦虑者带来掌控和控制的体验。
therapeutic_implications: 暴露治疗应设计为让患者成功完成任务，获得掌控感
atoms.evidence_excerpt: This gives the anxious person an experience of mastery and control when the journey is accomplished.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 谈论个人焦虑时的内在阻力
atoms.canonical_name_en: Resistance when talking about personal anxieties
atoms.claim: 当试图公开谈论个人焦虑时，患者通常会体验到一种内在的阻力，这可能与羞耻感、感到幼稚无助、不信任他人或担心被嘲笑有关。
therapeutic_implications: 需要处理患者对公开焦虑的抵抗
atoms.evidence_excerpt: When trying to be open about personal anxieties, one will often experience a kind of resistance within oneself. This may be related to the fact that fear is often connected with shame, or that one gets an uneasy feeling of being childish and helpless, or that one does not trust that the other has the capacity to be helpful or, worse, may misuse the information to ridicule or shame them.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了内在阻力的可能原因。

atoms.claim: 焦虑容易泛化到其他领域，例如对电梯的焦虑变成对封闭空间的恐惧。
therapeutic_implications: 注意焦虑的泛化模式
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Anxiety can easily generalize to other areas—for example, anxiety about being in lifts becomes fear of enclosed spaces.
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自模块11的总结。

atoms.claim: 焦虑障碍的治疗通常涉及控制性暴露。
therapeutic_implications: 采用控制性暴露技术
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Treatments for anxiety disorders typically involve controlled exposure
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自模块11的总结。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 信任陪伴下的焦虑管理
atoms.canonical_name_en: Managing anxiety with a trusted person
atoms.claim: 研究表明，当人们在信任的人陪伴下接近触发情境时，能够更好地管理焦虑。
therapeutic_implications: 鼓励患者在信任的人陪伴下面对焦虑情境
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Studies have shown that people are able to manage anxiety better when they approach the triggering situation in the company of a trusted person
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自模块11的总结。

atoms.claim: 丧失不一定指死亡，也可以是长期旅行、被送离家庭、依恋对象生病或不可得、父母离婚、搬家失去朋友，或失去社会地位。
therapeutic_implications: 探索患者经历的各种丧失形式
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The “loss” does not need to be a death: it could be that someone travels away for a long period of time, that you yourself are sent away from your family, that the attachment person is ill and unavailable, that one’s parents divorce, or that one moves away and loses close friends. Or, rather than the loss of a person, it may involve the loss of social standing and social position, for example, by being disgraced in public in some way.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确列举了多种非死亡的丧失形式。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 早期丧失与抑郁易感性
atoms.claim: 如果一个人在年幼时经历过严重丧失且哀伤反应未得到良好处理，成年后遭遇丧失时更容易出现抑郁。
therapeutic_implications: 关注患者童年期的丧失经历及其处理情况
atoms.evidence_excerpt: If a person has experienced a serious loss at a young age that led to a poorly processed grief reaction, that person will be more disposed to depression after a loss in adult life.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述早期丧失与成年后抑郁易感性的关联。

atoms.claim: 抑郁发作次数越多，再次抑郁的可能性越大，似乎形成了一种对压力和不适的自动反应模式。
therapeutic_implications: 识别并干预自动化的抑郁反应模式
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The more depressive episodes one has had, the more likely one is to experience depression again. It is as if one establishes an automatic response pattern to stress and discomfort.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述抑郁发作次数与复发风险的关系及自动反应模式的概念。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 哀伤反应与抑郁的差异
atoms.canonical_name_en: difference between grief reaction and depression
atoms.claim: 强烈的哀伤反应与抑郁非常相似，但在性质上有所不同。
therapeutic_implications: 区分哀伤反应与抑郁，避免误诊
atoms.evidence_excerpt: An intense grief reaction is quite similar to depression, although qualitatively different.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述哀伤反应与抑郁的相似性和质性差异。

atoms.claim: 小组领导者必须公开说明每位参与者都有机会谈论自己的经历，并且可用时间应平均分配。
therapeutic_implications: 确保所有成员都有机会发言，避免只听取少数人的详细故事而忽略其他人。
response_constraints: 如果为每人留出五分钟，八人小组的活动将耗时四十分钟。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The group leader must say openly to the group that it is important that everyone is given a chance to talk about their experiences, and the available time should be divided equally.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确的小组领导原则，关于时间分配和公平参与。

atoms.claim: 抗抑郁药有时对焦虑和惊恐发作也有效，并能减少因情绪普遍不稳定引起的强烈情绪波动。
clinical_signals: 情绪普遍不稳定导致的强烈情绪波动
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Antidepressants can sometimes also be effective for anxiety and panic attacks, and they can also reduce strong mood swings that are due to general emotional instability.
atoms.extraction_notes: 关于抗抑郁药额外适应症的陈述。

atoms.claim: 抑郁与分离焦虑和悲伤的基本情绪密切相关。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Depression is closely connected to the basic emotions of separation anxiety and sadness
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述抑郁与基本情绪的联系。

atoms.claim: 依恋反应系统通过进化发展而来，因为它对儿童与依恋对象的关系有益。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: This attachment response system has developed through evolution, because it turns out to be beneficial for the relationships between children and their attachment figures
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述依恋反应系统的进化起源。

atoms.claim: 抑郁思维模式表明心智化丧失。
therapeutic_implications: 当患者表现出抑郁思维模式时，提示需要恢复心智化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Depressive thought patterns indicate a loss of mentalizing.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述，无额外推断。

atoms.canonical_name_en: ending the group and loss of attachment
atoms.claim: 结束团体可以与团体过程中建立的依恋丧失过程相关联。
therapeutic_implications: 团体领导者应关注患者对团体结束的感受
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Of course, ending the group can be linked to the loss of attachment processes that have built up over the course of the group.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 团体过程不能放任自流
atoms.canonical_name_en: Group process cannot be left to the group
atoms.claim: 在MBT中，团体过程不能放任自流，临床医生必须管理团体以确保焦点并防止过程崩溃为非心智化模式。
therapeutic_implications: 临床医生需要主动管理团体焦点
atoms.evidence_excerpt: As such, the group process cannot be left to the group. The clinician “manages” the group to ensure focus and to prevent the process collapsing into nonmentalizing modes.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述团体过程不能放任自流，临床医生需管理以防止非心智化。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 团体治疗中的心智化复杂性
atoms.canonical_name_en: Complexity of mentalizing in group therapy
atoms.claim: 团体治疗中，BPD患者需要监控和回应六到九个心智，而非像个体治疗中只关注两个，这增加了心智化的复杂性。
therapeutic_implications: 团体治疗对BPD患者更具挑战性
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Yet group therapy is one of the more difficult aspects of treatment for BPD patients, who have the task of monitoring and responding to six to nine minds in the group, rather than being able to focus on only two as in individual therapy.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述BPD患者在团体中需监控更多心智，增加了难度。

atoms.claim: 在MBT中，心智化是关于核心问题和日常生活中的情绪显著事件，对于BPD和ASPD患者而言，这些是边缘性或反社会人格障碍患者面临的问题。
therapeutic_implications: 团体讨论应聚焦于核心问题和情绪显著事件
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In MBT for BPD and ASPD it is about the core problems and emotionally salient events of everyday life faced by patients with borderline or antisocial personality disorders.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述MBT团体治疗的内容聚焦于核心问题和情绪显著事件。

atoms.claim: MBT临床医生必须在过度管理和疏于管理之间取得平衡。
clinical_signals: 群体过程可能失控或缺乏结构
therapeutic_implications: 需要主动管理群体，同时允许人际心理化发展
response_constraints: 避免过度控制或放任不管
atoms.evidence_excerpt: So MBT clinicians must navigate between the Scylla and Charybdis of over-management and under-management, authority and benign neglect, over-control and possible chaos, in the group.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述了平衡的必要性。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 关注显性-隐性心理化维度
atoms.canonical_name_en: Attention to explicit-implicit dimension of mentalizing
atoms.claim: 在临床实践中，临床医生需要持续关注心理化的显性-隐性维度。
clinical_signals: 群体互动中隐含的心理化过程
therapeutic_implications: 将隐性过程显性化，并让患者专注于显性过程
response_constraints: 在显性和隐性理解之间灵活转换
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In clinical practice, this means constant attention on the part of the clinician to the explicit–implicit dimension of mentalizing.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述了临床医生的持续关注。

atoms.claim: 隐性心理化是自动的、程序性的、自然的，且低于意识水平。
clinical_signals: 患者无意识地监控自己和他人
therapeutic_implications: 需要将隐性过程显性化以促进心理化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: implicit mentalizing is automatic, procedural, natural, and below the level of consciousness.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接定义。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 临床医生维持权威并管理群体
atoms.canonical_name_en: Clinician maintains authority and manages the group
atoms.claim: MBT-G中临床医生维持权威并管理群体，不等待群体自行处理。
therapeutic_implications: 主动管理群体互动
response_constraints: 不采取放任态度
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Clinician maintains authority and manages the group—does not wait to see how the group “deals with it”
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自Box 12.1。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 临床医生积极促进群体互动
atoms.claim: MBT-G中临床医生积极促进群体互动。
therapeutic_implications: 鼓励患者之间的交流
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Clinician actively promotes group interaction
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自Box 12.1。

atoms.claim: MBT-G关注心理化的显性-隐性维度。
clinical_signals: 群体过程中显性和隐性心理化交替
therapeutic_implications: 在显性和隐性之间转换
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Attention to implicit–explicit dimension of mentalizing.
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自Box 12.1。

atoms.claim: 当我们心智化他人时，我们监控他们的心理状态，理解他们的观点、情绪状态和潜在动机。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: When we mentalize others we monitor their mental states, taking in their point of view, their emotional states, and a sense of their underlying motives.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述心智化他人的过程。

atoms.claim: 在顺利的心智化互动中，双方的心理状态会相互协调变化，彼此都受到对方的影响而改变。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: We intuitively reflect on these and, when things go smoothly, our mind states change in tune with theirs; we take pleasure in the interaction as it progresses and we see that not only have we changed them a little but we, too, have been changed.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述心智化互动中的相互影响。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: MBT-G中临床医生的积极参与和“不知”立场
atoms.canonical_name_en: active participant and not-knowing stance in MBT-G
atoms.claim: 在MBT-G中，临床医生是积极的参与者，采取“不知”和非专家的立场。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: ◆ Clinician is an active participant adopting a “not-knowing,” non-expert stance
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自Box 12.2，明确列出MBT-G的特点。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: MBT-G中临床医生使自己的思考明确、透明且可理解
atoms.canonical_name_en: clinician makes own thinking explicit, transparent, and understandable in MBT-G
atoms.claim: 在MBT-G中，临床医生使自己的思考明确、透明且可理解。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: ◆ Clinician makes his/her own thinking explicit, transparent, and understandable
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自Box 12.2，明确列出MBT-G的特点。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: MBT-G中临床医生保持会话流程和结构
atoms.canonical_name_en: clinician maintains flow and structure of session in MBT-G
atoms.claim: 在MBT-G中，治疗依赖于“积极”的临床医生维持会话的流程和结构，而不是采取从属于团体过程的立场。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: ◆ Therapy relies on an “active” clinician maintaining the flow and structure of the session rather than adopting a position secondary to group process.
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自Box 12.2，明确列出MBT-G的特点。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: MBT-G鼓励关系好奇心的团体文化
atoms.canonical_name_en: MBT-G encourages group culture of relational curiosity
atoms.claim: MBT-G鼓励一种关系好奇心的团体文化，而不是提出复杂的关系假设。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: ◆ MBT-G encourages a group culture of relational curiosity rather than suggesting complex relational hypotheses
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自Box 12.2，明确列出MBT-G的特点。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 避免过早提供解决方案
atoms.claim: 治疗师应避免过早提供解决方案，因为这可能使患者更难自己解决问题。
clinical_signals: 患者快速给出解决方案
患者接受他人建议作为唯一答案
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应阻止快速解决方案被隐含地接受为答案
促进对心理状态和人际过程的明确关注
response_constraints: 治疗师应要求患者探索自己的不确定感
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Giving her a final solution might make it more difficult for her to work it out.
atoms.extraction_notes: 干预原则：避免过早提供解决方案，以促进患者自己的思考。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 隐含心智化自我与他人的描述是人类完美状态
atoms.canonical_name_en: Implicit mentalizing of self and other as human perfection
atoms.claim: 实现隐含心智化自我与他人的描述是人类完美状态，大多数人只能偶尔达到，在严重人格障碍患者群体中很少见。
clinical_signals: 患者群体为严重人格障碍
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应设定现实目标，促进隐含与明确心智化之间的运动
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Achieving this description of implicit mentalizing of self and other as described here is human perfection, achieved only occasionally by most people for any length of time and rarely in a group of patients with severe personality disorder.
atoms.extraction_notes: 心智化概念：隐含心智化自我与他人的描述是罕见的人类完美状态。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 探索患者之间的隐含过程
atoms.claim: 在互动中，患者之间存在需要探索的隐含过程，例如一个患者认为另一个患者软弱。
clinical_signals: 患者之间快速给出建议
患者接受建议后感到困惑
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应明确探索隐含的人际过程
atoms.evidence_excerpt: within the interaction there is implicit process between Rose and Kate that needs exploration, for example, a sense that Kate thinks Rose is being weak, perhaps.
atoms.extraction_notes: 干预原则：探索患者之间的隐含过程，如认为对方软弱。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 阻止隐含接受解决方案
atoms.canonical_name_en: Prevent implicit acceptance of a solution
atoms.claim: 治疗师应阻止解决方案被隐含地接受为问题的答案。
clinical_signals: 患者快速给出解决方案
其他患者似乎接受该解决方案
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应明确指出快速回答的潜在影响
促进对心理状态的明确关注
response_constraints: 治疗师应要求患者探索自己的不确定感
atoms.evidence_excerpt: not to allow the suggested solution to become implicitly accepted as the answer to the problem.
atoms.extraction_notes: 干预原则：阻止隐含接受解决方案。

atoms.claim: 临床医生立场包括：权威但不专制、维持焦点、监控唤醒水平和非心智化模式、在可能的当前心理现实中工作、维持临床医生心智化并示范心智化。
therapeutic_implications: 临床医生需要监控团体唤醒水平和非心智化模式
临床医生需要在当前心理现实中工作
临床医生需要维持自身心智化并示范心智化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: ◆ Authority without being authoritarian ◆ Maintain focus and do not allow persistent nonmentalizing dialogue ◆ Monitor arousal levels and nonmentalizing modes; beware of hypermentalizing ◆ Work in current mental reality when possible ◆ Maintain clinician mentalizing and model mentalizing.
atoms.extraction_notes: Box 12.3 明确列出临床医生立场原则。

atoms.claim: 临床医生权威包括：公开反复解释团体的首要任务、维持结构并陈述团体原则、保持积极和参与的立场、通过指出和赞扬心智化来表扬团体、维持焦点并控制团体节奏。
therapeutic_implications: 临床医生需要公开解释团体任务
临床医生需要维持结构并陈述原则
临床医生需要表扬心智化行为
atoms.evidence_excerpt: ◆ Clinician openly and repeatedly explains the primary task of the group ◆ Maintains structure and states group principles ◆ Maintains an active and participating stance ◆ Praises the group by pointing out and acclaiming mentalizing when it happens ◆ Maintains focus and paces the group.
atoms.extraction_notes: Box 12.4 明确列出临床医生权威的具体行为。

atoms.claim: 临床医生积极监控整个团体和每个个体的焦虑水平，确保其处于最佳状态，既不过高也不过低。
therapeutic_implications: 避免过度唤起导致失控
避免情绪表达不足和过度理智化阻碍心智化发展
atoms.evidence_excerpt: the clinician actively monitors the anxiety levels of the whole group and of each individual in the group to ensure they are optimal and become neither too high nor too low.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述临床医生的监控行为及其目的。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 即时干预以增加心智化
atoms.claim: 旨在在当下时刻增加团体内心智化的干预是团体建设性发展的关键。
therapeutic_implications: 大部分工作在当下心理现实中完成
同时考虑过去和未来作为当前现实的一部分
atoms.evidence_excerpt: interventions that aim to increase mentalizing within the group in the immediacy of the moment form the key to constructive development of the group.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述即时干预的重要性。

atoms.claim: 如果团体中有两位临床医生，他们互相交谈，阐述或质疑对方的话，甚至挑战对方，这模拟了心智化的互动过程，并表明分歧可以是迈向更好理解的积极一步。
therapeutic_implications: 模拟心智化互动过程
展示分歧的积极价值
atoms.evidence_excerpt: If two clinicians are in the group they talk to each other, in turn elaborating or questioning what the other says, and even challenging each other. This models the mentalizing interactive process and shows that disagreement can be a positive step toward better understanding.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述双临床医生互动的目的和效果。

atoms.claim: 临床医生应使用一致的情感体验参与团体。
therapeutic_implications: 通过情感共鸣参与
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Participate using concordant affective experience.
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自Box 12.5的提示，明确列出。

atoms.claim: 临床医生应关注小组中的每个成员，而不仅仅是正在发言的人。
therapeutic_implications: 旨在随时评估每个成员的理解/心智化状态。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: ◆ Give attention to each member of the group (not just the one speaking) ◆ Aim to gauge understanding/mentalizing of each member at all times
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用自Box 12.6之前的要点。

atoms.canonical_name_en: Hybrid role of floor manager and dinner party host
atoms.claim: 临床医生的角色是“场地管理员”和“晚宴主人”的混合体。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: ◆ Role is a hybrid of “floor manager” and “dinner party host.”
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用自Box 12.6之前的要点。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 暂停讨论处理并发活动
atoms.canonical_name_en: Pause discussion to address concurrent activity
atoms.claim: 当小组中出现并发活动时，应暂停当前讨论，邀请小组关注该活动，待其解决后再返回暂停的讨论。
clinical_signals: 小组中出现可能表明情绪反应的并发活动
therapeutic_implications: 在并发活动变得不可控之前进行处理。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: ◆ Put the current group discussion “on hold” while the group is invited to attend to the concurrent activity before it gathers momentum and becomes unmanageable. Once the concurrent activity is resolved, return to the “paused” group discussion.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用自Box 12.6。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: MBT团体治疗中临床医生数量
atoms.canonical_name_en: Number of clinicians in MBT group
atoms.claim: 没有证据表明MBT团体治疗中配备一名或两名临床医生在团体过程、患者保留率或治疗结果方面更优。
therapeutic_implications: 决定配备一名或两名临床医生可能更多取决于成本和人员配置等实际问题，而非有充分证据支持的临床过程。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: there is no evidence to suggest that having either one or two is superior in terms of group process, retention of patients in treatment, or outcomes.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确陈述无证据表明优劣，故为explicit。

atoms.claim: 只有一名临床医生可以鼓励一致且专注的团体文化，并且更具成本效益。
therapeutic_implications: 一名临床医生有助于维持团体焦点和一致性，且对服务更经济。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Having only one clinician encourages a consistent and focused group culture and, on a practical note, is likely to be more cost-effective for services.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确陈述这些优势。

atoms.claim: 通常建议患者不要在小组外相互接触，除非是治疗计划的一部分（例如社区治疗项目中的同伴支持）。
therapeutic_implications: 限制小组外社交以避免负面影响，但需考虑个体差异
atoms.evidence_excerpt: As a rule, all recommend that patients do not contact each other outside the group unless it is part of a treatment plan, for example, peer support in a community-based therapeutic program.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述关于小组外社交的一般建议。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 小组外社交的潜在影响
atoms.claim: 小组外社交可能对某些个体有积极影响，但也可能让其他小组成员感到被排斥、被背后议论、怨恨，甚至要求临床医生制止。
clinical_signals: 其他成员感到被排斥或怨恨
therapeutic_implications: 需平衡个体获益与小组整体动力
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The effects may be positive for some individuals but less so for other group members, who can feel excluded, talked about behind their backs, resentful, and may even demand that the clinician puts a stop to it.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述小组外社交的双重影响。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 小组前和小组后的社交
atoms.claim: 小组前见面和小组后聊天通常被容忍和忽略，但小组之间的接触更有问题。
therapeutic_implications: 区分不同时间点的小组外社交，管理重点在于小组之间的接触
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Meeting up beforehand and chatting afterwards is usually tolerated and ignored. It is the between-group contact that is more problematic.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接区分小组前/后社交与小组间社交的不同处理。

atoms.claim: 在MBT-G中，临床医生在管理小组时承担一定程度的权威，但这不应被解释为变得专横。
therapeutic_implications: 临床医生需在权威与灵活性之间保持平衡
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It has already been mentioned that in MBT-G the clinician takes a level of authority in managing the group. This should not be interpreted as becoming
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接提及临床医生的权威角色，但句子不完整，仅提取已有内容。

atoms.claim: 在MBT-G中，小组外活动应作为需要额外讨论的“问题”来处理，包括治疗师公开表达自己的观点。
clinical_signals: 患者之间在小组外有接触
therapeutic_implications: 将小组外活动视为需要讨论的问题，而非直接禁止
response_constraints: 避免威权式回应，如直接禁止或威胁终止治疗
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Contact between groups is taken to be a “problem” that needs additional discussion, which includes the clinician presenting his/her views openly.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确将小组外接触视为需要讨论的问题，并包含治疗师公开观点。

atoms.claim: 每次小组会议以对上次会议的简要总结开始，由治疗师进行，但鼓励患者补充。
therapeutic_implications: 帮助缺席者跟上主题，并作为所有人的提醒
atoms.evidence_excerpt: We start with a brief summary of the previous group. This allows anyone who was unable to attend the previous session to catch up with the main themes and it acts as a reminder for all of us. One of us [the clinicians] will do the summary, but it is often helpful if any of you have something to add.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文是治疗师对新小组的引言，明确描述了总结环节。

atoms.claim: 随着时间的推移，小组结构成为小组文化的一部分，新加入的成员可以快速了解模式。
therapeutic_implications: 结构内化，便于新成员融入
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Over time, the structure becomes part of the culture of the group and new members who join the group can be quickly introduced to the pattern.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确说明结构随时间成为文化的一部分。

atoms.claim: 从团体开始到整个团体生命周期，必须尽可能清晰地阐明并反复重申团体目的。
therapeutic_implications: 当患者提问时，需重新陈述并探讨触发因素，将隐含内容明确化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The purpose needs to be as clear as possible throughout the “life” of the group and, at times, it may be necessary to revisit some of the information provided in the MBT-I group
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确要求目的清晰并可能需回顾MBT-I信息。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 新成员加入时重申团体目标
atoms.canonical_name_en: Restating group aims when new patient joins
atoms.claim: 每当有新患者加入时，必须重新陈述并商定团体目标。
therapeutic_implications: 新患者需陈述个人期望，讨论如何实现，听取他人意见，接受目标差异，并倾听他人问题
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It is essential to restate and agree the aims of the group whenever a new patient joins.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确要求新患者加入时重新陈述并商定目标。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 团体作为心智化训练场
atoms.canonical_name_en: Group as training ground for mentalizing
atoms.claim: 商定团体目标的过程本身有助于促进团体的首要目标——作为心智化的训练场。
therapeutic_implications: 通过协商目标促进心智化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Working on agreement is in itself likely to facilitate the primary aim of the group to act as a training ground for mentalizing.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确表述商定目标促进心智化训练。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 团体初始阶段概述心智化过程
atoms.canonical_name_en: Outlining mentalizing process at group start
atoms.claim: 在团体开始时，临床医生概述心智化过程，强调心智化的互惠性、相互学习、依恋缓解焦虑以及安全探索个人问题的背景。
therapeutic_implications: 建立团体心智化框架
atoms.evidence_excerpt: At the beginning of the group, the clinicians outline the mentalizing process and emphasize the reciprocity of mentalizing, how we learn from each other, and how attachments can allay anxieties and are a context to explore personal concerns safely.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确描述初始阶段内容。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 团体聚焦人际过程与问题领域
atoms.canonical_name_en: Group focus on interpersonal processes and problem areas
atoms.claim: 团体的目的是研究人与人之间的过程，并聚焦于BPD和/或ASPD中常见的问题领域。
therapeutic_implications: 组织心智化过程围绕问题，寻求管理心理过程的解决方案，避免失调或攻击
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The purpose of the group is for studying these processes between people, as well as focusing on problem areas that are very common in BPD and/or ASPD.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确团体目的包括研究人际过程和常见问题领域。

atoms.claim: MBT小组临床医生通过每次小组开始时总结上一次会议的内容来培养小组的连续性文化。
therapeutic_implications: 培养小组的连续性文化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The MBT group clinician engenders a culture of continuity in the group by beginning each group with a summary of the previous session.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述了总结上一次会议的作用。

atoms.claim: 总结包括对讨论的主要主题的简要陈述，包含临床医生对讨论的看法以及任何未解决问题的概述。
therapeutic_implications: 提供连续性
识别未解决问题
atoms.evidence_excerpt: This is a brief statement about the main themes that were discussed, including the clinician’s perspective of the discourse and an outline of any unresolved problems.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接描述了总结的内容。

atoms.claim: 如果有两位临床医生，他们的观点将在小组后会议中形成并达成一致。
therapeutic_implications: 确保临床医生观点一致
atoms.evidence_excerpt: If there are two clinicians in the group their perspective will have been formulated in the post-group meeting and agreed between them (Box 12.9).
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述了双临床医生协调的方式。

atoms.claim: 总结的目的是增强跨时间的心理化连续性，促进凝聚力，在不规律出席的背景下向患者介绍主题，并组织临床医生自己的思维。
therapeutic_implications: 增强心理化连续性
促进团体凝聚力
在不规律出席时介绍主题
组织临床医生思维
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The aim of the summary is to enhance the continuity of mentalizing across time, to facilitate cohesion, to initiate patients to the themes in the context of erratic attendance, and to organize the clinician’s own mind.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述总结的目的。

atoms.claim: 临床医生完成总结后，可以询问团体成员总结是否准确，以及他们是否想补充任何内容。
therapeutic_implications: 验证总结准确性
鼓励成员参与
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Once the clinician has completed the summary he/she can ask the group members if it is accurate and whether there is anything they would like to add
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接描述总结后的步骤。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 轮流询问中不探索问题
atoms.canonical_name_en: do not explore problems during go-around
atoms.claim: 在轮流询问中，临床医生不探索每个患者的问题，只在所有患者都被询问后才会进行探索。
therapeutic_implications: 确保所有患者有机会提出议题
避免过早深入讨论
response_constraints: 轮流询问时不探索问题
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The clinician does not explore the problems of each individual at this point; he/she does so only once all the patients have been asked if they have a concern they want to discuss.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接描述轮流询问中的限制。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 轮流询问中不允许其他患者评论
atoms.canonical_name_en: do not allow other patients to comment during go-around
atoms.claim: 在轮流询问中，临床医生不允许其他患者评论当前患者的问题。
therapeutic_implications: 保持轮流询问的结构
避免分散注意力
response_constraints: 轮流询问时不允许其他患者评论
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Similarly, during the “go-around” the clinician does not allow the other patients to
atoms.extraction_notes: 句子被截断，但明确表示不允许其他患者评论。

atoms.claim: 临床医生在总结中应包含三个方面：特定主题的良好心理化方面、自我和他人心理化的重要成分、以及总体主题。
therapeutic_implications: 结构化总结内容
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It is helpful for the clinician to keep in mind three major aspects to include in the summary: 1 Good aspects of mentalizing around particular topics 2 Important components of self and other mentalizing 3 Overarching themes.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接列出总结的三个方面。

atoms.claim: 轮流发言鼓励患者相互倾听，不急于对彼此做出假设。
therapeutic_implications: 鼓励患者相互倾听
减少对彼此的快速假设
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Third, it encourages the patients to listen to each other and not to make rapid assumptions about each other.

atoms.claim: 轮流发言鼓励心智化作为小组文化的基本组成部分，从每次小组开始就建立。
therapeutic_implications: 鼓励心智化作为小组文化的基本组成部分
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Finally, it encourages mentalizing as a fundamental part of the group culture right from the outset of each group.

atoms.claim: 轮流发言可能耗时过长，临床医生容易失去对过程的控制，任务可能被转移而从未完成。
response_constraints: 临床医生应遵守与患者商定的时间限制
临床医生必须熟练地维持对过程的掌控
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The “go-around” can become beset with problems. It can take too long. It is easy for the clinician to lose control of the process and for the task to become diverted so that it is never completed.

atoms.claim: 当患者反复说“我只想死”且不愿多谈时，临床医生可以承认患者有严重的感受，但不确定是否能谈论它们，并将此作为小组的问题。
response_constraints: 承认患者有严重的感受
承认患者不确定是否能谈论它们
将此作为小组的问题
atoms.evidence_excerpt: clinician: OK. But let’s put on the table that you have serious feelings at the moment and are not sure if you can talk about them, and that is the problem for us as a group.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 处理声称无问题的患者
atoms.canonical_name_en: handling patients who say they have no problem
atoms.claim: 对于声称无问题的患者，先问几个探究性问题，若无效则继续下一位，稍后再返回；若仍说无问题，有两种选择：接受并推进小组核心工作，或给予患者一个问题。
therapeutic_implications: 先探究
稍后返回
接受或给予问题
response_constraints: 先问几个探究性问题
若无效则继续下一位
稍后返回
若仍无问题则选择接受或给予问题
atoms.evidence_excerpt: A patient who says that they do not have a problem is asked a few probing questions to see if they can identify anything, but if this fails the clinician moves on to the next patient, leaving the first patient for a few minutes to think about it. The clinician can then return to the “no problem” patients later. If they still say they have no problems, there are two options.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了处理声称无问题患者的步骤。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 临床医生需把控讨论节奏
atoms.claim: 临床医生必须把控讨论节奏，确保“轮流发言”中确定的所有问题都得到一定程度的处理。
therapeutic_implications: 确保所有问题被覆盖
合理利用时间
atoms.evidence_excerpt: From this point in the group, the clinician must “pace” the discussion to ensure that all the problems identified in the “go-around” are addressed to some extent.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确要求临床医生把控节奏。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 利用综合焦点共同处理问题
atoms.canonical_name_en: Use synthesis focus to work on problems jointly
atoms.claim: 只要临床医生利用综合焦点共同处理一些问题，就能确保所有问题得到一定程度的处理。
therapeutic_implications: 促进小组共同工作
提高效率
atoms.evidence_excerpt: This will be made possible as long as the clinician uses the focus of the synthesis to work on some problems jointly.
atoms.extraction_notes: 强调综合焦点在小组治疗中的作用。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 患者对时间使用的责任
atoms.claim: 确保时间合理使用的部分责任仍由小组和患者个人承担。
therapeutic_implications: 鼓励患者主动参与
培养责任感
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Of course, some of the responsibility for making sure time is used appropriately remains with the group and the individual patient.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确患者和小组对时间使用的责任。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 轮流发言的时间分配方法
atoms.claim: 一些临床医生建议为每个问题分配固定时间，称为“轮流发言”，以确保时间平均分配。
therapeutic_implications: 确保时间公平分配
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Some clinicians suggest that a set time is allocated to each problem; this is known as “turn-taking” and ensures time is shared equally.
atoms.extraction_notes: 描述了轮流发言的方法，但未明确推荐或反对。

atoms.claim: 过度结构化可能减少心智化过程的促进，因为它扭曲了正常的社会互动过程，并可能阻止问题的连接。
clinical_signals: 患者坚持要求固定时间发言，即使无话可说
therapeutic_implications: 谨慎使用结构化方法，避免过度结构化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: it may reduce the facilitation of mentalizing process through excessive structure.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确提到过度结构化可能减少心智化过程的促进。

atoms.canonical_name_en: managing the trajectory and pace of the group
atoms.claim: 通过管理团体的轨迹和控制节奏来形成心智化训练场的框架。
therapeutic_implications: 临床医生应管理团体轨迹和控制节奏以形成心智化训练场的框架
atoms.evidence_excerpt: This is done in part by managing the trajectory of the group and taking authority for controlling the pace of the group, as described earlier. This forms the frame for the mentalizing “training ground.”

atoms.claim: 探究文化涉及意识到哪些感受和想法促成了决定和选择；尊重他人的想法并允许他们持有不同视角；以及心智改变心智。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It is about becoming aware of what feelings and thoughts contribute to decisions and choices; about respecting others’ ideas and allowing them to hold a different perspective; about minds changing minds.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 近期事件与历史事件的讨论
atoms.canonical_name_en: discussion of recent vs historical events
atoms.claim: 认为讨论近期事件比讨论历史事件更能产生情感心智化的讨论是一种概括，尽管通常如此，但并非总是如此。
therapeutic_implications: 不应一概认为近期事件讨论更有效。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It is a generalization to suggest that discussion of recent events is more fruitful in generating affectively mentalized discussion than discussion of historical events. While this is often the case, it is not
atoms.extraction_notes: 句子在原文中不完整，但已提取完整部分。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 避免使不连贯的叙事变得有意义
atoms.canonical_name_en: Avoid making sense of an incoherent narrative
atoms.claim: 临床医生最大的危险是使一个不连贯的叙事变得有意义。
clinical_signals: 患者讲述的故事不连贯
therapeutic_implications: 临床医生不应填补故事空白或偏袒患者，而应持续激发小组成员对故事细节和潜在心理体验的真实兴趣
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The gravest danger for the clinician is to make sense of a narrative that is incoherent.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 鼓励患者觉察讲述故事时的想法和感受
atoms.canonical_name_en: Encourage patients to be aware of thoughts and feelings while telling a story
atoms.claim: 鼓励患者觉察他们在讲述故事时的想法和感受。
therapeutic_implications: 临床医生应引导患者关注自身心理状态
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Encourage patients to be aware of what they are thinking and feeling as they tell a story
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自Box 12.11

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 邀请其他患者考虑叙述者和自己的思维感受
atoms.canonical_name_en: Ask other patients to consider thinking and feeling of themselves and the narrator
atoms.claim: 邀请其他患者考虑他们自己以及叙述者的思维和感受。
therapeutic_implications: 促进小组内对心理状态的反思
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Ask other patients to consider the thinking and feeling of themselves and the narrator
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自Box 12.11

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 建议患者思考自己/他人为何如此想/感受
atoms.canonical_name_en: Suggest patients consider why they/others think/feel as they do
atoms.claim: 建议患者思考他们自己或他人为何有特定的想法或感受。
therapeutic_implications: 深化对心理过程的理解
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Suggest that patients consider why they/others think/feel as they do in the story
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自Box 12.11

atoms.claim: MBT临床医生通过澄清故事来防止小组中自我导向的孤立。
therapeutic_implications: 澄清故事是防止自我导向孤立的一种干预
atoms.evidence_excerpt: This is done through clarification of the story, exploration of the experience, and active stimulation of interpersonal interactions, with identification of any nonmentalizing responses.
atoms.extraction_notes: 澄清故事是MBT临床医生用于防止非心智化的一种干预原则。

atoms.claim: MBT临床医生通过探索体验来防止小组中自我导向的孤立。
therapeutic_implications: 探索体验是防止自我导向孤立的一种干预
atoms.evidence_excerpt: This is done through clarification of the story, exploration of the experience, and active stimulation of interpersonal interactions, with identification of any nonmentalizing responses.
atoms.extraction_notes: 探索体验是MBT临床医生用于防止非心智化的一种干预原则。

atoms.claim: MBT临床医生通过积极刺激人际互动来防止小组中自我导向的孤立。
therapeutic_implications: 积极刺激人际互动是防止自我导向孤立的一种干预
atoms.evidence_excerpt: This is done through clarification of the story, exploration of the experience, and active stimulation of interpersonal interactions, with identification of any nonmentalizing responses.
atoms.extraction_notes: 积极刺激人际互动是MBT临床医生用于防止非心智化的一种干预原则。

atoms.claim: MBT临床医生通过识别任何非心智化反应来防止小组中自我导向的孤立。
therapeutic_implications: 识别非心智化反应是防止自我导向孤立的一种干预
atoms.evidence_excerpt: This is done through clarification of the story, exploration of the experience, and active stimulation of interpersonal interactions, with identification of any nonmentalizing responses.
atoms.extraction_notes: 识别非心智化反应是MBT临床医生用于防止非心智化的一种干预原则。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 支持患者明确阐述故事细节
atoms.canonical_name_en: Support patients to make explicit their working through of their story (detail)
atoms.claim: 支持患者明确阐述他们处理故事的细节，以便小组识别何时发生了心智化和非心智化。
therapeutic_implications: 使小组能够识别心智化和非心智化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: ◆ Support patients to make explicit their working through of their story (detail) so that the rest of the group (clinician and patients) can identify when mentalizing and nonmentalizing has occurred.
atoms.extraction_notes: 这是MBT小组中促进心智化的具体干预原则。

atoms.claim: 过度心智化是一种有害的非心智化模式，通常用于缓解患者的显著焦虑。
therapeutic_implications: 需要尽早挑战过度心智化，防止其嵌入治疗过程
response_constraints: 临床医生可能需要要求患者提供故事的“编辑版”
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Hypermentalizing needs to be challenged as soon as possible to prevent it becoming embedded in the process
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确将hypermentalizing描述为pernicious nonmentalizing mode，并指出需要尽早挑战。

atoms.claim: 临床医生首先尝试澄清患者描述的事件顺序，包括前因后果、涉及人物及互动过程。
clinical_signals: 患者叙述事件时提供过多细节
therapeutic_implications: 澄清事件有助于识别过度心智化
response_constraints: 临床医生可要求患者提供主要要点
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Initially, the clinician attempts to clarify the sequence of events that the patient describes—what led to what, who was involved, how did the interaction unfold?
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确描述了澄清事件的步骤。

atoms.claim: 故事本身不一定表明问题所在，临床医生应保持“不知”立场，鼓励患者识别问题的确切性质。
clinical_signals: 患者叙述故事但未明确问题
therapeutic_implications: 使用不知立场提问，如“你能描述一下那件事有什么困难吗？”
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Stories do not necessarily indicate the problem. At each stage it is useful for the clinician to maintain a not-knowing stance to encourage the patient to identify the exact nature of the problem
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确说明故事不一定表明问题，并建议保持不知立场。

atoms.claim: 在澄清问题的每个阶段，临床医生保持不知立场有助于鼓励患者识别问题的确切性质。
therapeutic_implications: 促进患者主动识别问题
atoms.evidence_excerpt: At each stage it is useful for the clinician to maintain a not-knowing stance to encourage the patient to identify the exact nature of the problem
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确建议保持不知立场。

atoms.claim: 如果患者使用过多细节，临床医生可能需要要求患者提供故事的“编辑版”，以打断持续叙述，促进心智化。
therapeutic_implications: 打断持续叙述是必要的，以刺激心智化
response_constraints: 临床医生可以说“我不想打断你，但故事变得更清晰了。你能只给我们主要要点吗？”
atoms.evidence_excerpt: While this might sound too challenging to some clinicians, it is necessary to disrupt continuous storytelling if mentalizing is to be stimulated.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确说明打断持续叙述对于刺激心智化是必要的。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 探究故事中人物的动机
atoms.canonical_name_en: explore motivations of people in the story
atoms.claim: 在团体中生成一种探究文化，探究故事中人物的动机。
therapeutic_implications: 鼓励患者考虑他人视角
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Generate a group culture of enquiry about the motivations of people in the story
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确列出此原则。

atoms.claim: 临床医生应坚持要求患者考虑他人的视角，并努力理解他人的观点。
therapeutic_implications: 促进心智化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Insist that patients consider others’ perspectives and work to understand someone else’s point of view
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确列出此原则。

atoms.claim: 临床医生应直接表达自己对干扰理解故事的事物的感受。
clinical_signals: 临床医生认为有事物干扰对故事的理解
therapeutic_implications: 促进探究文化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Clinician should directly express his/her own feelings about something that he/she believes is interfering with understanding of the story.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确列出此原则。

atoms.claim: 治疗师应从共情验证患者的体验开始。
therapeutic_implications: 先共情再探索问题
atoms.evidence_excerpt: I can see that it is a problem if you are told something and then it does not happen, and that when you feel there is some urgency it is even more of a problem. [Beginning empathic validation of the experience.]
atoms.extraction_notes: 治疗师开始共情验证患者的体验。

atoms.canonical_name_en: Identify the problems within the story
atoms.claim: 治疗师应识别患者故事中的问题。
clinical_signals: 患者叙述事件但未明确问题
therapeutic_implications: 帮助患者明确问题所在
atoms.evidence_excerpt: ◆ Identify the problems within the story
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自Box 12.14的要点。

atoms.claim: 治疗师应激发患者提供替代视角。
therapeutic_implications: 鼓励其他患者或患者自身考虑不同观点
atoms.evidence_excerpt: ◆ Stimulate alternative perspectives from patients
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自Box 12.14的要点。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 促进讨论管理心理状态作为问题
atoms.canonical_name_en: Facilitate discussion of managing mental states as the problem
atoms.claim: 治疗师应促进讨论将管理心理状态视为问题本身。
clinical_signals: 患者将问题归因于外部事件
therapeutic_implications: 引导患者关注如何管理自己的心理状态
atoms.evidence_excerpt: ◆ Facilitate discussion of managing mental states as the problem
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自Box 12.14的要点。

atoms.claim: 患者认为临床医生故意不给他回电话是因为不喜欢他，这体现了情感驱动的非心智化。
clinical_signals: 患者认为临床医生故意不给他回电话是因为不喜欢他
therapeutic_implications: 需要帮助患者在敏感时刻维持心智化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The patient believed that the clinician had deliberately not rung him back because she did not like him. This indicates affectively driven nonmentalizing, which is the target of MBT.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述情感驱动的非心智化是MBT的目标。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 在团体中避免个体治疗
atoms.canonical_name_en: Avoiding individual therapy in the group
atoms.claim: MBT-G 警告不要在团体中进行个体治疗。
clinical_signals: 治疗师逐渐陷入与单个患者的个体治疗
therapeutic_implications: 当治疗师专注于一个患者时，其他患者可能退缩，将工作留给治疗师
response_constraints: 当发生这种情况时，需要‘三角化’
atoms.evidence_excerpt: MBT-G cautions against individual therapy within the group.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用原文，明确禁止在团体中进行个体治疗。

atoms.claim: MBT小组治疗的重点是刺激患者的心智化过程，而不是代替患者心智化或传递临床医生优越心智化过程所形成的理解。
therapeutic_implications: 临床医生应避免代替患者心智化或传递自己的理解
atoms.evidence_excerpt: focus of MBT, which is to stimulate mentalizing processes in the patients; it is not to take over mentalizing on their behalf or to deliver understanding formed through the clinician’s superior mentalizing process.

atoms.claim: 临床医生需要通过持续使用“停止”和“回放”并加以澄清来维持控制，防止小组互动过快导致反思丧失。
therapeutic_implications: 使用“停止”和“回放”技术维持控制
澄清互动内容
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The clinician needs to maintain control through the constant use of “stop” and “rewind” with clarification.

atoms.claim: 快速互动会导致反思丧失，并倾向于导致非心智化或成为提供建议的论坛。
therapeutic_implications: 避免快速互动
促进反思
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Rapid interaction leads to loss of reflection and tends to lead to nonmentalizing or becomes a forum for advice.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 支持患者谈论关系模式
atoms.canonical_name_en: support patient in talking about relational patterns
atoms.claim: 在将新患者引入小组时，临床医生可以要求患者谈论他/她的关系，并支持他/她谈论他/她所具有的关系模式。
therapeutic_implications: 鼓励患者分享关系模式
atoms.evidence_excerpt: the clinician may ask the patient to talk about his/her relationships and support him/her in talking about the relational patterns that he/she has.

atoms.claim: 所有患者应开放式分享其初始评估中关系方面的内容。
therapeutic_implications: 鼓励患者分享关系方面的内容
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Open sharing by all patients of the relational aspects of their initial formulation

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 在小组中关注依恋过程
atoms.canonical_name_en: focus on attachment processes in group
atoms.claim: 在个体治疗中关注小组内的依恋过程。
therapeutic_implications: 在个体治疗中讨论小组内的依恋过程
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Focus on attachment processes in the group during individual sessions

atoms.claim: 在MBT中，依恋模式的外显化是重要的，并且始终以协作和明确的方式进行。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应协作且明确地外显患者的依恋模式
atoms.evidence_excerpt: We would like to emphasize here the importance that is now attached to explication of the attachment patterns in MBT. This is done collaboratively and explicitly at all times.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述了依恋模式外显化的重要性及其协作、明确的方式。

atoms.claim: 当团体接近结束时，治疗师可以建议患者简要总结或等到下周再讨论。
clinical_signals: 患者迟到并请求额外时间
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应明确时间限制，避免因个别患者延长团体时间
atoms.evidence_excerpt: As the group was nearly at an end, the clinician said that there was very limited time so perhaps Nigel could summarize quickly or even wait until the following week.
atoms.extraction_notes: 治疗师在团体结束时对迟到患者的回应。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 团体成员支持延长团体时间
atoms.claim: 其他团体成员表示可以多留一会儿，建议继续讨论。
clinical_signals: 团体成员愿意为患者延长团体时间
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师需要平衡个别患者需求与团体结构
atoms.evidence_excerpt: other group members [stating that they could stay for a time]: We have got a bit of time so why don’t we go on for a bit?
atoms.extraction_notes: 团体成员主动提出延长团体时间。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 减少唤醒并探索关系过程
atoms.canonical_name_en: reduce arousal and explore relational process
atoms.claim: 临床医生正确尝试减少患者的唤醒，然后开始探索关系过程，发展关于正在发生的事情的替代视角。
clinical_signals: 患者试图通过威胁控制他人
therapeutic_implications: 先降低唤醒再探索关系过程
发展替代视角
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The clinician correctly tried to reduce his arousal and then start exploring the relational process, developing an alternative perspective about what was happening.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接描述临床医生的正确做法。

atoms.claim: 验证性陈述可以使患者稍微平静下来。
therapeutic_implications: 使用验证性陈述降低唤醒
atoms.evidence_excerpt: nigel [A little calmer from this validating statement]: Yes.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接显示验证性陈述的效果。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 区分人际互动工作与关系心理化
atoms.canonical_name_en: differentiate interpersonal work from mentalizing the relationship
atoms.claim: 在团体治疗中，需要区分对人际互动的工作与从移情角度进行的关系心理化干预。
therapeutic_implications: 临床医生可以从患者显性的人际生活入手，先处理团体中体现的关系模式，再深化干预
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It is important to differentiate the work on interpersonal interactions in the group from interventions using mentalizing the relationship.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确提出了区分两种干预的重要性。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 人际工作涵盖多种关系领域
atoms.canonical_name_en: interpersonal work covers multiple relationship domains
atoms.claim: 人际工作涉及个体的家庭关系、友谊模式、工作互动和社区关系，以及它们如何建设性或破坏性地影响患者的生活。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗需考虑患者多方面的关系背景
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It is concerned with the individual’s family relationships, friendship patterns, work interactions, and community relations, and how they impinge on the patient’s life, both constructively and destructively.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确列举了人际工作涵盖的关系领域。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 链接团体体验与外部关系
atoms.canonical_name_en: Link group experience to outside relationships
atoms.claim: 治疗师需要将患者在团体中的体验与其外部关系联系起来。
therapeutic_implications: 促进团体内外关系的整合
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Link the patients’ experience in the group to their relationships outside it.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用原文。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 链接到评估中确定的依恋模式
atoms.canonical_name_en: Link to attachment patterns identified in formulation
atoms.claim: 治疗师需要将团体互动与初始评估中确定的依恋模式联系起来。
clinical_signals: 出现与依恋相关的互动
therapeutic_implications: 深化对关系模式的理解
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Link to attachment patterns identified in formulation.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用原文。

atoms.claim: 患者轻易同意治疗师的提议可能表明其处于假装模式。
clinical_signals: 患者轻易同意治疗师的提议
therapeutic_implications: 在转向对关系的心理化之前，需要先进行人际过程的初步探索和其他准备工作
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The initial exploration of the interpersonal process and other preparatory work had not been done to indicate a move toward mentalizing the relationship with him and others in the group.
atoms.extraction_notes: 文本中治疗师担心患者轻易同意，暗示可能处于假装模式，但未明确诊断。

atoms.claim: 在转向对关系的心理化之前，需要进行人际过程的初步探索和其他准备工作。
clinical_signals: 患者表现出假装模式迹象
therapeutic_implications: 先进行人际过程探索，再尝试心理化关系
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The initial exploration of the interpersonal process and other preparatory work had not been done to indicate a move toward mentalizing the relationship with him and others in the group.
atoms.extraction_notes: 文本明确说明在转向心理化关系之前需要先进行探索和准备工作。

atoms.claim: 治疗师可以通过温和的挑战来促使患者反思自己的行为模式。
clinical_signals: 患者习惯性顺从或自我贬低
therapeutic_implications: 使用温和挑战，如询问患者是否在顺从治疗师
atoms.evidence_excerpt: clinician: Are you deferring to me now? [A small challenge; this surprised Jeannie.]
atoms.extraction_notes: 文本明确描述治疗师的小挑战。

atoms.claim: 三角化是在两人对话中插入第三人，创造空间、替代维度和视角。
clinical_signals: 两人对话陷入僵局或需要新视角
therapeutic_implications: 通过引入第三方观察者来丰富理解
atoms.evidence_excerpt: triangulation is creating a space, an alternative dimension and perspective, in the dialogue between two people by inserting a third person.

atoms.claim: 在心智化关系中，主动探索临床医生的贡献。
clinical_signals: 临床医生意识到可能强加观点，合作丧失
therapeutic_implications: 先验证患者被强迫谈论的感受，然后澄清临床医生的贡献，探索患者屈服的倾向
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In mentalizing the relationship, the contribution from the clinician is actively explored.

atoms.claim: 在两名患者进行亲密对话时，过早让其他人介入可能具有破坏性；过晚则可能失去增加详细视角和理解的机会。
clinical_signals: 两名患者正在进行亲密对话
therapeutic_implications: 临床医生需凭敏感性决定何时让其他患者参与对话
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Involving others in an intimate conversation between two group members too early can be disruptive; too late and the potential for increasingly detailed perspectives and understanding is lost because the minds of the other patients are no longer attending to the issue under scrutiny.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明三角化时机的考虑

atoms.claim: 在严重人格障碍患者中，配对更常导致其他成员坐着观看并逐渐游离，而非形成有益的组织性想法。
clinical_signals: 两名患者形成共谋的同一性和同意
其他成员坐着观看并逐渐游离
therapeutic_implications: MBT-G避免对小组过程本身进行解释，而是通过三角化干预
atoms.evidence_excerpt: However, in patients with severe personality disorder the converse is more common; they tend to sit and watch and slowly drift away.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述严重人格障碍患者中配对的结果

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 临床医生配对时的三角化
atoms.claim: 当两名临床医生与一名患者互动时，他们被视为一个人，互动在心理上是二元的，同样会干扰小组的整体心智化。
clinical_signals: 两名临床医生都专注于一名患者
临床医生可能长时间未意识到小组其他成员
therapeutic_implications: 在MBT-G中，临床医生有明确协议：如果一人专注于患者，另一人应考虑三角化并干预
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Of particular significance is ensuring that triangulation takes place when two clinicians become involved with one patient. In this context, the clinicians are viewed as one person; that is, the interaction is psychologically dyadic even though there are three people involved.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明临床医生配对时需三角化

atoms.claim: 在MBT-G中，临床医生将对话三角化至特定个体，而非整个团体。
therapeutic_implications: 指定个体迫使互动过程，防止团体陷入无效沉默
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In MBT-G, the clinician triangulates to a specific person. Rarely does he/she triangulate to the group as a whole by saying, for example, “What do others think?” “Has anyone else any thoughts about this?” Specifying an individual forces the interactive process and does not allow the group to easily sink into ineffectual silence.

atoms.claim: 边缘型人格障碍患者常难以抑制主导欲望以关注次主导过程，因此可能需要使用停车技术。
therapeutic_implications: 帮助患者暂时搁置自身强烈愿望，以便关注他人相关话题
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Problems with attentional control are frequent in patients with BPD and other personality disorders. Patients often find it hard to suppress a dominant desire in order to attend to a subdominant process. This means they may not be able to easily focus on a topic of relevance and importance to another person if they, themselves, have a strong desire to talk about something affecting them.

atoms.claim: MBT临床医生持续监控所有患者的唤醒水平，遵循唤醒必须维持在中等范围的原则，以促进而非阻碍心智化。
therapeutic_implications: 维持唤醒在中等范围以促进心智化
response_constraints: 临床医生需持续警惕行为或心理的唤醒指标
atoms.evidence_excerpt: MBT clinicians constantly monitor the arousal levels of all patients, following the MBT principle that arousal has to be maintained within a moderate range, neither too high nor too low, if mentalizing is to be facilitated rather than impeded.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述了监控唤醒水平的原则和目的。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 识别患者体验而非问题内容
atoms.canonical_name_en: identifying the experience of the patient rather than the content of the problem
atoms.claim: 在停车技术中，临床医生识别患者的体验而非问题内容。
clinical_signals: 患者无法维持注意力控制
therapeutic_implications: 帮助患者聚焦于次主导主题
response_constraints: 临床医生需主动帮助患者聚焦
atoms.evidence_excerpt: ◆ Identifies the experience of the patient rather than the content of the problem
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自Box 12.19的要点列表，明确陈述。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 主动帮助患者聚焦次主导主题
atoms.canonical_name_en: actively helps the patient focus on a subdominant theme
atoms.claim: 临床医生主动帮助患者聚焦于次主导主题。
clinical_signals: 患者无法维持注意力控制
therapeutic_implications: 提高注意力控制
response_constraints: 临床医生需主动帮助
atoms.evidence_excerpt: ◆ Actively helps the patient focus on a subdominant theme
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自Box 12.19的要点列表。

atoms.canonical_name_en: keeping a lid on the dominant desire
atoms.claim: 临床医生通过暂时释放压力来抑制患者的主导欲望。
clinical_signals: 患者有主导欲望需要表达
therapeutic_implications: 帮助患者维持注意力控制
response_constraints: 临床医生需暂时让患者释放压力
atoms.evidence_excerpt: ◆ Keeps a lid on the dominant desire by momentarily letting off steam
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自Box 12.19的要点列表。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 临床医生不能忘记已停车患者
atoms.canonical_name_en: clinician must not forget he/she has parked a patient
atoms.claim: 临床医生不能忘记已“停车”的患者，如果患者变得过度焦虑，可能需要暂停小组。
therapeutic_implications: 确保患者被关注，避免遗忘
response_constraints: 临床医生需记住已停车患者
必要时暂停小组
atoms.evidence_excerpt: ◆ Clinician must not forget he/she has “parked” a patient—may have to pause the group if the patient becomes excessively anxious.
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自Box 12.19的要点列表。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 以稍微秘密的方式请求患者等待
atoms.canonical_name_en: slightly conspiratorially asking the patient to wait
atoms.claim: 临床医生以稍微秘密的方式请求患者等待，这会让患者感到特别和被关注。
therapeutic_implications: 让患者感到特别和被关注
response_constraints: 临床医生需以稍微秘密的方式请求
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Often, this is best done slightly conspiratorially as this will make the patient feel special and attended to by the clinician.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述了以秘密方式请求等待的效果。

atoms.canonical_name_en: openly asking the patient to wait
atoms.claim: 临床医生也可以公开请求患者等待，例如说“Rachel，你能稍等一下吗？我们和Peter先结束，马上回来找你。”
therapeutic_implications: 让患者感到被看见
response_constraints: 临床医生需公开请求
atoms.evidence_excerpt: But, equally, it can be stated openly—“Rachel, can you hang on a short time so that we can finish off this with Peter. We will be back to you in a minute.”
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述了公开请求等待的方式。

atoms.claim: 停车技术是治疗师在团体中行使权威的一种方式，确保患者的唤醒水平和需求得到识别和管理。
clinical_signals: 无法集中注意力于当前讨论
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师通过承认患者的需求并请求其等待，帮助患者暂时抑制谈论自己问题的冲动
治疗师需要知道患者能被‘停车’多久
必要时需明确‘取消停车’并‘停车’当前活跃的患者
response_constraints: 治疗师需记住谁被‘停车’了，并适时敏感地回到他们的关注点
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It will be apparent that parking is a further way in which the clinician takes some authority in the group. He/she ensures that arousal levels and patient imperatives are recognized and managed.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述停车是治疗师行使权威的方式，确保识别和管理唤醒水平和患者需求。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 停车技术作为明示线索
atoms.claim: 停车作为一种明示线索，使患者感到被承认为一个‘主体’，一个有需求的人。
therapeutic_implications: 明示线索向患者发出信号，表明治疗师有沟通意图针对其需求，但要求其等待
鼓励患者管理内部压力，不主导话语或对他人提出要求
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Parking serves as an ostensive cue making the patient feel recognized as an “agent,” a person who has needs. This ostensive cue signals to the patient that the clinician has a communicative intention addressed to his/her needs but asks that he/she waits for a short time while other concerns are dealt with.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述停车作为明示线索，使患者感到被承认为主体，并传达治疗师的沟通意图。

atoms.canonical_name_en: maintaining reasonable levels of attachment arousal
atoms.claim: 支持弱势患者的目的是维持适度的依恋唤醒水平并降低即时压力。
therapeutic_implications: 临床医生通过支持弱势患者来降低即时压力
临床医生确保其他患者不会变得脆弱或感到受攻击
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The aim is to maintain reasonable levels of attachment arousal and to reduce the immediate stress of the situation
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述了支持弱势患者的目标。

atoms.claim: 当脆弱患者状态更稳定时，临床医生必要时可以转换支持对象。
therapeutic_implications: 临床医生在脆弱患者稳定后可能转换支持对象
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Clinician switches sides if necessary when the vulnerable patient is more stable.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了转换支持对象的条件。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 另一位临床医生扮演对抗者角色
atoms.canonical_name_en: other clinician takes the position of antagonist
atoms.claim: 当一位临床医生支持弱势患者时，另一位临床医生（如果在场）可以扮演对抗者的角色。
clinical_signals: 一位临床医生正在支持弱势患者
therapeutic_implications: 另一位临床医生采取对抗者立场
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Other clinician (if present) takes the position of antagonist
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了另一位临床医生的角色。

atoms.claim: 当一名成员被另一名成员攻击时，临床医生可以站在被攻击者一边，将焦点转回攻击者，以减轻被攻击者的压力。
clinical_signals: 一名成员被另一名成员批评或贬低
therapeutic_implications: 暂时支持被攻击者可以降低其应激水平
response_constraints: 之后需要监控攻击者的反应，因为攻击者也可能变得脆弱
atoms.evidence_excerpt: At this point the clinician has taken the side of Andrea and pushed the focus back to Catherine. This will reduce Andrea’s stress. Now the clinician has to monitor the effect on Catherine as she, too, may become vulnerable.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了临床医生站在Andrea一边并转移焦点，以及需要监控Catherine的反应。

atoms.claim: 当临床医生将焦点保持在攻击者身上时，需要确保在一定程度上支持该成员。
clinical_signals: 攻击者感到被忽视或不被喜欢
therapeutic_implications: 在挑战攻击者的同时提供支持，有助于维持治疗联盟
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The clinician is keeping the focus on Catherine at this point but trying to ensure that he supports her to some extent.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明临床医生在保持焦点于Catherine的同时试图支持她。

atoms.claim: 当紧张降低后，临床医生可以不再偏袒任何一方，将焦点重新转回最初被攻击的成员。
therapeutic_implications: 促进被攻击者反思自己的体验
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The conversation continued, and as the tension reduced the clinician passed the focus back to Andrea, no longer taking sides.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述紧张降低后临床医生将焦点转回Andrea且不再偏袒。

atoms.claim: 临床医生可以要求成员在感到挫败时直接说出来，而不是通过批评表达。
clinical_signals: 成员对另一成员感到挫败
therapeutic_implications: 促进直接沟通，减少间接攻击
atoms.evidence_excerpt: the group members were tasked by the clinician to make sure that if they were becoming frustrated when talking to Andrea they should say so.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明临床医生要求成员说出挫败感。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 要求成员监控自身行为
atoms.claim: 临床医生可以要求被攻击的成员监控自己的消极行为，并识别有帮助的互动。
clinical_signals: 成员表现出持续的消极态度
therapeutic_implications: 增强成员的自我觉察和主动性
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Andrea was asked to monitor her negativity and to identify anything that she found helpful, so that she could let the group know.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明要求Andrea监控消极性并识别有帮助的内容。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 利用初始个案概念化指导小组过程
atoms.canonical_name_en: using initial formulation to inform group process
atoms.claim: 小组过程可以利用与每位患者共同制定的初始个案概念化，来理解他们在小组中的关系。
clinical_signals: 成员在小组中重复现实生活中的关系模式
therapeutic_implications: 将小组互动与个人目标联系起来
atoms.evidence_excerpt: the group process harnesses the initial formulation agreed with each patient to inform mentalizing of the relationships that each one has in the group.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明利用初始个案概念化来理解小组中的关系。

atoms.claim: 反社会型人格障碍患者更可能在结构良好的、图式化的依恋关系中表现出对情绪状态的过度控制，而非边缘型人格障碍患者常见的混乱依恋关系中的控制不足。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: First, people with ASPD are more likely to demonstrate over-control of their emotional states within well-structured, schematic attachment relationships, rather than the under-control in chaotic attachment relationships that are more commonly found in people with BPD.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 反社会型人格障碍与心智化
atoms.claim: 反社会型人格障碍患者对等级秩序的威胁会引发依恋系统的激活，进而抑制心智化，导致对无法控制内在状态的恐惧。
clinical_signals: 对等级秩序的威胁引发依恋系统激活
恐惧无法控制内在状态
therapeutic_implications: 治疗中需关注等级秩序威胁对心智化的影响
atoms.evidence_excerpt: it is specifically threats to the hierarchical order of relationships that lead to arousal within the attachment system in people with ASPD; this triggers an inhibition of mentalizing, which in turn leads to fears of inability to control internal states.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述了ASPD患者中等级威胁、依恋系统激活、心智化抑制和恐惧之间的因果链。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 反社会型人格障碍与自尊威胁
atoms.claim: 反社会型人格障碍患者最恐惧的内在状态是自尊受到威胁。
clinical_signals: 自尊威胁引发强烈恐惧
therapeutic_implications: 治疗中需处理自尊威胁相关议题
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It has been suggested that the internal state most feared by people with ASPD is threat to self-esteem (Gilligan, 2000).
atoms.extraction_notes: 引用Gilligan (2000)的观点，文本以‘It has been suggested’表述，故为强烈暗示。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 反社会型人格障碍与自尊膨胀策略
atoms.claim: 反社会型人格障碍患者通过要求他人尊重、控制他人和制造恐惧氛围来膨胀自尊，以维持骄傲、声望和地位。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗中需识别并处理这些策略
atoms.evidence_excerpt: People with ASPD inflate their self-esteem by demanding respect from others, controlling the people around them, and creating an atmosphere of fear. This maintains their pride, prestige, and status.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了ASPD患者膨胀自尊的具体行为及其目的。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 反社会型人格障碍与地位丧失
atoms.claim: 地位丧失对反社会型人格障碍患者是毁灭性的，因为它可能暴露令人羞耻的内在状态，从而需要用武力应对。
clinical_signals: 地位丧失引发毁灭性感受
therapeutic_implications: 治疗中需关注地位丧失的触发因素和应对方式
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Loss of status is devastating as it potentially reveals shameful internal states that threaten to overwhelm the individual, so any threat of loss of status becomes firmly rooted as a dangerous reality that has to be dealt with by physical force.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述了地位丧失的后果及应对方式。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 反社会型人格障碍与情感抑制暴力
atoms.canonical_name_en: ASPD and emotional inhibition of violence
atoms.claim: 内疚、对他人的爱和对自己恐惧等情感能力可能保护反社会型人格障碍患者不参与暴力行为，但心智化丧失和体验这些情感的能力减弱阻止了这种抑制。
clinical_signals: 内疚、爱、恐惧等情感能力减弱
therapeutic_implications: 治疗中需增强情感体验和心智化以减少暴力
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Emotional capacities such as guilt, love toward others, and fear for the self may protect them from engaging in violent behavior, but the loss of mentalizing and the attenuated ability of people with ASPD to experience such feelings prevent these inhibitory
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述了情感能力和心智化在抑制暴力中的作用及其在ASPD中的缺失。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 反社会型人格障碍与恐惧表情识别缺陷
atoms.canonical_name_en: ASPD and fear expression recognition deficit
atoms.claim: 反社会型人格障碍患者无法准确识别某些情绪（可能范围广泛），包括无法从面部表情识别恐惧情绪，这提示杏仁核等神经结构功能异常。
clinical_signals: 无法准确识别恐惧表情
therapeutic_implications: 治疗中需考虑神经基础对情绪识别的影响
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Fail to recognize fearful emotions from facial expressions. This suggests a dysfunction in neural structures, such as the amygdala, that subserve fearful expression processing
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自Box 13.1，明确陈述了恐惧表情识别缺陷及其神经关联。

atoms.claim: 在反社会型人格障碍患者的团体中，目的论系统往往占主导地位。
therapeutic_implications: 团体工作对于解决非心智化和混乱的团体行为至关重要
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In such groups, teleological systems tend to dominate (see Box 13.2).
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确提到在ASPD团体中目的论系统占主导。
population_details: 反社会型人格障碍患者

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 利用同伴群体层级过程探索心智化扭曲
atoms.claim: 团体工作能激发同伴群体内的层级过程，临床医生可借此现场探索参与者对层级和权威的敏感性以及随之产生的心智化扭曲。
therapeutic_implications: 临床医生应利用团体中自然出现的层级动态来探索心智化问题
atoms.evidence_excerpt: More importantly, group work stimulates a hierarchical process within a peer group, which can be harnessed in vivo by the clinicians to explore participants’ sensitivity to hierarchy and authority and the ensuing mentalizing distortions (see Box 13.3).
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确说明团体工作激发层级过程，临床医生可加以利用。
population_details: 反社会型人格障碍患者

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 反社会型人格障碍患者对他人情绪的识别困难
atoms.claim: 如果反社会型人格障碍患者识别他人情绪的能力下降不仅限于恐惧和悲伤，而是更普遍，那么治疗中必须关注识别所有情绪。
clinical_signals: 识别他人情绪能力下降
仅限于恐惧和悲伤的情绪识别困难
therapeutic_implications: 治疗应聚焦于识别所有情绪
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Fourth, if the reduction in ability to recognize others’ emotions is more pervasive than being restricted to fear and sadness, then a focus in treatment on recognizing all emotions in others is essential.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确陈述治疗焦点应放在识别所有情绪上。
population_details: 反社会型人格障碍患者

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 反社会型人格障碍患者攻击行为的后果次要于维持自我感
atoms.claim: 对于反社会型人格障碍患者，攻击的后果和危险变得次要于减少内在自我感崩溃的需要。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗需理解攻击行为背后的自我感维持功能
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Indeed, the consequences and dangers of aggression become secondary to the need to reduce internal collapse of a sense of self.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确陈述攻击的后果次于维持自我感的需要。
population_details: 反社会型人格障碍患者

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 目的论模式中的物理世界取向
atoms.claim: 在目的论系统中，对他人能动性的期望仅以物理世界术语表述：只有物质的东西才有意义。
clinical_signals: 将物理改变视为他人意图的真实指标
therapeutic_implications: 治疗需处理这种物理取向的心智化缺陷
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Expectations concerning the agency of the other are present, but these are formulated uniquely in terms restricted to the physical world: only what is material can be meaningful
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自Box 13.2，描述目的论系统的特征。
population_details: 反社会型人格障碍患者

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 目的论模式中的物理行动取向
atoms.claim: 在目的论系统中，只有具有物理影响的行动才被认为能够改变自我和他人的心理状态。
clinical_signals: 认为只有物理伤害行动才合法
要求他人通过物理行动证明意图
therapeutic_implications: 治疗需挑战这种物理行动取向的信念
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Only action that has a physical impact is felt as potentially capable of altering mental states in both self and other:
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自Box 13.2，描述目的论系统的特征。
population_details: 反社会型人格障碍患者

atoms.claim: 通过创造一种同情和理解的意愿来激活依恋。
therapeutic_implications: 创造同情和理解的态度
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Activate attachment by creating an attitude of compassion and wish to understand

atoms.claim: 增强团体成员对彼此想法和感受的好奇心。
therapeutic_implications: 鼓励对他人想法和感受的好奇
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Enhance the curiosity that members of the group have about each other’s thoughts and feelings

atoms.claim: 关注误解，因为心智化是对误解的理解。
therapeutic_implications: 聚焦于误解
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Focus on misunderstandings (mentalizing is the “understanding of misunderstanding”)

atoms.claim: 鼓励并发展一种好奇心文化，同时保持尊重的不知情态度。
therapeutic_implications: 鼓励好奇心
保持尊重的不知情
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Encourage and develop a culture of curiosity coupled with respectful not-knowing.

atoms.claim: 增加对自我（内部）状态的理解。
therapeutic_implications: 增加对内部状态的理解
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Increase understanding of self (internal) states

atoms.claim: 发展对自我-他人互动状态的意识。
therapeutic_implications: 发展互动状态意识
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Develop an awareness of self–other interactional states

atoms.claim: 考虑他人的主观体验。
therapeutic_implications: 考虑他人主观体验
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Consider others’ subjective experience

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 建立相互接受的治疗关系
atoms.claim: 与患者建立相互接受的关系，即治疗师将尽己所能从实践和心理角度处理问题，而这只有通过规律出勤才能实现。
therapeutic_implications: 明确治疗师角色和患者责任
response_constraints: 避免内疚诱导
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It is better to establish with participants a mutual acceptance that you will do what you can to work on their problems from a practical and a psychological point of view and that this can be achieved only through regular attendance.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确建议建立相互接受的关系。
population_details: 反社会型人格障碍患者

atoms.claim: MBT-ASPD关注理解情绪线索，即外部心理化及其与自我和他人内部状态的关联。
therapeutic_implications: 要求患者识别如何判断他人感受
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Understanding emotional cues—external mentalizing and its link to self and other internal states. Participants are asked to identify how they decide how someone else feels.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确将外部心理化作为MBT-ASPD的焦点之一。
population_details: 反社会型人格障碍患者

atoms.claim: 对于反社会型人格障碍患者，试图通过内疚感来增加动机是无效的，因为他们对这些感受的容量减弱。
therapeutic_implications: 不应使用内疚诱导策略
response_constraints: 避免呼吁社会/团体责任
contraindications: 不要利用内疚感
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The attenuated capacity for such feelings in people with ASPD means that they cannot be harnessed as powerful organizing factors.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明内疚感在ASPD患者中无效。
population_details: 反社会型人格障碍患者

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 反社会型人格障碍的MBT治疗格式
atoms.claim: MBT-ASPD结合每周MBT团体治疗与每月个体治疗。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗频率为每周团体加每月个体
atoms.evidence_excerpt: MBT-ASPD combines weekly MBT group therapy with monthly individual sessions.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述治疗格式。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 反社会型人格障碍的MBT治疗时长
atoms.claim: 每个个体的治疗持续1年。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗总时长为1年
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Treatment for each individual lasts 1 year.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述治疗时长。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 反社会型人格障碍团体治疗中的双治疗师模式
atoms.claim: 在MBT-ASPD的试点研究中，由两名临床医生带领团体。
therapeutic_implications: 团体治疗由两名治疗师共同带领
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In pilot studies of MBT-ASPD, two clinicians ran the group.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述试点研究中的做法。

atoms.claim: 团体治疗中包括生成人际过程以理解他人经验与自身经验的关系——即自我/他人心智化。
therapeutic_implications: 促进理解他人经验与自身经验的关系
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Generation of an interpersonal process to understand others’ experience in relation to one’s own—self/other mentalizing.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确列出自我/他人心智化作为团体治疗的一个步骤。

atoms.claim: 团体治疗中包括阐明导致目的论理解动机的心智化丧失威胁——自我/他人心智化和自我/情感心智化。
therapeutic_implications: 处理心智化丧失威胁
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Explication of threats to loss of mentalizing that lead to teleological understanding of motivation—self/other mentalizing and self/affective mentalizing.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确列出自我/情感心智化作为团体治疗的一个步骤。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 反社会型人格障碍团体治疗中的情感线索理解
atoms.canonical_name_en: Understanding emotional cues in MBT-ASPD group
atoms.claim: 团体治疗包括理解情感线索——外部心智化及其与内部状态的关联。
therapeutic_implications: 帮助患者理解情感线索与内部状态的联系
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Understanding emotional cues—external mentalizing and its link to internal states
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确列出理解情感线索作为团体治疗的一个步骤。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 允许假装模式以促进团结
atoms.canonical_name_en: allow pretend mode to foster unity
atoms.claim: 在MBT-ASPD团体开始时，允许参与者进行假装模式的对话，以给他们一种团结感。
clinical_signals: 团体开始时出现假装模式对话
therapeutic_implications: 不要立即挑战假装模式
允许其短暂存在以建立团结
然后尽快将对话引导回问题领域或此时此地的感受
response_constraints: 与通常的告诫相反，不要挑战假装模式或阻止其嵌入
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Contrary to the usual exhortation about pretend mode (challenge it and do not allow it to become embedded), it is important to allow the participants to do this at the beginning of a group to give them a sense of unity.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明允许假装模式以促进团结，并指出与通常做法相反。

atoms.canonical_name_en: bring conversation back to focus as soon as possible
atoms.claim: 在允许假装模式后，应尽快将对话带回问题领域或此时此地的感受。
therapeutic_implications: 在给予团结感后，引导对话回到问题领域或此时此地的感受
atoms.evidence_excerpt: However, the aim is to bring the conversation back to a focus on problem areas and/or on the here and now of how they are feeling as soon as possible.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明尽快将对话带回焦点。

atoms.claim: 在MBT-ASPD团体中，应避免使用暂停合同。
therapeutic_implications: 不要使用暂停合同
response_constraints: 避免暂停合同
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Avoid: ● Time-out contracts
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确列出避免暂停合同。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 个体治疗支持团体治疗
atoms.claim: 个体治疗主要用于支持反社会型人格障碍患者在团体中的参与。
therapeutic_implications: 个体治疗可帮助患者处理在团体中不愿或羞于讨论的问题，如人际关系困难、抑郁或自杀感受。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The individual sessions are provided primarily to support the person with ASPD in the group.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述个体治疗的主要目的。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 同伴互动作为改变过程
atoms.claim: 同伴群体互动可能比与临床医生的个体治疗对改变过程更重要。
therapeutic_implications: 强调团体互动在治疗中的核心作用。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The peer-group interaction may be more significant as a process for change than individual therapy with a clinician.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确比较，但使用“可能”表示不确定性。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 同一临床医生减少欺骗
atoms.claim: 由同一位临床医生提供个体和团体治疗，可减少关于团体中发生事件的欺骗机会。
therapeutic_implications: 保持治疗连续性，减少患者歪曲团体讨论的可能性。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Having the same clinician minimizes the opportunity for deception about what happens in the group, which may distort discussion about the group work in the individual session.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述同一临床医生的作用。

atoms.claim: 通过对比临床医生和参与者在团体中的经历，可以关注对团体事件和经历的不同感知。
therapeutic_implications: 促进对团体互动中不同视角的探索。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It allows a focus on different perceptions of events and experiences in the group by contrasting the experiences of the clinician in the group with those of the participant.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述对比感知的作用。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 个体治疗处理敏感话题
atoms.claim: 患者可能利用个体治疗讨论他们在团体中不愿或羞于谈论的问题，如人际关系困难、抑郁或自杀感受。
clinical_signals: 在团体中回避敏感话题
therapeutic_implications: 在个体治疗中探索这些敏感性，可能有助于患者未来在团体中谈论它们。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Participants may use the individual sessions to discuss issues that they are reluctant or ashamed to talk about in the group, such as difficulties in their personal relationships, depressed or suicidal feelings, etc. Exploring their sensitivities individually may facilitate the participant to talk about them in the group in future sessions.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述个体治疗的作用和潜在益处。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 新成员个体治疗复习心理教育
atoms.canonical_name_en: Individual sessions review psychoeducation for new members
atoms.claim: 当新成员加入已建立的团体时，个体治疗可用于复习MBT-I中的心理教育主题。
therapeutic_implications: 帮助新成员跟上团体进度。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: When new participants join an established group, the individual sessions may also be used to go over the psychoeducational topics covered in MBT-I.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述个体治疗的这一用途。

atoms.claim: 在反社会型人格障碍团体中，制定行为准则是核心任务，但参与者可能难以达成共识。
clinical_signals: 参与者有反社会型人格障碍
therapeutic_implications: 需要讨论参与者的道德价值观、责任感和公平感
不应由临床医生强加行为准则
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Developing a code of conduct is a central feature in groups for ASPD (see Box 13.8).
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确提到制定行为准则是核心特征。

atoms.claim: 临床医生必须既不谴责也不宽恕参与者的暴力行为，而是保持一种试图理解其内在心理状态和暴力前因的良性态度。
clinical_signals: 参与者因暴力行为被转介
therapeutic_implications: 避免引发羞耻感
保持好奇和理解的态度
atoms.evidence_excerpt: the clinician must appear neither to condemn nor condone his/her offenses, but instead maintain a benign attitude of attempting to understand the participant’s internal state of mind and mental precursors of violence.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确要求既不谴责也不宽恕。

atoms.claim: 应通过讨论参与者与他人的互动以及导致暴力的原因，来突出和探索他们自己的行为准则。
clinical_signals: 参与者有反社会型人格障碍
therapeutic_implications: 讨论互动和暴力原因
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Highlight and explore participants’ own code of conduct by discussing their interactions with others and what leads to violence
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自Box 13.8。

atoms.claim: 临床医生需注意不要触发参与者的羞耻感，因为违反自身内部行为准则（如伤害女性）可能引发羞耻和错误感。
clinical_signals: 参与者有反社会型人格障碍
可能违反自身内部行为准则
therapeutic_implications: 采取良性态度
避免评判
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The clinician takes care not to trigger this feeling of shame.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确要求小心避免触发羞耻感。

atoms.claim: 团体临床医生必须设定某些团体原则或规则，以使团体感到安全，但同时也必须允许表达。
therapeutic_implications: 设定规则
允许表达
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The group clinicians must set certain group principles or rules in order for the group to feel safe (see Box 13.9), but must also permit the expression of
atoms.extraction_notes: 句子未完整，但明确提到设定规则以感到安全。

atoms.claim: 对反社会型人格障碍患者施加内疚或鼓励无私是禁忌的。
therapeutic_implications: 避免使用内疚或无私作为动机
contraindications: 施加内疚
鼓励无私
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Applying pressure through inducing guilt and/or encouraging selflessness are contraindicated.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述为禁忌。

atoms.claim: 在MBT-I中，临床医生应解释小组原则背后的理由。
therapeutic_implications: 解释原则理由
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It is important that the clinicians explain the reasons underpinning these principles (see Box 13.10).
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确要求解释理由。

atoms.claim: 在小组中不应重现强制方法或惩罚，因为这些对反社会型人格障碍患者的行为影响甚微。
therapeutic_implications: 避免强制和惩罚
contraindications: 使用强制方法
使用惩罚
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The participants’ experience in life has been of coercive methods and sometimes punishment, all of which have had little effect on their behavior; do not recreate this in the group.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确指示不要重现。

atoms.claim: 鼓励出勤的理由是让个体能够持续处理问题，不规律出勤会导致获益丧失而非巩固。
therapeutic_implications: 强调出勤对问题解决和获益巩固的重要性
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The reason for encouraging attendance is so that the individuals can address their problems consistently; erratic attendance means that gains will be lost rather than consolidated.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述理由。

atoms.claim: 在MBT-I中，种族和性别刻板印象被指出是明显的非心智化现象。
therapeutic_implications: 识别并处理刻板印象作为非心智化现象
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In MBT-I, it is pointed out that racial and sexual stereotypes are manifestly nonmentalized phenomena.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述。
