atoms.claim: 过度和/或与年龄不相称的压力通常会导致奖赏敏感性和心智化能力的损害。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗中需关注压力对心智化的影响
atoms.evidence_excerpt: developmental cascades set in motion as a result of excessive and/or age-inappropriate stress, typically resulting in impairments in reward sensitivity and in the capacity for mentalizing
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确提到过度/年龄不相称压力导致奖赏敏感性和心智化能力损害。

atoms.claim: 从青少年的视角看，心智化和依恋的显著‘损害’是对特定人际环境的适应尝试。
clinical_signals: 在情感忽视和暴力环境中使用工具性攻击
therapeutic_implications: 理解行为背后的适应功能
避免简单将心智化受损视为缺陷
atoms.evidence_excerpt: even marked ‘impairments’ in mentalizing and attachment are in the eye of the beholder. From the perspective of the young person, they represent attempts at adaptation to a specific (interpersonal) environment.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确将心智化损害视为适应尝试。

atoms.claim: 在虐待环境中成长的青少年，抑制心智化通常与对他人的高认知不信任相结合，是保护自我免受进一步虐待和失望的可理解反应。
clinical_signals: 对他人的高认知不信任
therapeutic_implications: 治疗中需建立信任
理解不信任的自我保护功能
atoms.evidence_excerpt: for young people growing up in a context of abuse, the inhibition of mentalizing, typically combined with high levels of epistemic mistrust in others, are an understandable response to protect the self from further abuse and disappointment
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确将抑制心智化和认知不信任视为对虐待环境的适应。

atoms.claim: 人类生物行为应激系统是参与检测、整合和应对威胁的复杂神经结构网络。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The human biobehavioural stress system is a complex system of neural structures that are involved in detecting, integrating, and responding to threat.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接定义应激系统。

atoms.claim: 青春期与HPA轴应激反应性显著增加相关，青少年表现出更高的基础应激水平和更强的应激反应，尤其是对社会排斥和学业压力。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗中需关注青少年对社会排斥和学业压力的敏感性
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Similarly, adolescence is associated with a considerable increase in HPA axis reactivity to stress, compared to children and adults (Casey, Getz, & Galvan, 2008). Adolescents have been shown to have both higher basal stress levels and heightened reaction to stress, and social rejection and academic stressors in particular (Masten et al., 2009; Sebastian, Viding, Williams, & Blakemore, 2010; Sebastian et al., 2011)
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确提到青少年与儿童和成人相比，HPA轴反应性增加，且对社会排斥和学业压力反应更强。

atoms.claim: 有精神病理学风险的青少年会无意中部分生成自己的压力环境（主动压力生成或唤起性人-环境效应），导致恶性循环。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗需帮助青少年识别并打破压力生成循环
atoms.evidence_excerpt: There is now also good evidence to suggest that young people who are at increased risk for the development of psychopathology also unwittingly generate in part their own stressful environment (i.e. active stress-generation or evocative person-environment effects) (Hammen, 2005).
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确提到高风险青少年主动生成压力环境。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 青春期性别差异在奖励侧重
atoms.canonical_name_en: gender differences in adolescent reward emphasis
atoms.claim: 在西方文化中，男孩稍更强调能动性/自主，女孩稍更强调依恋。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗中需考虑性别差异对奖励偏好的影响
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Yet, at least in Western cultures, boys place slightly more emphasis on agency/autonomy, while in girls there is a somewhat greater emphasis on attachment (Luyten & Blatt, 2013; Spear, 2000).
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确提到西方文化中男孩和女孩在奖励侧重上的性别差异。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 青春期社会损失与拒绝的疼痛增强
atoms.canonical_name_en: increased pain of social loss and rejection in adolescence
atoms.claim: 与社交损失和拒绝相关的情感痛苦在青春期增加，尤其在女性中。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗需处理社交拒绝带来的强烈情感痛苦
atoms.evidence_excerpt: They mediate feelings of acceptance, support, agency and validation on the one hand, and the emotional pain associated with social loss and rejection, which is increased in adolescence, particularly in women (Hsu et al., 2015; Spear, 2000).
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确提到社交损失和拒绝的情感痛苦在青春期增加，尤其在女性中。

atoms.claim: 青春期与HPA轴应激反应性显著增加相关，青少年表现出更高的基础应激水平和更强的应激反应，尤其是对社会排斥和学业压力。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗中需关注青少年对社会排斥和学业压力的敏感性
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Similarly, adolescence is associated with a considerable increase in HPA axis reactivity to stress, compared to children and adults (Casey, Getz, & Galvan, 2008). Adolescents have been shown to have both higher basal stress levels and heightened reaction to stress, and social rejection and academic stressors in particular (Masten et al., 2009; Sebastian, Viding, Williams, & Blakemore, 2010; Sebastian et al., 2011)
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述青春期HPA轴反应性增加，并具体指出社会排斥和学业压力是特别应激源。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 不安全依恋与应激系统功能障碍
atoms.canonical_name_en: Insecure attachment and stress system dysfunction
atoms.claim: 在不安全依恋的青少年中，依赖他人并不带来奖赏，因为他们始终认为他人不可用，这导致应激系统功能障碍，增加对心理病理的脆弱性。
clinical_signals: 过度依赖或强迫性自主
therapeutic_implications: 治疗关系可能不被体验为奖赏，需谨慎建立信任
atoms.evidence_excerpt: For insecurely attached individuals, relying on others is not rewarding, as there is always the underlying belief that others will not be available. On the biological level, insecure attachment is therefore associated with increased vulnerability for stress, as expressed in dysfunctions of the stress system (Auerbach et al., 2014; Pizzagalli, 2014; Strathearn, 2011).
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述不安全依恋个体依赖他人无奖赏，并关联应激系统功能障碍。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 催产素对不安全依恋个体的负面效应
atoms.canonical_name_en: Negative effects of oxytocin in insecure attachment
atoms.claim: 在不安全依恋的个体中，催产素水平降低，且给予催产素会导致信任和合作行为减少，皮质醇对应激的反应增加，即使对群体内成员也是如此。
therapeutic_implications: 对不安全依恋青少年使用催产素相关干预需谨慎
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Individuals with an insecure attachment history show decreased basal oxytocin levels and, in these individuals, oxytocin administration leads to decreased trust and cooperative behaviour, and increased cortisol response to stress, even in relation to in-group members (Bartz et al., 2011; Feldman, 2017).
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述不安全依恋个体催产素水平低，且外源性催产素产生负面效应。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 青春期奖赏系统的性别差异
atoms.canonical_name_en: Gender differences in adolescent reward system
atoms.claim: 在西方文化中，男孩更强调自主性/自主，而女孩更强调依恋。
clinical_signals: 性别差异在依恋与自主性偏好上
therapeutic_implications: 治疗中需考虑性别差异对奖赏系统的影响
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Yet, at least in Western cultures, boys place slightly more emphasis on agency/autonomy, while in girls there is a somewhat greater emphasis on attachment (Luyten & Blatt, 2013; Spear, 2000).
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述性别差异，但限定于西方文化。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 催产素对群体内外的不同效应
atoms.canonical_name_en: Oxytocin effects differ by group membership
atoms.claim: 催产素的积极效应似乎仅限于群体内成员；对群体外成员，催产素增加不信任和减少合作行为，即使在安全依恋个体中也是如此。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗中需注意群体归属对催产素效应的影响
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Importantly, these positive effects of oxytocin seem limited to in-group members. In contrast, increased levels of oxytocin appear to lead to increased distrust, and less cooperative behaviour in relation to out-group members, even in securely attached individuals (Bartz, Zaki, Bolger, & Ochsner, 2011).
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述催产素效应因群体内外而异。

atoms.claim: 心智化为基础的治疗通常采用滴定式干预，以考虑依恋激活对心智化的负面影响。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应根据患者的依恋激活水平调整干预强度
response_constraints: 干预应逐步增加，避免过度激活依恋系统
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Mentalization-Based Treatment, therefore, typically titrates interventions to take into account the negative effects of attachment activation on mentalizing (Bateman & Fonagy, 2019).
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确提及MBT的滴定式干预原则。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 不安全依恋与压力系统功能障碍
atoms.canonical_name_en: insecure attachment and stress system dysfunction
atoms.claim: 不安全依恋与压力系统功能障碍相关，表现为对压力的脆弱性增加。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗中需关注压力调节
atoms.evidence_excerpt: On the biological level, insecure attachment is therefore associated with increased vulnerability for stress, as expressed in dysfunctions of the stress system (Auerbach et al., 2014; Pizzagalli, 2014; Strathearn, 2011).
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述不安全依恋与压力系统功能障碍的关联。

atoms.claim: 基于心智化的治疗通常对干预进行滴定，以考虑依恋激活对心智化的负面影响。
therapeutic_implications: 避免用温暖和支持使青少年不堪重负
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Mentalization-Based Treatment, therefore, typically titrates interventions to take into account the negative effects of attachment activation on mentalizing (Bateman & Fonagy, 2019).
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述MBT滴定干预以考虑依恋激活的负面影响。

atoms.canonical_name_en: reorganisation of the reward system in adolescence
atoms.claim: 青少年期奖赏系统的重组可能导致“迷你奖赏缺乏综合征”，表现为易 boredom、对归属感和成就的强烈需求受挫后产生强烈拒绝感和失败感，进而导致挫折和攻击。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Any clinician working with adolescents is familiar with this ‘syndrome’: adolescents may be easily bored and, at the same time, the frustration of their strong needs for belongingness and/or achievement and the status that is associated may give rise to intense feelings of rejection and failure, or a combination of both, and subsequent frustration and aggression.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述青少年奖赏缺乏综合征的表现。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 心智化能力与自我意识情绪
atoms.claim: 心智化能力的发展使自我意识情绪（如尴尬、后悔、羞耻和内疚）得以出现，这些情绪本质上是适应性的，但若慢性或过度则可能变得适应不良。
clinical_signals: 慢性或过度的自我意识情绪
therapeutic_implications: 关注自我意识情绪的调节
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Self-consciousness also led to the emergence of so-called self-conscious emotions (e.g., embarrassment, regret, shame, and guilt) which, although in essence adaptive, may become maladaptive when chronic and/or excessive.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述心智化与自我意识情绪的关系。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 心智化能力与想象力的脆弱性
atoms.canonical_name_en: mentalizing capacity and vulnerability from imagination
atoms.claim: 想象力不仅使人类能够设想理想自我状态，也使人痛苦地意识到实际自我与理想自我之间的差距。
clinical_signals: 理想自我与现实自我差距的痛苦意识
therapeutic_implications: 处理理想与现实自我差距
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Moreover, the capacity for imagination not only allows humans to envision an ideal state of the self but also to become painfully aware of the discrepancy between the actual and ideal self-states.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述想象力带来的脆弱性。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 青春期社会认知发展轨迹争议
atoms.canonical_name_en: linear vs. non-linear trajectory of social cognition in adolescence
atoms.claim: 关于青春期社会认知发展是线性增长还是非线性（中期下降）存在持续讨论。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应关注个体差异，不假设心智化能力持续线性增长
atoms.evidence_excerpt: These findings have led to an ongoing discussion whether the development of social cognition in adolescence follows a linear (with levels of social cognition simply increasing with age) or a non-linear trajectory (with levels of mentalizing actually decreasing in mid-adolescence because of the reorganisation of mentalizing networks).
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确提及关于青春期社会认知发展轨迹的持续讨论。

atoms.claim: 人类社会组织的社会嵌入性可能导致缺乏协作和沟通技能的个体产生彻底的孤立和孤独感。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗应关注提升社交技能以减轻孤独感
atoms.evidence_excerpt: the quintessential role of social embeddedness in the fabric of human social organisation may lead to feelings of utter isolation and loneliness in those who lack skills required for human collaboration and communication (Luyten et al. 2020).
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述社会嵌入性可能导致缺乏协作和沟通技能者的孤立和孤独感。

atoms.claim: 心智化能力使人类能够超越物理现实，进行想象，但也可能使个体痛苦地意识到实际自我与理想自我之间的差距。
clinical_signals: 对理想与现实自我差距的痛苦意识
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师需帮助青少年处理理想与现实自我差距带来的痛苦
atoms.evidence_excerpt: the capacity for imagination not only allows humans to envision an ideal state of the self but also to become painfully aware of the discrepancy between the actual and ideal self-states.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述想象力使人类能够设想理想自我状态，但也痛苦地意识到实际与理想自我之间的差距。

atoms.claim: 社交嵌入性在人类社会组织中至关重要，缺乏协作与沟通技能的青少年可能感到极度孤立和孤独。
therapeutic_implications: 评估青少年社交技能，促进协作与沟通能力发展
atoms.evidence_excerpt: the quintessential role of social embeddedness in the fabric of human social organisation may lead to feelings of utter isolation and loneliness in those who lack skills required for human collaboration and communication
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确提到缺乏协作与沟通技能会导致孤立和孤独，且上下文聚焦青春期。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 青春期心智化暂时下降
atoms.claim: 假设在皮层变化期间，青少年的心智化技能可能暂时中断，即社会认知的'青春期下降'。
therapeutic_implications: 在青春期中期对心智化能力保持耐心，提供支持
atoms.evidence_excerpt: it is hypothesised that during these cortical changes, mentalizing skills of adolescents may be temporarily disrupted, also referred to as the mentalizing or pubertal ‘dip’ in social cognition
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文使用'it is hypothesised'，表明是假设。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 青春期心智化下降与激素变化
atoms.canonical_name_en: pubertal dip related to hormonal changes
atoms.claim: 青春期心智化下降与激素变化有关。
therapeutic_implications: 考虑激素变化对心智化的潜在影响
atoms.evidence_excerpt: This pubertal dip in mentalizing has been related to hormonal changes.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确陈述了关联。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 早期逆境青少年与同伴的恶性循环
atoms.canonical_name_en: early adversity adolescents may spiral with peers
atoms.claim: 有早期逆境史的青少年可能因无法从矫正性体验中获益而陷入社会孤立，或寻求与有类似问题的同伴进行心智校准，在社交媒体作用下可能迅速失控。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: As a result, these young people are increasingly cut off from corrective experiences and might end up in complete social isolation and loneliness and/or seek social recalibration of the mind with peers that suffer from similar problems. With the current availability of social media, the latter strategy, in particular, may rapidly spiral out of control.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述后果和风险。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 过度心智化与心智化回避
atoms.claim: 无法理解青春期变化可能导致过度心智化（hypermentalizing）和/或心智化回避（hypomentalizing），两者均可视为避免思考的防御策略。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The inability to make sense of changes that come with the advent of adolescence may lead to excessive mentalizing (hypermentalizing) and/or the avoidance of mentalizing (hypomentalizing). Both can be seen as a defensive strategy to avoid thinking
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述因果关系和防御功能。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 早期逆境对心理化和认识论信任的影响
atoms.canonical_name_en: impact of early adversity on mentalizing and epistemic trust
atoms.claim: 早期逆境不仅损害心理化能力，也损害认识论信任，从而削弱面对新挑战时重新校准心智的能力。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: adversity undermines not only mentalizing capacities but also the capacity for epistemic trust and thus the capacity to re-calibrate one’s mind when faced with new challenges
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确陈述。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 理解青少年主观体验的谦逊态度
atoms.claim: 成人应保持谦逊，认识到自己理解青少年大脑与环境互动影响的能力有限，因为青少年看待世界的方式往往与成人不同。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: it behoves us to show modesty when it comes down to our own capacity to understand these influences in a human being that sees the world often very differently from how we do.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确陈述。

atoms.claim: 从青少年视角看，某些行为是适应策略，而外界通常视其为病态和异常。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: from the perspective of the adolescent, these represent adaptation strategies, whilst the outside world typically tends to consider these strategies as pathological and abnormal.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述青少年视角与外界视角的差异。

atoms.claim: 心智化使我们能够理解他人的体验，从而从他们的视角看世界。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: it is the essence of the mentalizing approach that mentalizing allows us to understand the experience of the other, and thus see the world from their perspective.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述心智化的核心功能。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 成人理解青少年的困难
atoms.claim: 成人试图理解青少年及其大脑时，误解可能尤其普遍。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: This is probably especially true for any adult trying to understand the adolescent and his or her brain.
atoms.extraction_notes: 使用'probably especially true'表示强烈暗示。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 青少年对大脑与环境互动的理解缺陷
atoms.canonical_name_en: adolescent impairments in understanding brain-environment interactions
atoms.claim: 青少年通常在理解大脑与环境及其互动如何决定自我感和他人感方面存在重大缺陷。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: adolescents often have major impairments in understanding how brain and environment, and their interactions, determine their sense of self and others
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述青少年存在重大缺陷。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 成人对自身理解能力的谦逊
atoms.canonical_name_en: adult modesty about own understanding capacity
atoms.claim: 成人应对自身理解这些影响的能力保持谦逊，因为青少年看待世界的方式往往与成人非常不同。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: it behoves us to show modesty when it comes down to our own capacity to understand these influences in a human being that sees the world often very differently from how we do.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确建议成人保持谦逊。

atoms.claim: 青少年面临建立自主性和自我导向身份的发展任务。
clinical_signals: 感到被自我体验失败淹没
在处理他人或关系时感到困惑
therapeutic_implications: 帮助青少年恢复适应性的发展轨迹
实现自主性、身份、掌控感和成就感
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Young people are faced with the developmental task of establishing autonomy and self-directed identity.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述青少年发展任务。

atoms.claim: 心智化困难是青少年在情感调节、冲动行为以及家庭和人际关系冲突中所有挣扎的基础。
therapeutic_implications: 通过恢复心智化能力减少人际困惑
增强韧性和恢复力
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The underlying principle of this model is that difficulties in mentalization underpin all the struggles young people experience with affect regulation, impulsive behaviour as well as conflict in families and other interpersonal relationships.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述心智化困难是基础。

atoms.claim: 保护因素包括反思能力、能动性和关联性，这些可总结为心智化能力。
therapeutic_implications: 增强反思自身想法、感受和动机的能力
增强作为有效且对自己行为负责的自我感
增强反思他人心智的能力
atoms.evidence_excerpt: They all showed a) a capacity for reflection about their thoughts, feelings and motivations, b) a sense of agency, namely a sense of oneself as effective and responsible for one’s actions, and c) relatedness, namely the ability to reflect on the minds of others
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确列出三个保护因素。

atoms.claim: MBT-A的目标是提高青少年更准确地觉察自己和周围他人心智的能力，以及觉察自己对他人影响的能力。
therapeutic_implications: 减少冲动行为
降低风险
减少关系风暴
带来希望感和掌控感
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In MBT-A therapy, the aim is to achieve precisely that – an increased ability in the adolescent to be mindful of themselves and those around them in a more accurate way, as well as being mindful of the impact they have on others.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述MBT-A目标。

atoms.claim: 家庭中强制性的非心智化循环会维持、强化和加剧青少年及其照顾者的非心智化状态。
therapeutic_implications: 帮助家庭从强制性的非心智化循环转向心智化互动
促进信任、安全、亲密、有效沟通和问题解决
response_constraints: 最小化父母的无能感或被责备感
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Often coercive, non-mentalizing cycles in families maintain, reinforce and exacerbate non-mentalizing in young people and their caregivers, leading to parental rejection, criticism and punishment, or disengagement, withdrawal and acting out behaviour in young people.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述非心智化循环及其后果。

atoms.claim: 在MBT-A中，父母和青少年被邀请作为治疗伙伴，从关注行为转向心智化对话。
therapeutic_implications: 使家庭成员理解彼此观点
以可接受的方式分享自己的观点
重新激发好奇心、尊重、共情、互惠和能动性
response_constraints: 避免试图强制改变
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In MBT-A, parents and young people are invited to work as partners in a treatment designed to shift from focusing on behaviours to a mentalizing conversation that enables family members to grasp each other’s point of view and share their own in a palatable way.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述合作治疗原则。

atoms.claim: 保护性因素包括反思自身想法、感受和动机的能力，能动性（即感到自己有效且对自己的行为负责），以及关联性（即反思他人心智的能力），这些可概括为心智化能力。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: They all showed a) a capacity for reflection about their thoughts, feelings and motivations, b) a sense of agency, namely a sense of oneself as effective and responsible for one’s actions, and c) relatedness, namely the ability to reflect on the minds of others
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用保护性因素列表，并总结为心智化能力。

atoms.claim: 心智化立场本质上是关怀和同情的态度，治疗师表现出温暖、尊重和真正的兴趣，对青少年的生活和内心感到好奇。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The mentalizing stance is essentially an attitude of care and compassion. An MBT-A therapist shows warmth and respect to the patients and conveys a real interest in them. The MBT-A therapist is curious about them, their lives, and what they are feeling.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用心智化立场的定义。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 减少父母的无能感或羞耻感
atoms.claim: 实现心智化互动需要最小化父母因孩子问题而感到的无能、被责备或羞耻的体验。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Such an aim requires minimising the parent’s experience of incompetence or of being blamed or shamed for their children’s problems.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 从关注行为转向心智化对话
atoms.canonical_name_en: shifting from focusing on behaviors to mentalizing conversation
atoms.claim: 在MBT-A中，父母和青少年被邀请作为治疗伙伴，从关注行为转向心智化对话，使家庭成员能够理解彼此的观点并以可接受的方式分享自己的观点。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In MBT-A, parents and young people are invited to work as partners in a treatment designed to shift from focusing on behaviours to a mentalizing conversation that enables family members to grasp each other’s point of view and share their own in a palatable way.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: MBT-A对自伤和边缘性人格特质的效果
atoms.canonical_name_en: MBT-A effectiveness on self-harm and borderline traits
atoms.claim: MBT-A在减少自伤和新兴边缘性人格特质方面优于常规治疗，且效果在治疗结束后六个月仍维持。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: When applied to adolescents (MBT- A), the therapy showed increased effectiveness over treatment as usual in terms of reduction in self-harm (p < 0.013) as demonstrated by Rossouw and Fonagy (2012) in a randomised controlled trial. A reduction in emerging borderline personality traits (p < 0.034) was also found. These gains were maintained six months after treatment ended.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用研究结果。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 对自伤青少年的共情困难
atoms.canonical_name_en: difficulty in remaining empathic with self-harming adolescents
atoms.claim: 当青少年自伤时，家人和工作人员有时难以保持共情和温暖，可能感到被破坏、愤怒、无力或焦虑，甚至认为青少年是故意为之。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In the situations where young people harm themselves, it is at times hard for family members and staff to remain empathic and warm. Family and staff can often feel that self-inflicting injuries are deliberately destructive of their treatment, or that it is attention-seeking. Parents and staff can feel undermined, angry, powerless or very anxious. Not uncommonly, parents and staff can at times think “you are doing this deliberately to make me feel powerless or anxious”.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用。

atoms.claim: 心智化立场本质上是关怀和同情的态度。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应展现温暖和尊重，传达对患者的真正兴趣。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The mentalizing stance is essentially an attitude of care and compassion.

atoms.claim: 采取不知晓立场允许治疗师提出开放性问题，例如“在你感到想伤害自己之前发生了什么？”
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应提出开放性问题以探索患者的体验。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Adopting a not-knowing stance allows us to ask open questions, such as “what happened before you felt like hurting yourself?”

atoms.claim: 在MBT-A中，治疗师相当主动，不采取中立立场，避免长时间沉默。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应主动提问，避免长时间沉默。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In MBT-A, the therapist is quite active. The therapist does not adopt a neutral stance and avoids long silences.

atoms.claim: MBT-A中最常用的技术是支持与共情。
therapeutic_implications: 当患者失调时，应优先使用支持与共情。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The most frequently used technique in MBT-A is support and empathy.

atoms.claim: MBT-A在减少自伤和边缘性人格特质方面优于常规治疗，效果在治疗结束后六个月仍维持。
therapeutic_implications: MBT-A可有效减少青少年自伤和边缘性人格特质。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: When applied to adolescents (MBT- A), the therapy showed increased effectiveness over treatment as usual in terms of reduction in self-harm (p < 0.013) as demonstrated by Rossouw and Fonagy (2012) in a randomised controlled trial. A reduction in emerging borderline personality traits (p < 0.034) was also found. These gains were maintained six months after treatment ended.

atoms.claim: MBT治疗师需要具备以直接、真实、透明的方式与患者沟通的能力，使用简单明确的陈述以最小化过度唤醒患者的风险。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应使用简单明确的陈述，避免复杂语言。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: An ability to communicate with the patient in a direct, authentic, transparent manner, using simple and unambiguous statements to minimise the risk of over-arousing the client.

atoms.claim: MBT治疗师需要具备对患者心理状态突然和戏剧性的心智化失败保持觉察并敏感回应的能力。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应识别并敏感回应患者心智化的突然失败。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: An ability to become aware of and respond sensitively to sudden and dramatic failures of mentalization in the patient.

atoms.claim: 采用不知晓姿态允许治疗师提出开放式问题，例如“在你感到想伤害自己之前发生了什么？”
clinical_signals: 患者难以关联内心世界
患者声称冲动无意义或前因
therapeutic_implications: 通过好奇和提问探索患者体验
帮助情感展开，便于探索或情感接触
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Adopting a not-knowing stance allows us to ask open questions, such as “what happened before you felt like hurting yourself?”

atoms.claim: 在MBT-A中，治疗师相当主动，不采取中立姿态，避免长时间沉默。
clinical_signals: 年轻人难以关联内心世界
therapeutic_implications: 主动姿态有助于年轻人探索内心世界
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In MBT-A, the therapist is quite active. The therapist does not adopt a neutral stance and avoids long silences. The active stance is particularly helpful when young people find it hard to relate to their inner world.

atoms.canonical_name_en: focus on here and now, not the past
atoms.claim: 治疗焦点是患者的心灵而非行为，主要关注此时此地，而非过去。
clinical_signals: 患者谈论当前情绪和恐惧
therapeutic_implications: 避免对遥远过去的解释，以免患者感到被否定或导致治疗破裂
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Our focus in therapy is the patient’s mind and not their behaviour, and we are mostly interested in the here and now, and not the past. For example, if a patient talks about upset feelings and fears about her boyfriend leaving her, we do not think it is helpful to make interpretations of her distant past as it would distance us from her current feelings and the patient is likely to experience this as invalidating.

atoms.claim: 当患者处于非心智化状态，无法理解或连接驱动行为的感受时，表现为假性模式或伪心智化，即行动与情感脱节。
clinical_signals: 患者无法连接情感与行为
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师需要帮助患者走出伪心智化状态，建立情感连接
atoms.evidence_excerpt: So here we can see Sally in a non-mentalizing state of mind, unable to make sense or even connect with the feelings which underpin her actions – in other words, she is in a state of pretend mode or pseudo-mentalizing where we see a disconnect between actions and affect.

atoms.canonical_name_en: focus on here and now, not the past
atoms.claim: 治疗应聚焦于患者的当下心理状态而非过去，对过去的解释可能使患者感到被误解并导致治疗破裂。
clinical_signals: 患者可能对过去解释感到疏远
therapeutic_implications: 维持干预在患者最可能连接情绪的水平
避免过早解释过去
response_constraints: 不进行远距离过去解释
contraindications: 当患者当前情绪强烈时，避免过去解释
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Our focus in therapy is the patient’s mind and not their behaviour, and we are mostly interested in the here and now, and not the past.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明治疗焦点，适用于青少年。

atoms.claim: 当患者处于假性心智化状态时，其行动与情感脱节，无法理解或连接驱动行为的情感。
clinical_signals: 患者报告自伤行为但无法解释原因
患者说‘只是发生了’或‘就是想’
therapeutic_implications: 需要帮助患者连接情感与行动
通过仔细探索事件细节来揭示情感
response_constraints: 避免直接挑战或说教
使用好奇和探索性提问
atoms.evidence_excerpt: So here we can see Sally in a non-mentalizing state of mind, unable to make sense or even connect with the feelings which underpin her actions – in other words, she is in a state of pretend mode or pseudo-mentalizing where we see a disconnect between actions and affect.
atoms.extraction_notes: 通过案例明确描述假性心智化状态。

atoms.claim: 通过仔细探索事件的具体细节，可以揭示患者的情感，帮助其从非心智化状态中走出。
clinical_signals: 患者处于非心智化状态
therapeutic_implications: 使用具体问题引导回忆
如‘想象我是你肩上的苍蝇，我会看到什么？’
response_constraints: 放慢节奏
避免直接给出解释
atoms.evidence_excerpt: So, by carefully exploring the detail of the event, the affect unfolded and became clear.
atoms.extraction_notes: 案例中明确展示此技术。

atoms.claim: 高唤醒可触发患者进入过度心智化状态，导致冲动性（目的论）行为作为对难以忍受的内在状态的解决方案。
clinical_signals: 患者快速从过度心智化到感到不堪重负
therapeutic_implications: 通过探索降低唤醒
帮助患者理解从想法到行为的链条
response_constraints: 避免进一步增加唤醒
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It also became clear how this increased the arousal in Sally and triggered her into a state of hypermentalization, which finally led to her seeking an impulsive (teleological) solution to the unbearable internal state.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述过度心智化与冲动行为的关系。

atoms.claim: 治疗师可以使用‘思维气泡’技术帮助患者考虑他人的心理状态，从而拓宽对事件的理解。
clinical_signals: 患者固着于单一负面解释
患者难以考虑其他可能性
therapeutic_implications: 提问‘如果在她头上画一个思维气泡，里面会是什么？’
促进心智化
response_constraints: 以好奇而非教导的方式提问
atoms.evidence_excerpt: If we were to draw a thought bubble above her head, what do you think would be in it?
atoms.extraction_notes: 案例中明确使用此技术。

atoms.claim: 治疗师应先验证患者的感受，然后温和地挑战其思维过程，例如指出‘你的思维可能过度运转并得出最坏情景’。
clinical_signals: 患者表达强烈负面自我归因
therapeutic_implications: 先共情再挑战
使用‘从我的角度看’等软化语言
response_constraints: 避免直接否定患者感受
atoms.evidence_excerpt: I can see how you can feel like that, but from my perspective it feels a bit as if when she didn’t greet you, your mind went into overdrive a bit to try and make sense of why she didn’t greet you, and you arrived at an understanding that really hurt your feelings – as if your mind arrived at the worst possible scenario in seconds, isn’t it?
atoms.extraction_notes: 案例中治疗师同时验证感受并挑战。

atoms.claim: 治疗师可以询问患者‘如果你的朋友看到这个情况，他们会怎么想？’来帮助患者考虑其他解释。
clinical_signals: 患者难以从他人角度看问题
therapeutic_implications: 拓宽患者对事件的理解
促进心智化
response_constraints: 以假设性问题引导
atoms.evidence_excerpt: If a friend of you saw her not greeting you, what would your friend have thought?
atoms.extraction_notes: 案例中明确使用此技术。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 支持性技术包括采取具体行动
atoms.claim: 支持性技术有时需要治疗师采取具体行动，这有助于管理风险并为青少年提供心智化支架。
clinical_signals: 高风险自伤或自杀行为
therapeutic_implications: 制定清晰具体的危机计划
与学校、家长等系统合作
response_constraints: 在治疗边界内采取具体行动
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The concrete action fulfils two functions; on the one hand, it helps with the management of risk that these young people present with, and on the other hand, it supports them in their quest to manage in their lives by creating supportive and mentalizing scaffolding around them.

atoms.claim: 过度心智化是一种非心智化模式，表现为快速得出最坏可能性的理解，导致情感淹没和行动化。
clinical_signals: 快速从过度心智化到行动化
患者只意识到自伤冲动，与潜在心智状态脱节
therapeutic_implications: 通过仔细探索帮助患者重新接触心智状态
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Her felt experience bypassed this process of understanding as she went very fast from hypermentalization and hyperarousal to feeling overwhelmed and needing to act out; hence she was only aware of the desire to cut herself, disconnected from the mental states which underpinned it.

atoms.claim: 治疗师保持支持性和好奇的立场，尝试与患者建立情感联系。
clinical_signals: 患者处于非心智化状态
therapeutic_implications: 维持支持、安慰和共情的关系
response_constraints: 不破坏患者的自主性
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In this example, we see how the therapist maintained a supportive and curious stance and tried to make emotional contact with Sally.

atoms.claim: 与青少年周围的系统（如学校、家长）合作，帮助他们理解青少年并提供支持。
clinical_signals: 高风险自伤或自杀行为
therapeutic_implications: 与学校沟通
与家长会面
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In our work with young people, we often end up working with the wider system around the young person too, such as communicating with their school to help the school understand what they are going through, to be more supportive, or meeting with the parents to help them with their understanding of the young person.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 制定清晰具体的危机计划
atoms.claim: 对于高风险青少年，制定清晰具体的危机计划有助于维持安全。
clinical_signals: 高风险自伤或自杀行为
therapeutic_implications: 制定危机计划
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It is also important to have a clear and concrete crisis plan which can help both young people and their parents and others around them to maintain their safety.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 谨慎表扬以鼓励心智化
atoms.claim: 当患者使用心智化并取得积极结果时，治疗师应谨慎地表扬患者，以鼓励和支持改变。
therapeutic_implications: 给予谨慎的表扬
atoms.evidence_excerpt: An ability to judiciously praise the patient when the patient uses mentalizing with a positive outcome to encourage and support change.

atoms.claim: 在青少年工作中，治疗师常需与学校、家长等更广泛的系统合作，以帮助系统理解青少年并提供支持。
clinical_signals: 青少年存在自伤或自杀风险
therapeutic_implications: 与学校沟通
与家长会面
制定清晰具体的危机计划
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In our work with young people, we often end up working with the wider system around the young person too, such as communicating with their school to help the school understand what they are going through, to be more supportive, or meeting with the parents to help them with their understanding of the young person.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了与系统合作的具体方式。

atoms.claim: 支持性技术有时需要采取具体行动，这有助于管理风险并为青少年创建支持性的心智化支架。
clinical_signals: 青少年存在较高自伤或自杀风险
therapeutic_implications: 采取具体行动
制定危机计划
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The concrete action fulfils two functions; on the one hand, it helps with the management of risk that these young people present with, and on the other hand, it supports them in their quest to manage in their lives by creating supportive and mentalizing scaffolding around them.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了具体行动的双重功能。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 澄清事件以揭示心理状态
atoms.canonical_name_en: Clarification of events to reveal mental states
atoms.claim: 通过积极提问澄清事件或行为，可以揭示事件背后的心理状态；仅询问心理状态而不详细探索事件可能无法接近心理状态。
clinical_signals: 患者行为或事件不清晰
therapeutic_implications: 使用澄清技术
详细探索事件
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Clarification of events can frequently bring to the fore the mental states which underpinned the event. If we merely asked about the mental state without the detailed exploration of the event, it may not have led us any closer to the mental state – as it was the case with Sally.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明了澄清事件与揭示心理状态的关系。

atoms.claim: 患者陈述自我憎恨可能是具体化心智化的证据，也是异己自我的证据。
therapeutic_implications: 识别具体化心智化
尝试连接导致心智化丧失的心理状态
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Sally’s statement that she hated herself might be incorrectly perceived as the feeling state, which created her dysregulation. However, such a state of self-hatred is evidence of concrete mentalizing, and it is evidence of the alien self, described in Chapter 7.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确将自我憎恨定义为具体化心智化和异己自我的证据。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 详细阐述感受以揭示潜在状态
atoms.canonical_name_en: Elaboration of feelings to reveal underlying states
atoms.claim: 详细阐述患者的感受可以揭示愤怒之下的深层羞耻感等不同心理状态。
clinical_signals: 患者表现出愤怒等表面情绪
therapeutic_implications: 详细阐述感受
探索感受与行为的联系
atoms.evidence_excerpt: However, careful elaboration of the patient’s feelings may expose a deep sense of shame underneath the rage.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明了详细阐述感受可以揭示潜在状态。

atoms.claim: 澄清事件可以经常揭示支撑事件的心理状态。
therapeutic_implications: 通过详细探索事件来连接心理状态
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Clarification of events can frequently bring to the fore the mental states which underpinned the event.

atoms.claim: 自我憎恨的状态是具体化心智化的证据，也是异己自我的证据。
therapeutic_implications: 需要探索导致心智化丧失的心理状态
atoms.evidence_excerpt: However, such a state of self-hatred is evidence of concrete mentalizing, and it is evidence of the alien self, described in Chapter 7.

atoms.claim: 必须真诚地验证患者的感受，因为患者经常遭遇无效的环境。
therapeutic_implications: 采取验证立场
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It is crucial to validate our patients’ feelings authentically. Our patients frequently encounter an invalidating environment; hence in the treatment of such young people, we must adopt a validating stance.

atoms.claim: 如果患者的情感得到验证，他们更可能接受挑战；否则有感到愚蠢的风险。
therapeutic_implications: 在挑战前先验证患者的感受
response_constraints: 避免让患者感到愚蠢
atoms.evidence_excerpt: A patient is also more likely to take a challenge on board if their feelings are validated; otherwise, there is a risk of them feeling stupid.

atoms.claim: 基本心智化是帮助青少年和父母更好地心智化他人，并更了解自己的感受和心理状态。
therapeutic_implications: 使用提问、澄清、阐述和挑战等技术来激发好奇心和不了解姿态
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The crux of the work is helping young people and their parents to become better able to mentalize those around them, as well as be more aware of their own feelings and other mental states.

atoms.claim: 在心理等价模式下，心理图像可能很快被视为事实。
therapeutic_implications: 帮助打开百叶窗以更准确地理解他人心理状态
atoms.evidence_excerpt: With the shutters closed, we are left with our mental images of what goes on around us, but there is no reality check; hence there is the risk that the mental images may soon be treated as facts (mode of psychic equivalence).

atoms.claim: MBT-A治疗师使用不了解姿态来激发对他人心理的好奇心。
clinical_signals: 患者对他人心理状态缺乏好奇
therapeutic_implications: 使用提问、澄清等技术
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The MBT-A therapist uses the techniques described above, such as asking questions, seeking clarification, using elaboration and challenge where needed to generate curiosity and a not-knowing stance about the minds of others.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 帮助患者接触自杀幻想下的情感
atoms.canonical_name_en: Helping Patient Make Emotional Contact with Feelings Underneath Suicidal Fantasies
atoms.claim: 治疗师帮助患者与自杀幻想下的情感建立情感联系，从而能够处理这些情感。
therapeutic_implications: 探索情感背后的真实感受
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In this way, the therapist helped the patient to make emotional contact with her feelings underneath the suicidal fantasies, which would then enable them to work with these feelings.

atoms.claim: 基本心智化的核心是帮助青少年及其父母更好地心智化周围的人，并更了解自己的感受和其他心理状态。
clinical_signals: 来访者表现出对他人心理状态缺乏好奇
来访者将心理图像当作事实（心理等价模式）
therapeutic_implications: 通过提问、寻求澄清、详细阐述和挑战来激发好奇心和不知情立场
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The crux of the work is helping young people and their parents to become better able to mentalize those around them, as well as be more aware of their own feelings and other mental states.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述了基本心智化的核心目标。

atoms.claim: 基本心智化试图建立的是：在心灵盲点时刻暂停，尝试想象相关人员的内心状态，并运用想象力设想他人当时的感受。
clinical_signals: 来访者或家长表现出缺乏对他人心理状态的好奇
来访者或家长基于单一视角行动
therapeutic_implications: 激发对心理状态的好奇心，以探索不同的视角
强调与感受的连接而非认知
atoms.evidence_excerpt: This is what basic mentalizing in MBT is trying to establish: stopping and pausing a moment of mind blindness, trying to imagine what was going on for those involved and also trying to use imagination to envision the feelings someone else may have had when they did what they did. We try and ignite curiosity about mental states in order to see if we can arrive at a different perspective.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了基本心智化的核心干预原则。

atoms.claim: 治疗师可以在治疗中适当使用自我表露，例如分享自己可能的感受，以帮助来访者探索不同视角。
clinical_signals: 来访者难以理解他人感受
治疗师认为自我表露可能有助于治疗
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师可以表达自己的假设感受，并邀请来访者确认或修正
response_constraints: 自我表露应谨慎使用，以促进心智化而非替代来访者的体验
atoms.evidence_excerpt: We can use ourselves if it seems that it may be helpful therapeutically. As an example, if the dad in this example spoke to us about what happened, we may say things like: I think if one of my neighbours shouted at me like that, I may have felt very embarrassed, but that is me, I don’t know if that is what you felt….
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了治疗师使用自我表露的技术。

atoms.claim: MBT-A治疗师使用提问、寻求澄清、详细阐述和挑战等技术，以激发好奇心和不知情立场。
clinical_signals: 青少年表现出心智化困难
青少年处于非心智化模式
therapeutic_implications: 运用MBT-A特定技术促进心智化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The MBT-A therapist uses the techniques described above, such as asking questions, seeking clarification, using elaboration and challenge where needed to generate curiosity and a not-knowing stance about the minds of others.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确提及MBT-A治疗师使用的技术。

atoms.claim: 通过改善心智化，个体可以看到心理状态如何与行为相联系，进而影响周围的人。
clinical_signals: 来访者难以理解自己或他人行为背后的心理状态
therapeutic_implications: 帮助来访者识别心理状态与行为之间的关联
atoms.evidence_excerpt: By getting better at mentalizing, they can see how mental states are linked to their behaviour, which in turn has an impact on those around them.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了心智化改善带来的结果。

atoms.claim: 在MBT中，首先验证患者的感受，否则患者会感到更羞辱而无法进行心智化。
therapeutic_implications: 先验证感受，再帮助患者反思
response_constraints: 避免让患者感到更羞辱
atoms.evidence_excerpt: With this technique, we try and validate the dad’s feeling first; otherwise, he will feel more humiliated and not be able to mentalize.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明验证感受是前提条件。

atoms.claim: MBT通过想象和探索其他可能性来激发对心理状态的好奇心。
therapeutic_implications: 帮助患者想象他人的感受
探索不同视角
response_constraints: 强调与感受的连接而非认知
atoms.evidence_excerpt: We try and ignite curiosity about mental states in order to see if we can arrive at a different perspective. This stage is imaginative, and it is exploring other possibilities.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述MBT技术中的想象阶段。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 使用治疗师自身感受作为示范
atoms.canonical_name_en: using therapist's own feelings as example
atoms.claim: 治疗师可以使用自己的感受作为例子，帮助患者探索自己的感受。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师分享自己的感受
邀请患者确认是否类似
response_constraints: 以试探性语气表达
避免强加感受
atoms.evidence_excerpt: We can use ourselves if it seems that it may be helpful therapeutically. As an example, if the dad in this example spoke to us about what happened, we may say things like: I think if one of my neighbours shouted at me like that, I may have felt very embarrassed, but that is me, I don’t know if that is what you felt….
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明治疗师可以使用自身感受作为示范。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 使用游戏性技术促进心智化
atoms.canonical_name_en: using playful techniques to promote mentalizing
atoms.claim: 当患者难以想象他人视角时，可以使用游戏性技术，如画图或扮演记者。
therapeutic_implications: 使用画图或角色扮演
降低防御
response_constraints: 保持游戏性
避免压力
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Sometimes it helps to be playful and ask the dad to be an interviewer for a newspaper and to ask the boy about events of the day prior to him kicking the pots.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述游戏性技术。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 帮助患者觉察自身感受而非直接行动
atoms.canonical_name_en: helping patient notice own feelings rather than act on them
atoms.claim: 帮助父亲觉察自己的感受而非直接行动，并激发对孩子的兴趣，有助于理解孩子的感受。
therapeutic_implications: 暂停和停顿
想象他人感受
response_constraints: 先验证感受
再引导好奇
atoms.evidence_excerpt: If the dad could be helped to notice his own feelings, rather than just act on them, and then be more curious about the boy, he may have found out what happened.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明帮助患者觉察感受而非行动。

atoms.claim: 在MBT-A中，首先验证父亲（家长）的感受，否则他会感到更羞辱而无法心智化。
therapeutic_implications: 先验证感受，再帮助反思
atoms.evidence_excerpt: With this technique, we try and validate the dad’s feeling first; otherwise, he will feel more humiliated and not be able to mentalize.

atoms.claim: 在MBT-A中，可以请父亲像记者一样询问男孩当天的事件，以激发父亲对男孩心智的好奇心。
clinical_signals: 父亲缺乏对儿子心智的好奇
therapeutic_implications: 使用游戏性技巧，如扮演记者
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Sometimes it helps to be playful and ask the dad to be an interviewer for a newspaper and to ask the boy about events of the day prior to him kicking the pots.

atoms.claim: 如果男孩不在场，可以请父亲想象从男孩的视角看问题，以理解他的感受和想法。
clinical_signals: 父亲难以理解儿子的行为
therapeutic_implications: 使用想象技巧，如画图加思想气泡
atoms.evidence_excerpt: If the boy is not in the room, one could still get the dad to imagine life from the boy’s perspective to try and understand what he feels and what was going through his mind at the time.

atoms.claim: 当患者因自身心理状态而盲目时，治疗师明确表达自己的感受或意图（如“我不生你的气”）有助于降低患者的唤醒水平。
therapeutic_implications: 明确表达不生气、不评判，站在患者一边
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It is very helpful for patients if we explicitly state during these times “I am not angry with you”. Alternatively, when they feel overwhelmed with humiliation or shame, it can be helpful for us to state our feelings explicitly, to avoid them feeling we judge them too, by saying: “I am not angry or judging you, I am on your side. All I want to do, is try and understand”.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 表达自身限制以降低威胁
atoms.canonical_name_en: expressing own limitations to reduce threat
atoms.claim: 治疗师对愤怒的青少年说“当你那样尖叫时，我无法思考”，通过表达自己的限制来降低威胁和青少年的唤醒水平，迫使青少年心智化治疗师。
therapeutic_implications: 表达想听和理解，但指出尖叫让自己无法思考
atoms.evidence_excerpt: By communicating that, he stated explicitly his intention of wanting to hear and understand and by saying, “when you scream like that, I cannot think” he presented himself as another human being with his own limitations, therefore reducing the threat and the young person’s arousal levels, and forcing the young person to mentalize him, which kick-started mentalization in the young person.

atoms.claim: 治疗师必须意识到自己犯了错误，并承担责任以修复与患者的连接。
clinical_signals: 患者行为举止突然改变
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应道歉并请求帮助理解错误所在
atoms.evidence_excerpt: We must pick up when we have made an error and then take responsibility for it to try and repair the connection with the patient. If a patient says: “You have not understood me”. We would say: “I am so sorry, I really want to understand you, please help me see where I got it wrong”.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了治疗师在误解患者后应如何回应。

atoms.claim: 当患者被自己的心理状态蒙蔽时，治疗师明确表达自己的感受或意图是有帮助的。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应明确说“我没有生你的气”或“我没有评判你，我站在你这边”
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It is sometimes helpful for our patients if we are explicit with what we feel or what our intentions are, mainly when our patients are a bit blinded by their own mental states or, as described earlier, where the shutters are down. For example, if a patient is very angry, either with the therapist or with themselves, they are often likely to think the therapist is angry too. It is very helpful for patients if we explicitly state during these times “I am not angry with you”. Alternatively, when they feel overwhelmed with humiliation or shame, it can be helpful for us to state our feelings explicitly, to avoid them feeling we judge them too, by saying: “I am not angry or judging you, I am on your side. All I want to do, is try and understand”.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明了在患者情绪强烈时表达治疗师感受的益处。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 降低唤醒以恢复心智化
atoms.claim: 治疗师承认自己对患者的影响，并尝试重新建立联系以恢复心智化。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应承认自己的影响并重新建立联系
atoms.evidence_excerpt: We take full responsibility for the fact that we have an impact upon our patients, and this can sometimes lead to an increase in arousal, and hence compromise the young person’s ability to mentalize. It is important for us to own this and try and re-establish contact with the patient in order to re-instate mentalization.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了治疗师的影响与患者心智化能力的关系。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 通过表达自身局限降低威胁
atoms.canonical_name_en: reducing threat by expressing own limitations
atoms.claim: 治疗师通过表达自己作为人类的局限（如“我无法思考”）来降低威胁和患者的唤醒水平，并促使患者心智化治疗师。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师可以说“我真的很想听和理解你说的话，但如果你这样尖叫，我无法思考”
atoms.evidence_excerpt: By communicating that, he stated explicitly his intention of wanting to hear and understand and by saying, “when you scream like that, I cannot think” he presented himself as another human being with his own limitations, therefore reducing the threat and the young person’s arousal levels, and forcing the young person to mentalize him, which kick-started mentalization in the young person.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了该技术如何降低威胁并启动心智化。

atoms.claim: 在青少年MBT工作中，我们将家庭纳入治疗计划。
therapeutic_implications: 使家庭成员能够支持和搭建家庭环境的发展
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In our work with young people, we involve families in the treatment plan.

atoms.claim: 随着家庭更能心智化，家庭成员在某种程度上成为治疗师，在家庭中支持和搭建心智化。
therapeutic_implications: 家庭在家庭中支持和搭建心智化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: as the family becomes more able to mentalize, family members become in a way therapists themselves who can support and scaffold mentalization at home at times when it breaks down.

atoms.claim: MBT-A通常将个体治疗与MBT-家庭和/或MBT-团体相结合。
therapeutic_implications: 在更密集的项目中，个体治疗与家庭和团体治疗结合；在较不密集的项目中，与家庭治疗结合
atoms.evidence_excerpt: MBT-A is a model in which individual therapy is usually combined with MBT-Family and or MBT-Group.

atoms.claim: 家庭治疗不需要每周进行；有初步临床证据表明六次家庭工作可能足够，每两周一次给家庭更多时间应用所学。
therapeutic_implications: 家庭治疗频率可调整为每两周一次
atoms.evidence_excerpt: There is emerging clinical evidence to suggest that six sessions of family work can be sufficient, and stretching it out to twice a month, gives families more time to apply what they have learned.

atoms.claim: 评估过程不应超过三次会谈，且第一次会谈后家庭和青少年通常希望得到反馈或治疗计划。
therapeutic_implications: 评估应在三次会谈内完成
第一次会谈后提供反馈或治疗计划
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Our view is that it should not be longer than three sessions and our view is also that after the first session, families and young people usually want some form of feedback or clear idea about the treatment plan.

atoms.claim: 如果存在风险问题，需要在第一次会谈中处理，并与青少年和家庭制定危机计划。
therapeutic_implications: 第一次会谈中处理风险问题并制定危机计划
atoms.evidence_excerpt: If there are concerns about risk, this needs to be addressed in the first session too and a crisis plan needs to be developed with the young person and the family.

atoms.claim: 评估阶段通常以讨论个案概念化结束。
therapeutic_implications: 评估阶段结束时讨论个案概念化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The assessment phase is usually concluded with the discussion of the formulation

atoms.claim: 评估阶段通常不超过三次会谈，并在第一次会谈后提供反馈或治疗计划。
therapeutic_implications: 评估应高效，避免超过三次会谈
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Our view is that it should not be longer than three sessions and our view is also that after the first session, families and young people usually want some form of feedback or clear idea about the treatment plan.

atoms.claim: 如果存在风险问题，必须在第一次会谈中处理，并与青少年和家庭共同制定危机计划。
therapeutic_implications: 首次会谈需包含危机计划制定
atoms.evidence_excerpt: If there are concerns about risk, this needs to be addressed in the first session too and a crisis plan needs to be developed with the young person and the family.

atoms.claim: 在MBT-A评估中，临床医生会询问心智化追踪问题，例如“当他那样做时，你觉得他有什么感受？”以了解心智化困难。
therapeutic_implications: 评估中关注心智化困难
atoms.evidence_excerpt: the clinician would pay attention to evidence of good mentalizing or examples of non-mentalizing functioning and hence may ask a few mentalizing tracer questions, such as “when he did that, what do you think he was feeling…”

atoms.claim: 评估结束时，MBT-A临床医生应了解呈现问题与诊断、起草初步个案概念化、描述治疗计划，并在必要时制定清晰的安全或危机计划。
therapeutic_implications: 评估产出包括概念化、治疗计划和危机计划
atoms.evidence_excerpt: At the end of the assessment, the MBT-A clinician would want to be in a position to do the following: • Have an idea of the presenting problems and the diagnosis when this is useful • Draw up a draft formulation of the young person’s difficulties • Describe the treatment plan • Develop a clear safety or crisis plan, when indicated

atoms.claim: 治疗合同是治疗计划的具体描述，明确治疗内容、频率、时长和实际安排，以便青少年和家庭知情同意。
therapeutic_implications: 合同促进知情同意和明确期望
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It is more a description of the treatment plan in a concrete way which makes explicit for the young person and family what the treatment will entail, how often the sessions will be, what is being offered and how long it will last. It makes the practical arrangements clear from the start so that the young person and the family know what they can expect, have a clear understanding of what is offered and can sign up for it willingly, or in other words, consent to participate in it.

atoms.claim: 治疗合同中不设定具体期望，如要求青少年停止自伤等行为。
therapeutic_implications: 避免在合同中设定具体行为改变目标
atoms.evidence_excerpt: We do not bring in concrete expectations that the young person would stop self-harming or anything along such lines.

atoms.claim: 在MBT-A评估中，临床医生希望理解青少年和家庭的心智化困难，关注良好心智化或非心智化功能的证据，并可能提出心智化追踪问题。
therapeutic_implications: 评估中需注意心智化表现
使用心智化追踪问题
atoms.evidence_excerpt: in the MBT-A assessment, the clinician is also hoping to get an understanding of the mentalizing difficulties experienced by the young person and the family, so the clinician would pay attention to evidence of good mentalizing or examples of non-mentalizing functioning and hence may ask a few mentalizing tracer questions
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了MBT-A评估中关注心智化困难和使用追踪问题。

atoms.claim: 治疗合同是对治疗计划的具体描述，明确治疗内容、频率、时长和实际安排，使青少年和家庭能够知情同意。
therapeutic_implications: 提供清晰的治疗计划
促进知情同意
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It is more a description of the treatment plan in a concrete way which makes explicit for the young person and family what the treatment will entail, how often the sessions will be, what is being offered and how long it will last. It makes the practical arrangements clear from the start so that the young person and the family know what they can expect, have a clear understanding of what is offered and can sign up for it willingly, or in other words, consent to participate in it.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了治疗合同的目的和内容。

atoms.claim: MBT-A不支持规定‘如果你自伤，治疗将被终止’的合同。
therapeutic_implications: 不应因自伤终止治疗
需理解自伤背后的感受
contraindications: 以自伤为理由终止治疗
atoms.evidence_excerpt: We do not support contracts that state, ‘if you harm yourself your treatment will be terminated’.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确反对因自伤终止治疗的合同条款。

atoms.claim: 书面概念化对青少年有帮助，他们可以保留并在日后参考，尤其是在感到不知所措时，具体提醒可以支撑他们。
therapeutic_implications: 提供书面概念化
青少年可保留并参考
atoms.evidence_excerpt: it can be very helpful for young people to hold onto it and refer back to it at a later stage, especially at times when they may feel overwhelmed and hence unable to remember the session’s discussion without a concrete reminder to scaffold them.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了书面概念化对青少年的益处。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 家庭与个体概念化的区分
atoms.canonical_name_en: Distinction between family and individual formulation
atoms.claim: 在MBT-A中，个体治疗师常与青少年讨论其个人概念化，不与其他家庭成员分享；家庭治疗中的概念化则更关注家庭互动而非个人。
therapeutic_implications: 个体概念化不共享给家庭
家庭概念化聚焦互动
atoms.evidence_excerpt: As different therapists frequently offer the individual MBT-A work and the MBT family work, the formulation of the young person is often discussed in the young person’s individual therapy and not shared with the rest of the family. In the family sessions, formulations are developed, but those tend to focus more on family interactions and less on one particular individual.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了青少年个体概念化与家庭概念化的区分，属于青少年治疗的适应性安排。

atoms.claim: 不支持包含‘如果你自伤，治疗将终止’条款的合同。
therapeutic_implications: 应将高风险行为纳入危机计划或合同，而非以终止治疗相威胁
atoms.evidence_excerpt: We do not support contracts that state, ‘if you harm yourself your treatment will be terminated’.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确反对此类合同条款。

atoms.claim: 年轻人转向冲动或自毁行为作为应对方式，如果治疗师不理解这一点并在他们最可能恢复旧有应对方式时撤走治疗，就像在他们跌倒时不帮助其重新站起来。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应理解自伤行为背后的应对功能，而非惩罚或终止治疗
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Young people turn to impulsive or self-destructive behaviours as a way of coping and if we do not understand that and pull treatment away when they will most likely turn to their old coping styles. It is like leaving someone when they have fallen and not helping them get back on their feet.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确比喻，强调理解和支持的重要性。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 心智化框架下的风险行为处理
atoms.canonical_name_en: addressing risky behaviors within a mentalizing framework
atoms.claim: 风险行为需要在一个心智化框架内处理，其中治疗师心智化了行为背后可能的感受。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应表达对危险后果的担忧，同时理解这可能是年轻人管理困难感受的唯一方式，并传达希望共同找到其他帮助方式
atoms.evidence_excerpt: These issues need to be addressed in a mentalizing framework where we have mentalized the possible feelings underneath the behaviours.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确要求在心智化框架下处理。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 危机计划中的风险行为讨论
atoms.canonical_name_en: including risky behavior discussions in crisis plan
atoms.claim: 通过心智化视角看待风险行为，将这些讨论纳入危机计划和个案概念化比纳入合同更有意义。
therapeutic_implications: 将风险行为讨论放在危机计划和个案概念化中，而非合同中
atoms.evidence_excerpt: As we see the risky behaviour through a mentalizing lens, it may therefore make more sense to include these discussions in the crisis plan and formulation, rather than in the contract.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确建议纳入危机计划和概念化。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 个案概念化作为心智化过程
atoms.claim: 临床医生完成评估后，能够心智化年轻人及其家庭，以及促使他们寻求专业帮助的问题，这就是草案概念化。
therapeutic_implications: 临床医生应形成对年轻人和家庭的心智化理解，作为概念化草案
atoms.evidence_excerpt: As clinicians complete an assessment, they would be in a position to formulate an understanding of the young person and their family, as well as the issues that brought them to seek professional help. In other words, the clinician would be in a position to mentalize them and see them and the struggle they present with through a mentalizing lens. This is what a draft formulation is.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确将概念化定义为心智化过程。

atoms.claim: 书面概念化对年轻人有帮助，他们可以保留并在以后参考，尤其是在感到不知所措而无法记住讨论内容时。
therapeutic_implications: 提供书面概念化作为具体提醒，帮助年轻人在困难时回顾
atoms.evidence_excerpt: it can be very helpful for young people to hold onto it and refer back to it at a later stage, especially at times when they may feel overwhelmed and hence unable to remember the session’s discussion without a concrete reminder to scaffold them.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确书面概念化的支持作用。

atoms.claim: 个案概念化以类似个人信件的形式呈现给青少年，并作为草稿一起讨论，以确认青少年是否同意，避免被体验为侵入性心智化。
clinical_signals: 青少年可能将治疗师的陈述体验为侵入性心智化
therapeutic_implications: 使用如“是这样吗？”等短语邀请评论，使陈述显得试探性而非事实
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It is presented to the young person as a draft and then discussed together to see if the young person agrees with it. Otherwise, the risk is that it may be experienced as intrusive mentalization, i.e. the therapist telling the young person what they are feeling. Hence, we use phrases in the formulation such as: “is that correct?” Such phrases invite comment from the young person at each stage and read as a tentative statement rather than a fact.

atoms.claim: 在个案概念化中明确表达治疗师的情感（如“看到你对自己如此负面，我感到难过”），将治疗师呈现为有情感的人，帮助青少年更准确地心智化治疗师。
clinical_signals: 青少年以非人化的方式对待自己，并预期治疗师也以同样方式看待他们
therapeutic_implications: 通过明确陈述意图，帮助青少年更准确地心智化治疗师，体现人性
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The reader will also notice comments such as “it makes me feel sad to see how negative you feel about yourself ”. In this way, we explicitly present ourselves as humans with feelings. So often these youngsters relate to themselves in a dehumanising manner and when they do, they anticipate that we view them in the same light. By explicitly stating our intentions, we help them to mentalize us more accurately.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 危机计划的心智化方式
atoms.claim: 安全计划应以心智化术语思考风险，处理潜在感受，理解触发因素，并考虑更安全的替代方案。
clinical_signals: 青少年出现自伤、自杀感受或其他风险行为（如暴力）
therapeutic_implications: 与家庭和青少年共同制定安全计划，讨论潜在感受和触发因素，思考更安全的替代方案
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The safety plan aims to think about the risk in mentalizing terms and to address the underlying feelings as well as have some understanding of the trigger factors and then to think about safer alternatives that can be used.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 青少年危机计划的数字化适应
atoms.canonical_name_en: digital adaptation of crisis planning for adolescents
atoms.claim: 鉴于青少年生活在网络世界而非纸质世界，作者开发了一款移动应用程序作为危机计划讨论的一部分，但应用程序需要个性化且以心智化方式使用。
clinical_signals: 青少年对纸质危机计划反应不佳
therapeutic_implications: 在讨论危机计划时结合使用移动应用程序，但应用程序必须个性化且以心智化方式使用
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Young people live in a cyber world and not a paper world anymore. She, therefore, developed a mobile app that she uses as part of the crisis planning discussion with young people. Given that the app is very general, it will not be helpful if crisis planning is exclusively just the app. It needs to be personalised and mentalized in the way that is mentioned above.

atoms.claim: 危机计划应以心智化术语思考风险，处理潜在感受，理解触发因素，并思考更安全的替代方案。
therapeutic_implications: 与家庭和青少年共同制定安全计划
提供书面计划供青少年和家长带回家参考
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The safety plan aims to think about the risk in mentalizing terms and to address the underlying feelings as well as have some understanding of the trigger factors and then to think about safer alternatives that can be used. The safety plan is drawn up with the family and the young person and our view is that it is best if it can be discussed in the session, but also that it can be provided to the young person and their parents in written format so that they can take it home with them and refer to it at a later stage.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了危机计划的目的和制定方式。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 青少年危机计划数字化
atoms.claim: 青少年生活在网络世界而非纸质世界，因此作者开发了一款移动应用程序作为危机计划讨论的一部分。
therapeutic_implications: 在治疗中讨论并演示应用程序
将个性化心智化危机计划与应用程序结合
contraindications: 仅使用通用应用程序而不进行个性化心智化讨论无效
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Young people live in a cyber world and not a paper world anymore. She, therefore, developed a mobile app that she uses as part of the crisis planning discussion with young people. Given that the app is very general, it will not be helpful if crisis planning is exclusively just the app. It needs to be personalised and mentalized in the way that is mentioned above.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确提到青少年特点及应用程序的使用条件。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 危机计划中的延迟与反思
atoms.canonical_name_en: delay and reflection in crisis plan
atoms.claim: 当青少年有冲动行为时，建议尝试延迟行动10分钟，并利用这10分钟反思触发感受的关系事件。
therapeutic_implications: 帮助青少年理解感受和关系触发因素
促进从不同视角思考解决方案
atoms.evidence_excerpt: When you feel like that again, I would like you to try and stop the action by trying to delay it for 10 minutes. Then use the 10 minutes to try and reflect on what was happening a few moments before you had the bad feeling. That might help you to understand more clearly what it is that you feel as well as what might have happened in a close relationship which may have contributed to the feeling.
atoms.extraction_notes: 危机计划示例中的具体步骤。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 为家长提供单独危机计划
atoms.claim: 作者为家长提供单独的危机计划，以指导并帮助他们在家长角色中发挥作用。
therapeutic_implications: 提供家长指导
支持家长角色
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The author also provides a separate crisis plan for parents to guide them and help them in their role as parents.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确提到为家长提供单独计划。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 应对技能应用程序内容
atoms.claim: 应对技能应用程序包含从DBT借用的痛苦耐受技巧、正念练习、心智化练习、引导冥想和渐进式肌肉放松录音，并可链接青少年自己的平静音乐和美好回忆的图片。
therapeutic_implications: 在治疗中与青少年一起浏览应用程序以理解如何使用
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The COPING SKILLS app is a combination of distress tolerance skills, borrowed from DBT, mindfulness exercises, a mentalization exercise and guided meditation as well as progressive muscle relaxation tapes. It also has a functionality where young people can link it to calming music of their own, and also images and photos which hold good memories for them.
atoms.extraction_notes: 详细描述了应用程序内容。

atoms.claim: 危机计划包括对青少年自伤和风险的基本理解，以及关于如何应对和说什么/做什么的实用建议。
therapeutic_implications: 为父母提供指导
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The crisis plan with the parents includes some basic understanding of self-harm and risk in young people and practical advice on how to behave and what to say/do when young people self-harm.

atoms.claim: 鼓励关于自伤的沟通，允许青少年在感到有风险时告知父母，例如通过预先约定的表情符号。
therapeutic_implications: 促进青少年表达风险
atoms.evidence_excerpt: encourage communication about self-harm and allow your child to tell you when they feel at risk. Young people will find this very hard to do and for some young people it is easier to agree on an emoji that they can send their parents on their phone as a code that they are at risk of harming themselves.

atoms.canonical_name_en: stay with child at higher risk
atoms.claim: 如果青少年风险较高，父母应陪伴他们，确保他们不独处。
therapeutic_implications: 提供持续监护
atoms.evidence_excerpt: If your child is at higher risk, be with them and ensure that they are not on their own.

atoms.claim: 父母应尝试理解青少年自伤前的感受，并帮助他们谈论感受和事件，即使事件涉及父母，也要倾听并验证其感受，而不必持有相同观点。
therapeutic_implications: 促进情感验证
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Just try and understand what your child felt before they wanted to harm themselves and help them to speak about the feelings and the events leading up to the feelings. If the events involved you, listen and try to understand their perspective without becoming defensive. You don’t have to hold the same perspective, but it is important that you validate their feelings.

atoms.claim: 如果青少年有自杀倾向，父母应明确表示自杀不是选项，表达爱意，并提议转移注意力或寻求帮助。
therapeutic_implications: 提供明确界限和支持
atoms.evidence_excerpt: If your child is suicidal, you could say: “Killing yourself is not an option. I love you and do not want you to kill yourself. You are not alone. We will get through this together. I am going to stay here with you to keep you safe. Let’s try and think of something that will help right now. Will distraction help such as going for a walk or watching TV?”

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 危机中父母应避免的行为
atoms.claim: 父母在危机中不应恐慌、责备或惩罚。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Don’ts: • Panic • Blame • Punish

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 危机中父母应做的行为
atoms.claim: 父母在危机中应倾听、理解并让孩子知道他们在那里支持孩子。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Dos: • Listen • Understand • Let them know you are there for them

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 危机中父母应避免责备
atoms.claim: 父母不应责备孩子或自己，而应尝试理解孩子自伤前的感受。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Don’t blame your child and don’t blame yourself. Just try and understand what your child felt before they wanted to harm themselves and help them to speak about the feelings and the events leading up to the feelings.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 危机中父母应验证孩子的感受
atoms.claim: 如果事件涉及父母，父母应倾听并尝试理解孩子的视角而不防御，验证孩子的感受。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: If the events involved you, listen and try to understand their perspective without becoming defensive. You don’t have to hold the same perspective, but it is important that you validate their feelings.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 危机中父母应承认自己的责任
atoms.claim: 如果父母对误解有贡献，应承认错误，目标是恢复连接而非赢得争论。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: If there was a misunderstanding between you which you contributed to, own up to it. You are not here to win battles but to restore the connection between you.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 危机升级时父母应寻求专业帮助
atoms.claim: 如果所有方法都失败，父母应致电诊所或带孩子去急诊。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: If all else fails, call the clinic or if it is after hours, you may have to take your child to the emergency department.

atoms.claim: 在无法提供工作坊或心理教育小组的情况下，可以通过在治疗中融入相关陈述来进行非正式心理教育。
therapeutic_implications: 在初始阶段，通过回应治疗材料中的内容，自然地融入心理教育陈述。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Where workshops or psychoeducation groups are not available or possible, psychoeducation can be done more informally, particularly during the initial sessions, by weaving it into the treatment where relevant.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了非正式心理教育的适用情境和方法。

atoms.claim: 心理教育陈述可以用于激发好奇心，并传达心理状态是不透明的信息。
therapeutic_implications: 使用如“很多时候人们做事情是因为他们内心有感受，如果我们对此好奇，可以帮助我们更好地理解他人”等陈述。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Here are a few examples of psychoeducational statements which could be used in response to material from the session: “You know, many times when people do what they do, it is because they have feelings inside them and if we are curious about that, it can help us to try and make more sense of other people”.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用了心理教育陈述的示例。

atoms.claim: 当出现非心智化时，可以通过指出假设和过度思考来应对。
therapeutic_implications: 使用如“听起来你对X的感受做了假设。当我们对别人的感受做假设时，很容易出错”等陈述。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: We could also address non-mentalizing when it occurs, by saying something like: “It sounds as if you have made an assumption about what X was feeling. You know when we make assumptions about what people feel, we can easily get it wrong - ….”
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了应对非心智化的具体陈述。

atoms.claim: 当过度思考时，可以暂停并提醒自己无法真正看透他人的想法。
therapeutic_implications: 使用如“我们可以暂停一下吗？我想知道你是否开始过度思考了。当我们过度思考时，会对别人的想法做出大量假设，并把这些假设当作事实。”
atoms.evidence_excerpt: “Can we pause for a minute, I was wondering if you are beginning to overthink a bit, and you know when we overthink, we start making massive assumptions about other people’s minds and then we start to treat these assumptions as if they are facts, when they aren’t– we cannot really see into other people’s minds.”
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用了应对过度思考的陈述。

atoms.claim: 焦虑时，头脑可能会失控并做出假设，最好的做法是停下来，询问对方的感受。
therapeutic_implications: 使用如“当我们焦虑时，头脑有时会失控，对别人的想法或感受做出假设。最好的做法是停下来，问问对方在想什么或感受什么。”
atoms.evidence_excerpt: “When we are anxious our minds can sometimes run away with us and make assumptions of what other people are thinking or feeling, but the best thing to do when we catch ourselves making assumptions or overthinking, is to stop, pause and perhaps ask the other person what they are thinking or feeling.”
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用了焦虑时的应对陈述。

atoms.claim: 心理教育工作坊可以全天进行，或分几次进行，通常以小组形式由两名临床医生主持。
therapeutic_implications: 工作坊包括破冰练习、关于青少年大脑的简短教学、电影片段讨论、关系理解、自我伤害理解、暴力理解等环节。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Psychoeducational workshops can be conducted over the course of a whole day or over a couple of sessions. They are usually offered in a group format and best delivered by two clinicians.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了工作坊的时长、形式和人员配置。

atoms.claim: 在理解自我伤害的环节中，使用卡片上的陈述让参与者判断对错，并讨论如何帮助自伤者。
therapeutic_implications: 使用如“自伤是为了引起注意”或“我的孩子自伤时就是有自杀倾向”等陈述，通过讨论来澄清误解。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Understanding self-harm: In our service, instead of giving didactic input on self-harm, we wrote several statements on cards which were handed out to everyone. Participants took turns to read the statements on the card and then they had to say whether they thought the statement was true or false.
atoms.extraction_notes: 描述了自我伤害环节的具体方法。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 非心理化互动处理流程
atoms.claim: 处理非心理化互动的流程是：停止并暂停，表达共情并验证感受，倒回到失去心理化能力的时刻，询问细节，使用验证、共情、阐述和探索来开启心理化，温和地处理非心理化错误。
therapeutic_implications: 倒回到心理化能力丧失的时刻
心理化当时无法被心理化的感受
response_constraints: 温和地处理非心理化错误
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Non-mentalizing action – STOP and PAUSE – expressing empathy and trying to validate what the young person felt at the time, even if this is based on them not mentalizing – then trying to rewind to the moment where the young person lost the ability to mentalize – then asking for detail and using validation, empathy as well as elaboration and exploration to open things up and in the process trying to kick start mentalizing by gently addressing the non-mentalizing errors which may have escalated the emotions or driven the person into impulsive action.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了非心理化互动的处理步骤。

source_anchor.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

supporting_anchors.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

atoms.claim: 治疗师应保持好奇、温暖和不知情的姿态，并积极工作。
therapeutic_implications: 使用支持和共情作为主要技术
在支持共情与情感阐述或挑战之间移动
atoms.evidence_excerpt: we are active in work and convey a stance of curiosity, warmth and not-knowing. Support and empathy are the techniques used most of the time and we move between support and empathy and affect elaboration or challenging most of the time in our attempt to foster basic mentalizing.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了治疗师姿态和常用技术。

source_anchor.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

supporting_anchors.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

atoms.claim: MBT-A的每次治疗内容主要基于年轻人带来的内容，而非预设结构。
therapeutic_implications: 不试图建立不必要的过去联系
response_constraints: 避免因联系过去而否定当下感受
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Unlike structured therapies, MBT-A does not have prescribed structures for each session. The content of the sessions is mostly based on what the person brings to therapy. We do not try to make unnecessary links to the past or past events as this often invalidates the feelings the person has about the here and now.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明MBT-A无预设结构，内容基于来访者带来内容。

source_anchor.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

supporting_anchors.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

atoms.claim: 青少年期的发展任务包括：从强烈依恋父母转向同伴依恋、形成清晰一致的认同、变得独立、管理更复杂的社交和浪漫世界以及教育世界，以及学习管理社交媒体的复杂性。
therapeutic_implications: 帮助青少年完成发展任务
atoms.evidence_excerpt: the period of adolescence has a few well-known tasks associated with it, such as: • Moving from strong parental attachments to attachments in the peer group • Starting to form a clear and coherent identity • Becoming independent • Managing and negotiating a much more complex social and romantic world as well as a much more demanding and challenging educational world, and more recently, an additional important task is also learning to manage the complexities of social media
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确列出青少年发展任务。

source_anchor.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

supporting_anchors.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

atoms.claim: 当年轻人因焦虑和恐惧而回避学校、社交并退缩到房间时，治疗师需要提供发展性支架或帮助他们摆脱回避模式。
therapeutic_implications: 提供发展性支架
帮助摆脱回避模式
response_constraints: 将回避模式理解为非心理化模式
使用STOP和PAUSE，验证感受
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Young people start to avoid school and social situations and withdraw to their rooms, often with the curtains drawn and their only interactions being online. In those situations, we often need to offer developmental scaffolding or help them out of their avoidant patterns.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述回避行为及治疗师干预。

source_anchor.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

supporting_anchors.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

atoms.claim: 青少年发展任务包括从强烈的父母依恋转向同伴依恋、形成清晰连贯的身份认同、变得独立、管理更复杂的社会和浪漫世界以及教育世界，还包括学习管理社交媒体的复杂性。
clinical_signals: 在人际关系中感到不知所措
在社交和教育领域感到失败
therapeutic_implications: 帮助青少年回到适应性的发展轨道
提供发展性支架
帮助克服回避模式
atoms.evidence_excerpt: the period of adolescence has a few well-known tasks associated with it, such as: • Moving from strong parental attachments to attachments in the peer group • Starting to form a clear and coherent identity • Becoming independent • Managing and negotiating a much more complex social and romantic world as well as a much more demanding and challenging educational world, and more recently, an additional important task is also learning to manage the complexities of social media
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确列举了青少年发展任务。

source_anchor.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

supporting_anchors.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

atoms.claim: 当青少年因焦虑和恐惧而回避学校和社会情境时，治疗师需要提供发展性支架或帮助他们摆脱回避模式。
therapeutic_implications: 提供具体支持，如清晰的结构帮助重返学校
与学校和家长合作制定明确计划
必要时提供实际支持，如首次陪同上学
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In those situations, we often need to offer developmental scaffolding or help them out of their avoidant patterns.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确提到需要提供发展性支架。

source_anchor.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

supporting_anchors.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

atoms.claim: 对于因自我否定感而在学业任务面前感到焦虑的青少年，治疗师应STOP和PAUSE，帮助他们不急于回避，而是尝试工作而不逃跑。
clinical_signals: 面对学业任务时感到焦虑
therapeutic_implications: 使用STOP和PAUSE
鼓励逐步尝试
提醒只做眼前的事，不责备不比较
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Our task again is to STOP and PAUSE and help them not to rush into avoidance, but actually, help them to attempt the work and not run away.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了针对学业回避的干预步骤。

source_anchor.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

supporting_anchors.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

atoms.claim: 治疗师有时会使用具体语句，如“只做眼前的事，不要抬头或低头，不要责备或批评自己，也不要与他人比较”，并建议青少年将这句话保存在手机备忘录中，以便恐慌时参考。
therapeutic_implications: 使用具体鼓励语句
建议保存在手机中以便随时查看
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The author sometimes asks young people to put the sentence on their phones in the note section so that they can draw from that when they find themselves panicking.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了使用具体语句并保存到手机的做法。

source_anchor.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

supporting_anchors.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

atoms.claim: 在治疗结束阶段，目标是增加独立性和责任感、巩固稳定性、制定后续计划、理解并处理结束的意义以及关注与丧失相关的情感状态、出院并与合作机构联络。
clinical_signals: 治疗接近结束时情绪下降
therapeutic_implications: 提前计划结束
帮助青少年变得更加独立
预期情绪调节和身份认同更稳定
减少“异己自我”或强烈的自我憎恨
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In the final phase, we are hoping to achieve the following: • Increase independence and responsibility • Consolidate stability • Develop follow-up plans • Understand and process the meaning of the ending and focus on affective states associated with loss • Discharge and liaise with partner organisations
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确列出了结束阶段的目标。

source_anchor.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

supporting_anchors.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 治疗结束时的情绪下降
atoms.canonical_name_en: mood dip at end of therapy
atoms.claim: 在MBT-A研究中，随着治疗接近结束，观察到情绪下降，尽管这种下降在治疗结束后不会持续。
therapeutic_implications: 提前计划结束
注意结束的情感影响
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In our study (Rossouw & Fonagy, 2012), we noticed a dip in mood as therapy approached the end. Although this dip is not maintained after the end of therapy, it is important to bear in mind the emotional impact of the end of therapy.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了治疗结束时的情绪下降现象。

source_anchor.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

supporting_anchors.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

atoms.claim: 治疗师可能需要提供具体支持，例如清晰的结构帮助青少年重返学校，包括与学校和家长合作制定明确计划。
therapeutic_implications: 提供具体支持如陪同上学、使用公共交通等
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Additionally, we often have to provide some concrete support, such as a clear structure to help them back to school. This will involve working with the school and parents to get a clear plan agreed.

source_anchor.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

supporting_anchors.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

atoms.claim: 治疗师的任务是帮助青少年暂停并避免匆忙回避，而是尝试完成任务而不逃跑。
therapeutic_implications: 鼓励逐步尝试任务，不批评不比较
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Our task again is to STOP and PAUSE and help them not to rush into avoidance, but actually, help them to attempt the work and not run away.

source_anchor.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

supporting_anchors.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

atoms.claim: 治疗师可以具体提醒青少年只做眼前的一点任务，不抬头不低头，不责备不比较。
therapeutic_implications: 使用简单具体的语言提醒
建议将句子保存在手机备忘录中
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Sometimes this feels a bit like constantly reminding them – just do a little, like just putting one foot in front of the other – look in front of you and just do what is in front of you - like climbing a mountain – don’t look up and don’t look down, just do what is in front of you and don’t blame or criticise yourself, or compare yourself with others.

source_anchor.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

supporting_anchors.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

atoms.claim: 保留一些备用治疗次数，以便青少年在需要时回来“补充”，这对青少年发展有益。
therapeutic_implications: 允许青少年在需要时返回进行少量治疗
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Other services have an ending date but keep a few sessions “in reserve” in case the young person needs to come back for a “top up”. These arrangements are usually quite useful as it allows for a re-fuelling, as the tasks of adolescence progress.

source_anchor.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

supporting_anchors.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

atoms.claim: 心智化是思考我们自己的想法和感受的能力，也帮助我们理解他人的想法和感受。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Mentalization is the ability to think about our thoughts and feelings. Mentalization also helps us understand other people’s thoughts and feelings.

source_anchor.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

supporting_anchors.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

atoms.claim: 在青少年MBT-A中，逐步减少治疗频率（如从每周一次减至每两周一次，再减至每月一次）并保留备用治疗次数，有助于青少年在青春期任务中“重新充电”。
therapeutic_implications: 逐步减少治疗频率
保留备用治疗次数
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Some services allow a slow ending of sessions, with sessions reducing to fortnightly from weekly for a couple of months and then sessions once a month for a few months. Other services have an ending date but keep a few sessions “in reserve” in case the young person needs to come back for a “top up”. These arrangements are usually quite useful as it allows for a re-fuelling, as the tasks of adolescence progress.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了逐步结束和备用次数的安排及其对青少年的益处。

source_anchor.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase

supporting_anchors.section_title: 4 Bulk of the work – main phase
