therapeutic_implications: 保持非评判性立场
觉察自身转换点
atoms.evidence_excerpt: keeping a mentalizing non-judgmental stance and being aware of his or her own switch point is crucial for successful treatment.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 利用青少年热情建立共同注意
atoms.canonical_name_en: engage with adolescent's passion to establish joint attention

therapeutic_implications: 利用青少年热情
引入游戏元素
创造性方式
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It is recommended to engage with something the adolescent is passionate about, including playful elements and creative ways to establish joint attention (e.g., drawing).
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确建议。

atoms.claim: 在初始阶段，对青少年进行动机访谈，评估最问题行为的利弊，为制定治疗目标奠定基础。
therapeutic_implications: 使用动机访谈
评估利弊
制定治疗目标
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Individually with the adolescent, motivational interviewing (Rollnick & Miller, 1995) is provided to assess the pros and cons to the most problematic behaviour that sets the ground to formulate therapy goals.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 保持心智化非评判立场

therapeutic_implications: 避免因患者挑衅性不感兴趣或焦虑引发行为而导致的共情缺失或拒绝感受的恶性循环
降低脱落风险

therapeutic_implications: 帮助重新建立对核心问题行为之外的心理状态的好奇心
使治疗师能够仔细关注情感焦点和治疗关系
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It is recommended to engage with something the adolescent is passionate about, including playful elements and creative ways to establish joint attention (e.g., drawing).

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 青少年品行障碍治疗中的挑战
atoms.canonical_name_en: challenges in treating adolescents with conduct disorder
atoms.claim: 患有品行障碍的青少年可能在治疗中不开放、显得不感兴趣、否认问题，并难以用语言表达自己。
therapeutic_implications: 可能导致治疗师不耐烦和居高临下行为
可能引发共情缺失或拒绝感受的恶性循环
高脱落风险
atoms.evidence_excerpt: adolescents with CD might not open up in therapy, appear not interested, deny problems and have problems to express themselves in words.

atoms.claim: 采用不知晓姿态，与患者共同探索感受体验的质量，而不由治疗师强加自己的情绪词汇。
therapeutic_implications: 与患者合作探索情绪
避免强加治疗师的情绪词汇
response_constraints: 不要强加自己的情绪词汇
atoms.evidence_excerpt: This is well in-line with the not-knowing stance to explore the quality of experienced feelings together, without the therapist imposing their own words for emotions.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明不知晓姿态与共同探索情绪一致。

atoms.claim: 治疗师通过发展患者的心智化轮廓来理解其心智化困难，并据此设定治疗焦点，以解决僵化模式并激活有效心智化。
clinical_signals: 患者表现出僵化的心智化模式
therapeutic_implications: 评估心智化轮廓
设定治疗焦点以解决僵化模式
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The therapist developed Susan’s Mentalizing profile (Fig. 9.2) to understand her mentalizing difficulties better and accordingly set session foci for contrary moves to resolve rigid patterns and activate aspects of effective mentalizing.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明使用心智化轮廓来理解困难并设定焦点。

atoms.claim: Susan的他人心智化能力中等：她更关心他人的内心世界（如担心父亲），但经常错误地将敌意意图归因于他人（如认为母亲想“惹恼她”）。
clinical_signals: 关心他人但常误判意图
therapeutic_implications: 纠正敌意归因偏差
促进对他人意图的准确理解
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Focusing on others, her mentalizing capacity can be described as medium. She was somewhat more concerned with other people’s inner worlds, e.g., caring for her father, who was not able to withstand quarrels in the family without having severe headaches. However, she often misattributed hostile intentions to others, e.g., she assumed her mother wanted “to annoy her” when her mother pushed her to do something.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述他人心智化中等及敌意归因偏差。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 认知心智化与情感心智化
atoms.claim: Susan的心智化更侧重于认知方面（中等），而非情感方面（低）：她能在一定程度上想象不同视角，但共情性“感受”或感受他人感受的能力严重受损。
clinical_signals: 能想象不同视角但缺乏情感共情
therapeutic_implications: 促进情感心智化
帮助识别和命名情绪
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Her mentalizing was quite focused on cognitive (medium) instead of affective (low) aspects: She could imagine different perspectives to some extent; however, an empathic “feeling with” or feeling what others feel, i.e. affective mentalizing, was severely impaired.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确区分认知与情感心智化水平。

atoms.claim: Susan无法命名情绪，也不了解许多情绪或情感状态（如 defiance）的含义。
therapeutic_implications: 教授情绪词汇
探索情绪含义
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Furthermore, she could not name emotions and did not know the meaning of many emotions or affective states, such as defiance.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明无法命名情绪及不了解情绪含义。

atoms.claim: 苏珊的自我心智化能力较低：她无法用语言描述自己的内心世界，只能做出非常笼统的陈述，例如只想放松。
clinical_signals: 无法用语言描述内心世界
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师需要帮助患者发展自我心智化能力
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Susan’s capacity for mentalizing the Self can be described as low: She had no words for her internal world other than quite general statements as, e.g., just wanting to relax.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接描述自我心智化能力低，并给出具体表现。

atoms.claim: 苏珊的他人心智化能力中等：她更关心他人的内心世界，但经常错误地将敌意意图归因于他人。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师需要帮助患者纠正对他人的错误归因
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Focusing on others, her mentalizing capacity can be described as medium. She was somewhat more concerned with other people’s inner worlds, e.g., caring for her father, who was not able to withstand quarrels in the family without having severe headaches. However, she often misattributed hostile intentions to others, e.g., she assumed her mother wanted “to annoy her” when her mother pushed her to do something.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述他人心智化能力中等，并给出具体例子。

atoms.claim: 苏珊的心智化相当侧重于认知方面（中等），而非情感方面（低）。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师需要促进情感心智化的发展
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Her mentalizing was quite focused on cognitive (medium) instead of affective (low) aspects: She could imagine different perspectives to some extent; however, an empathic “feeling with” or feeling what others feel, i.e. affective mentalizing, was severely impaired.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确区分认知和情感心智化，并指出苏珊的认知心智化中等，情感心智化低。

atoms.claim: 苏珊通过可见的“信号”和证据来审视世界（外部：中等），这让她过于清晰地看到他人的心理状态，而很少考虑他人不可见的思想、感受或意图（内部：低）。
clinical_signals: 很少考虑内部心理状态
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师需要帮助患者发展内部心智化能力
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Susan screened her world for visible “signals” and evidence (external: medium), giving her too clear a view into other people’s mental states, while she barely seemed to consider not visible thoughts, feelings or intentions of others (internal: low).
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述外部心智化中等，内部心智化低。

atoms.claim: 苏珊大多处于内隐心智化状态（中等），其特点是快速、反射性的假设，导致自动关联的（反应）行动。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师需要促进外显心智化的发展
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Susan was mostly in a state of implicit mentalizing (medium), which is characterised by quick and reflexive assumptions leading to automatically associated (re)actions: She assumed an attack whenever someone said or did anything that could be interpreted negatively to her family or friends, and then – almost like a reflex reaction – would physically attack them.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述内隐心智化状态及其行为表现。

atoms.claim: 在MBT-CD中，治疗师应避免控制行为或对患者的行为负责，而是尝试支持能动性并积极站在患者的心理世界一边。
clinical_signals: 患者只有对立回避和身体暴力两种冲突处理方式
自动心智化中无法质疑心理状态或接受新视角
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应聚焦于共同关注的问题，如动机性访谈和谈论非冲突性话题，以首先建立对心理状态的好奇心
response_constraints: 治疗师应避免控制行为
治疗师不应感到对患者的行为负责
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It is an important aspect of the stance in MBT-CD that the therapist refrains from controlling behaviour or feeling responsible for the patient’s actions and instead tries to support agency and actively sides with the patient’s mental world.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述MBT-CD中的治疗立场。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 聚焦自我、情感、内部和外显心智化
atoms.canonical_name_en: focus on self, affective, internal and explicit mentalizing
atoms.claim: 根据苏珊的心智化剖面，治疗师决定在治疗中聚焦于自我、情感、内部和外显心智化。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应针对这些维度进行干预
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Given this profile, the therapist decided to focus on self, affective, internal and explicit mentalizing during the sessions.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接描述治疗师根据心智化剖面设定的治疗焦点。

atoms.claim: 治疗师避免控制行为或对患者的行为感到负责，而是支持能动性并积极站在患者的心理世界一边。
clinical_signals: 患者完全反对任何义务
存在非治疗性家长式互动的风险
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应专注于联合注意问题，如动机性访谈和讨论非冲突话题，以首先建立对心理状态的好奇心。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It is an important aspect of the stance in MBT-CD that the therapist refrains from controlling behaviour or feeling responsible for the patient’s actions and instead tries to support agency and actively sides with the patient’s mental world.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述了MBT-CD中的立场要素。

atoms.claim: 动机性访谈是一种人本主义技术，以非评判和验证的方式探索维持或改变特定行为的动机，与MBT立场契合。
clinical_signals: 患者使用暴力作为冲突解决方法
使用暴力作为冲突解决方式
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师询问改变行为的重要性（1-10分）和改变行为的信心（1-10分），并探索愿望与主观无能之间的差异。
探索改变行为的重要性和信心
讨论改变意愿与主观无能之间的差异
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Motivational Interviewing is a humanistic technique that focuses on the exploration of motives to sustain or change a specific behaviour in a non-judgmental and validating manner, which fits well with the MBT stance.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了动机性访谈及其与MBT的契合。

atoms.claim: 案例表述以信件形式呈现，总结治疗师对患者症状与心智化之间联系的理解，旨在让患者参与讨论可能的治疗焦点，并达成一致。
clinical_signals: 患者不愿在治疗师面前阅读信件
患者表现出烦躁或抗拒
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师介绍信件时说它包含自己的理解，但也表示不确定，以邀请患者讨论。
促进治疗师与患者就后续工作重点达成共识
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The formulation summarises the therapists’ understanding of Susan concerning the link between her symptoms and mentalizing. It serves to engage the patient in a discussion about possible treatment foci, with the aim of therapist and patient reaching an agreement regarding what they want to work on in the subsequent sessions.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了案例表述的目的和形式。

atoms.claim: 患者主要处于隐式心智化状态，特点是快速、反射性的假设导致自动关联的（反应）行动。
clinical_signals: 患者假设任何可能被负面解读的言行都是攻击
几乎像反射一样进行身体攻击
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Susan was mostly in a state of implicit mentalizing (medium), which is characterised by quick and reflexive assumptions leading to automatically associated (re)actions: She assumed an attack whenever someone said or did anything that could be interpreted negatively to her family or friends, and then – almost like a reflex reaction – would physically attack them.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了隐式心智化及其表现。

atoms.claim: 患者依赖外部可见信号和证据，对他人心理状态有过于清晰的看法，而几乎不考虑不可见的想法、感受或意图。
clinical_signals: 患者回答“我怎么知道？！”当被问及他人心理状态时
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师聚焦于内部心智化。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Susan screened her world for visible “signals” and evidence (external: medium), giving her too clear a view into other people’s mental states, while she barely seemed to consider not visible thoughts, feelings or intentions of others (internal: low).
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了外部高、内部低的心智化维度。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 双重检查情感词汇理解
atoms.claim: 每当治疗师引入情感名称时，她会双重检查患者是否理解该词的含义。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应确保患者理解情感词汇，以促进心智化。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Consequently, whenever the therapist introduced a name for an affect, she double-checked if Susan would understand the meaning of the word.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了治疗师的行为。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 动机性访谈用于暴力使用
atoms.claim: 针对青少年，动机性访谈可用于探讨使用暴力作为冲突解决方法的利弊。
clinical_signals: 患者认为暴力是恢复他人尊重的有效方式
患者认为暴力是利他和防御性的
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师探索改变行为的重要性（1-10分）和信心（1-10分），并聚焦于心智化使用暴力的动机。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The first Motivational Interviewing (Rollnick & Miller, 1995) dealt with the pros and cons of using violence as a conflict resolution method.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了针对青少年的动机性访谈应用。

atoms.claim: 治疗师使用“停止、倒回和探索”技术，让苏珊微观切片她与警察和店主的互动。
clinical_signals: 患者快速报告事件，未详细描述
therapeutic_implications: 通过微观切片互动，促进对事件的详细探索
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The therapist slowed down the process by bringing herself back into their present interaction (“This is way too fast for me”) and engaged Susan in the process of micro-slicing the interaction with the police and the store manager using the technique “stop, rewind and explore”.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了技术名称及其应用。

atoms.claim: 治疗师使用“停止并站立”技术，强调苏珊罕见地用言语而非行动成功处理了情况。
clinical_signals: 患者用言语成功处理冲突
therapeutic_implications: 突出患者的成功经验，强化积极行为
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The therapist used the “Stop and stand” technique at this moment to stress that this was a rare occasion that Susan was actually successful with words instead of actions.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了技术及其目的。

atoms.claim: 在MBT-CD中，使用心理化循环来探索焦点行为。
clinical_signals: 治疗师在会话总结中应用心理化循环
therapeutic_implications: 通过心理化循环系统探索焦点行为
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The following session summary illustrates how the mentalizing loop is used to explore the focus behaviour in MBT-CD.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确提及心理化循环用于探索焦点行为。

atoms.claim: 治疗师通过将自己带回当前互动来放慢过程，说“这对我来说太快了”。
therapeutic_implications: 放慢节奏以促进更细致的探索
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The therapist slowed down the process by bringing herself back into their present interaction (“This is way too fast for me”)
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了放慢节奏的技术。

atoms.claim: 治疗师使用“停止、倒带和探索”技术对与警察和店主的互动进行微切片，帮助苏珊探索她的“什么都没做”意味着她没有像姐姐那样吸大麻，但当店主靠得太近时，她让他退后一步。
clinical_signals: 患者声称自己什么都没做
therapeutic_implications: 通过微切片探索患者对事件的解释
帮助患者识别自己实际采取的行动
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The therapist slowed down the process by bringing herself back into their present interaction (“This is way too fast for me”) and engaged Susan in the process of micro-slicing the interaction with the police and the store manager using the technique “stop, rewind and explore”. In doing this, Susan explored that her “doing nothing” meant that she wasn’t smoking pot like her sister, however, when the store manager stepped up “too close” to her sister and told her to stop, Susan told him to take a step back, which he did.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了微切片技术的使用和效果。

atoms.claim: 治疗师使用“停止并站立”技术强调苏珊罕见地通过言语而非行动成功改变了局面。
clinical_signals: 患者成功用言语而非行动解决问题
therapeutic_implications: 突出患者的成功经验
强化言语解决问题的有效性
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The therapist used the “Stop and stand” technique at this moment to stress that this was a rare occasion that Susan was actually successful with words instead of actions.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了“停止并站立”技术的使用。

atoms.claim: 治疗的效果可能是使患者能够在感受、想法和行动之间使用心理化缓冲。
clinical_signals: 患者情绪强烈时仍能进行反思
therapeutic_implications: 促进患者在情绪激动时仍能进行反思
增强感受、想法和行动之间的缓冲
atoms.evidence_excerpt: This might have been an effect of therapy: enabling her to use a mentalizing buffer between feelings, thoughts and actions.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确提到心理化缓冲作为治疗效果。

atoms.claim: 通过探索和微切片事件，最终可以在之前无法心理化的情境中建立心理化，从而可能带来新的视角。
clinical_signals: 患者之前无法在特定情境中心理化
therapeutic_implications: 通过微切片建立心理化
促进新的视角
atoms.evidence_excerpt: By exploring and micro-slicing such events, eventually mentalizing can be established in situations where no mentalizing was possible before, which may lead to a new perspective.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了探索和微切片事件的效果。

atoms.claim: 通过探索和微切片事件，强化了患者对其行动的能动性和责任。
clinical_signals: 患者对自己的行动缺乏责任意识
therapeutic_implications: 增强患者对自身行动的能动性和责任感
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Furthermore, agency and responsibility for her actions are reinforced.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确提到强化能动性和责任。

atoms.claim: 治疗师引入狮子攻击的隐喻来描述苏珊的转换点和反射性反应。
clinical_signals: 患者出现非心理化反应
therapeutic_implications: 通过隐喻帮助患者理解自己的反应模式
atoms.evidence_excerpt: She introduced the metaphor of a lion attack to describe Susan’s switch point and reflex reactions.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了引入隐喻。

atoms.claim: 通过探索和微切片事件，最终可以在之前无法进行心智化的情境中建立心智化，并可能带来新的视角。
therapeutic_implications: 逐步建立心智化能力
促进新视角的形成
atoms.evidence_excerpt: By exploring and micro-slicing such events, eventually mentalizing can be established in situations where no mentalizing was possible before, which may lead to a new perspective.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确描述了微切片的作用。

atoms.claim: 治疗师采用不知姿态，对苏珊的内在状态表示好奇，并质疑“只想睡觉”是否完全捕捉了她的感受。
therapeutic_implications: 探索更深层的内在状态
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Th: But that’s why I am curious what is going on inside of you in that moment, because I think “just wanting to sleep” doesn’t quite capture it. (not-knowing stance)
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确标注了不知姿态。

atoms.claim: 治疗可能使患者能够在感受、想法和行动之间使用心智化缓冲。
therapeutic_implications: 促进反思而非行动
atoms.evidence_excerpt: This might have been an effect of therapy: enabling her to use a mentalizing buffer between feelings, thoughts and actions.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文用“might have been”表示推测，但明确描述了心智化缓冲的概念。

atoms.claim: 家庭会议是MBT-CD的重要组成部分，因为需要在家庭内部建立心智化沟通，以开启治疗之外的社会学习良性循环。
therapeutic_implications: 建立心智化沟通
促进社会学习
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Family sessions are an essential part of MBT-CD because there is a need to establish a mentalizing communication within the family to open a virtuous cycle of social learning outside of therapy.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确说明了家庭会议的目的。

atoms.claim: 通过探索和微切片事件，强化了患者对其行为的能动性和责任感。
therapeutic_implications: 增强自我效能感
促进责任承担
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Furthermore, agency and responsibility for her actions are reinforced.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确陈述了强化能动性和责任感。

atoms.claim: 治疗师引入狮子攻击的隐喻来描述苏珊的转换点和反射性反应。
therapeutic_implications: 帮助理解非心智化模式
atoms.evidence_excerpt: She introduced the metaphor of a lion attack to describe Susan’s switch point and reflex reactions.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确描述了隐喻的使用。

atoms.claim: 治疗师采用好奇且不知情的立场，例如说“我很好奇你内心发生了什么，因为我觉得‘只是想睡觉’并不完全准确”。
therapeutic_implications: 促进患者探索内心状态
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Th: But that’s why I am curious what is going on inside of you in that moment, because I think “just wanting to sleep” doesn’t quite capture it. (not-knowing stance)
atoms.extraction_notes: 治疗师明确使用好奇且不知情的立场来探索患者内心状态。

atoms.claim: 治疗师直接指出患者可能无法清晰思考，例如说“我不知道你此刻是否能清晰思考”。
clinical_signals: 患者表现出僵化、绝对化的言语
therapeutic_implications: 帮助患者意识到自己的非心智化状态
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Th: Mh… But I think what might be going inside of you is you interpreting the situation a certain way. And I don’t know if you can think clearly in this moment. (addressing non-mentalizing)
atoms.extraction_notes: 治疗师明确指出患者可能处于非心智化状态。

atoms.claim: 治疗师通过比喻（如狮子）验证并正常化患者的反应，例如说“当有狮子时，每个人都会那样反应”。
clinical_signals: 患者表现出强烈的情绪反应
therapeutic_implications: 减少患者的防御，促进心智化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Th: Yes, but then I get why you are saying these things in such an absolute way, everybody would react like that: when there is a lion around, you need to act fast, otherwise you’re lost. But of course, you’re also telling me now, that there is no lion, just your mother. (validating and normalising).
atoms.extraction_notes: 治疗师明确使用验证与正常化技术。

atoms.claim: 心智化立场在与高度受损和不信任的青少年工作中似乎富有成效，有助于重建对心理状态的好奇和信任。
clinical_signals: 高度受损、不信任的青少年
therapeutic_implications: 重建信任和好奇心，改变反社会认知和行为
atoms.evidence_excerpt: So far, the mentalizing stance seems fruitful in work with these highly impaired and distrustful adolescents to re-establish trust and curiosity in mental states and by this change antisocial cognitions and behaviour.
atoms.extraction_notes: 文本明确说明心智化立场对这类青少年的效果。

atoms.claim: 治疗师通过将青少年的极端反应比作面对狮子时的本能反应，来验证和正常化其行为。
clinical_signals: 青少年以绝对化的方式说话
therapeutic_implications: 帮助青少年理解自己的反应是正常的，从而降低防御
atoms.evidence_excerpt: But of course, you’re also telling me now, that there is no lion, just your mother. (validating and normalising).
atoms.extraction_notes: 治疗师在对话中明确使用了验证和正常化的技术。

atoms.claim: 治疗师指出青少年可能以某种方式解释情境，并质疑其当前清晰思考的能力，以处理非心智化状态。
clinical_signals: 青少年表现出非心智化
therapeutic_implications: 引导青少年反思自己的思维过程
atoms.evidence_excerpt: But I think what might be going inside of you is you interpreting the situation a certain way. And I don’t know if you can think clearly in this moment. (addressing non-mentalizing)
atoms.extraction_notes: 治疗师明确标记为处理非心智化。

atoms.claim: 治疗师使用'母亲像狮子'的隐喻来帮助青少年理解其极端反应。
clinical_signals: 青少年以戏剧化的方式说话
therapeutic_implications: 通过隐喻使青少年的体验更具体、可理解
atoms.evidence_excerpt: As if your mother was a lion about to eat your sister and you’re there to protect her from that
atoms.extraction_notes: 治疗师使用隐喻来探索青少年的内在体验。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 心智化立场对高度受损青少年的效果
atoms.canonical_name_en: mentalizing stance for highly impaired adolescents
atoms.claim: 心智化立场在与高度受损和不信任的青少年工作中似乎富有成效，有助于重建对心理状态的好奇心并改变反社会认知和行为。
therapeutic_implications: 重建信任和好奇心
改变反社会认知和行为
atoms.evidence_excerpt: So far, the mentalizing stance seems fruitful in work with these highly impaired and distrustful adolescents to re-establish trust and curiosity in mental states and by this change antisocial cognitions and behaviour.
atoms.extraction_notes: 文本使用'seems fruitful'，表明是初步观察而非确定结论。

atoms.claim: 严重忽视和混乱的依恋环境会损害心智化能力。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗需关注心智化能力的修复
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Throughout his childhood, his emotional experience was not recognised or contained but despised. This state of affairs laid the groundwork for damaged and disorganised thought processes, his capacity to modulate emotions and his mentalizing abilities seemed significantly impaired
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确将忽视与心智化受损联系起来。

atoms.claim: 无法言说的痛苦只能通过目的论模式的行为外化来宣泄。
therapeutic_implications: 帮助患者将行为转化为可心智化的体验
atoms.evidence_excerpt: unnamed pain that could only be evacuated in a teleological mode through acting out.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确将无法命名的痛苦与目的论模式的行为外化联系起来。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 适应性心智化整合治疗
atoms.claim: AMBIT模型是基于心智化的整合治疗，用于青少年心理健康外展团队。
therapeutic_implications: 采用外展团队模式
atoms.evidence_excerpt: ECID, a mental health outreach team for adolescents of the Vidal and Barraquer Foundation in Barcelona, based on the Adaptive Mentalization-based Integrative Treatment (AMBIT, Bevington, Fuggle, Cracknell, & Fonagy, 2017; Bevington, Fuggle, & Fonagy, 2015; Bevington, Fuggle, Fonagy, Target, & Asen, 2012).
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确将AMBIT描述为基于心智化的整合治疗，并用于青少年外展团队。

atoms.claim: 高风险心理状态指经历早期、低水平精神病迹象的青少年。
clinical_signals: 短暂或轻度精神病症状
短暂间歇性精神病症状
therapeutic_implications: 需要早期识别和干预
atoms.evidence_excerpt: when I speak about at-risk mental states (ARMS), I am referring to the term used by mental health professionals to describe young people who are experiencing early, low-level signs of psychosis.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确定义了高风险心理状态。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 适应性心智化整合治疗
atoms.claim: AMBIT是一种基于心智化的模型，适用于有多重复杂困难的青少年，通过四个层面（青少年及其家庭、团队、网络、学习立场）提供工具来刺激心智化。
therapeutic_implications: 拓宽干预领域，提供刺激心智化的工具
atoms.evidence_excerpt: AMBIT is a mentalization-based model for teams working with young people who have multiple and complex difficulties. AMBIT broadens the field of intervention by providing tools to stimulate mentalizing, applying principles and practices based on four different levels: working with young people and their families, working with teams, working with our network and supporting teams to adopt a learning position regarding our own practice.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了AMBIT的定义和四个层面。

atoms.claim: 高风险青少年常处于认识论超警觉或不信任状态，这与他们可理解的非求助态度相关。
therapeutic_implications: 需要调整治疗立场以建立信任
atoms.evidence_excerpt: They live trapped in states of epistemic hypervigilance or epistemic mistrust, something that is related to their understandable non-help-seeking attitude.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了认识论超警觉/不信任与非求助态度的关联。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 不良童年经历与青少年精神病理
atoms.canonical_name_en: adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) and adolescent psychopathology
atoms.claim: 不良童年经历（ACEs）在患有严重精神障碍的青少年中极为常见，且这些青少年的父母也常有自己的ACEs。
therapeutic_implications: 需要评估ACEs并理解其对发展的影响
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Data collected in recent years on the work with this group of young people (Dangerfield, 2012 & 2017) supports the existing evidence that demonstrates the relationship between suffering ACEs and a greater psychopathological risk, as well as the relationship between ACEs of adolescents with the fact that their parents also suffered ACEs in their own childhood.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了ACEs与青少年精神病理风险的关系，以及代际传递。

atoms.claim: 不一致、不可预测和忽视的照料会导致青少年情绪调节困难和心智化能力缺陷。
therapeutic_implications: 理解症状为发展失败，设计治疗过程时需考虑
atoms.evidence_excerpt: if we consider this situation through the understanding of the inconsistent, unpredictable and neglectful caregiving – including family, school and other care systems–, Andrew’s difficulties in modulating his emotional life and his very deficient relational and mentalizing skills can be understood as failures in his developmental process
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了照料缺陷与心智化能力缺陷的关系。

atoms.claim: 干预的总体目标是为青少年及其周围系统提供不同的关系模型，以促进不同情感体验在青少年关系环境中的泛化。
therapeutic_implications: 关注关系环境的泛化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The overall aim of this intervention is to provide a different model of relationship for both the adolescent and the systems around them, in order to facilitate a generalisation of a different emotional experience in the context of the young person’s relational environment – family, peers and others – as the condition that determines the therapeutic effect of the intervention.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了干预的泛化目标。

atoms.claim: 依恋与心智化之间的联系是明确的，依恋情境为培养心智化提供了理想条件。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: “the link between attachment and mentalizing is clear” and that “attachment contexts provide the ideal conditions for fostering mentalizing”
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用原文，强调依恋与心智化的关系。

atoms.claim: 处于风险精神状态（ARMS）的青少年常陷入认识论过度警觉或认识论不信任的状态，这与他们可以理解的不寻求帮助的态度有关。
therapeutic_implications: scaffolding the treatment by modifying the approach to facilitate a secure base built on epistemic trust
atoms.evidence_excerpt: They live trapped in states of epistemic hypervigilance or epistemic mistrust, something that is related to their understandable non-help-seeking attitude.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接描述ARMS青少年的认识论状态。

atoms.claim: 对于有早期依恋缺陷的青少年，需要一种更积极的治疗态度来建立基本信任，而经典精神分析的中立和疏远立场是失败的。
clinical_signals: early deficits of having been held in mind predictably and consistently
therapeutic_implications: a more active therapeutic attitude is needed in order to establish basic trust
contraindications: the more neutral and distant position predicated on a classical psychodynamic stance fails
atoms.evidence_excerpt: A more active therapeutic attitude is needed in order to establish basic trust in the relationship with young people who had such early deficits of having been held in mind predictably and consistently.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确提到需要更积极的治疗态度，并指出经典立场失败。

atoms.claim: 对于有早期依恋缺陷的青少年，需要更积极的治疗态度来建立基本信任，因为经典精神分析的中立和疏远立场是失败的。
clinical_signals: early deficits of having been held in mind predictably and consistently
therapeutic_implications: a more active therapeutic attitude is needed in order to establish basic trust
contraindications: the more neutral and distant position predicated on a classical psychodynamic stance fails
atoms.evidence_excerpt: A more active therapeutic attitude is needed in order to establish basic trust in the relationship with young people who had such early deficits of having been held in mind predictably and consistently.
atoms.extraction_notes: 与第3条原子类似，但侧重治疗立场。

atoms.claim: 与暴露于毒性应激的青少年工作时，需要处理他们强烈的非心智化焦虑和受损的情绪领域，这是一种非常强烈、无言的痛苦，主导着他们的心理生活。
therapeutic_implications: taking care of their intense non-mentalized anxieties and damaged emotional sphere
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Working with young people who have been exposed to toxic stress is a tough and complex task, especially for what it means in having to take care of their intense non-mentalized anxieties and damaged emotional sphere: a very intense, wordless suffering that predominates in their psychic life.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接描述非心智化焦虑和痛苦。

atoms.claim: 当照顾者被自身痛苦淹没并以敌意或恐惧回应儿童的不适时，儿童可能内化这种关系体验，形成异己自我。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In a situation of a carer who is overwhelmed by their own suffering and responds in a hostile or fearful way to the child’s discomfort, we could imagine the young child’s experience could be described as follows: “If my carer misperceives my internal state, if they get scared or angry about my discomfort, what I will see and experience is the fear or anger in the other. So, the experience that I internalise is the experience that my discomfort scares or annoys the other whom I desperately need, which leads to the internal experience that I am fearful or I make the other angry, when what is really happening to me is that I am alone and terrified”.
atoms.extraction_notes: 通过描述性语言说明异己自我的形成过程。

atoms.claim: 异己自我指的是照顾者基于错误归因对儿童的表征，这促使儿童内化失调的自我表征。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: This concept of alien self refers to the process in which the caregiver’s representations of the child are based on erroneous attributions, something that will promote the child’s internalisation of misadjusted representations of themselves.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接定义异己自我。

atoms.claim: 对于早期缺乏可预测和一致被心智化体验的青少年，需要更主动的治疗态度以建立基本信任。
therapeutic_implications: 需要更主动的治疗态度
atoms.evidence_excerpt: A more active therapeutic attitude is needed in order to establish basic trust in the relationship with young people who had such early deficits of having been held in mind predictably and consistently.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确针对青少年群体提出更主动的治疗态度。

atoms.claim: 对于暴露于毒性压力的青少年，经典精神分析的中立和疏远立场是无效的，需要发展性视角。
therapeutic_implications: 需要发展性视角
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In this relational context, the more neutral and distant position predicated on a classical psychodynamic stance fails and there is a need for a developmentally informed lens.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明经典立场失败，需要发展性视角。

atoms.claim: 心智化能力很容易被压倒，且从不完全稳定、一致或单一维度。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Mentalizing is a capacity that is very easily overwhelmed and is never entirely stable, consistent or one-dimensional (Fonagy & Allison, 2011).
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述心智化的特性。

atoms.claim: 依恋与心智化之间的联系是清晰的，依恋情境为促进心智化提供了理想条件。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: “the link between attachment and mentalizing is clear” and that “attachment contexts provide the ideal conditions for fostering mentalizing” (Fonagy, Lorenzini, Campbell, & Luyten, 2014).
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用原文。

atoms.claim: 异己自我是指照顾者对儿童的错误归因被儿童内化，形成一种自我憎恨、自我批评的内部体验，阻碍心智化发展。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗需关注异己自我对心智化的阻碍
atoms.evidence_excerpt: This concept of alien self refers to the process in which the caregiver’s representations of the child are based on erroneous attributions, something that will promote the child’s internalisation of misadjusted representations of themselves.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了异己自我的定义和形成过程。

atoms.claim: 心智化是一种容易被压垮的能力，永远不完全稳定、一致或一维。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗需支持心智化恢复
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Mentalizing is a capacity that is very easily overwhelmed and is never entirely stable, consistent or one-dimensional (Fonagy & Allison, 2011).
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用原文定义。

atoms.claim: 在青春期，心智化能力下降直接导致理解他人行为困难、理解自身感受困难、焦虑增加、威胁感增加、丧失感、愤怒和绝望。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗需针对青少年心智化丧失的特定表现
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In adolescence, diminished mentalizing capacities lead directly to greater difficulty in finding meaning in the behaviour of others, a greater difficulty in understanding one’s own feelings, greater anxiety, increased feeling of threat, loss, anger and despair.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确提及青春期。

atoms.claim: 当心智化丧失时，青少年可能大量使用心理等价模式，产生高度威胁性的体验。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗需帮助青少年区分内在与外在现实
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Any mechanism that makes fragmentation stop is valuable for the adolescent, such as moving towards massive projections on external reality, the massive use of psychic equivalence that generates a highly threatening experience.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确提及青少年使用心理等价模式。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 异己自我与心智化阻碍
atoms.claim: 异己自我阻碍心智化的发展，是理解高危青少年困难的核心要素。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗需处理异己自我以促进心智化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It follows that the “alien self” prevents the development of mentalizing (Rossouw & Fonagy, 2012) and is an important element to understand central aspects of the difficulties of at-risk adolescents.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确提及异己自我阻碍心智化。

atoms.claim: 异己自我的内在体验类似于内在折磨者：持续的自我批评、自我厌恶、缺乏内在认可和对失败的预期。
therapeutic_implications: 需要帮助青少年识别和整合异己自我部分
atoms.evidence_excerpt: the internal experience of the alien self is similar to the experience of an internal tormentor: constant self-criticism, self-loathing, absence of internal validation and expectation of failure.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述异己自我的体验特征。

atoms.claim: 通过异己自我的投射透镜，外部世界可能被感知为潜在的敌意、羞辱和迫害。
therapeutic_implications: 需要帮助青少年检验对外部世界的感知
atoms.evidence_excerpt: through the projected lenses of the “alien self”, the external world can be perceived as potentially hostile, humiliating and persecuting
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述异己自我对外部世界感知的影响。

atoms.claim: 异己自我阻碍心智化的发展。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗需关注异己自我对心智化的阻碍
atoms.evidence_excerpt: the “alien self” prevents the development of mentalizing
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述异己自我阻碍心智化。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 青少年心智化能力下降
atoms.claim: 在青春期，心智化能力下降直接导致理解他人行为意义更困难、理解自身感受更困难、焦虑增加、威胁感增加、丧失感、愤怒和绝望增加。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗需增强心智化能力以减轻这些症状
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In adolescence, diminished mentalizing capacities lead directly to greater difficulty in finding meaning in the behaviour of others, a greater difficulty in understanding one’s own feelings, greater anxiety, increased feeling of threat, loss, anger and despair.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确提及青春期心智化能力下降的后果。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 青少年自我仇恨与破坏行为
atoms.claim: 感到糟糕、感到从内部被摧毁是强烈痛苦的来源，也是自毁和异毁行为的高风险因素。
therapeutic_implications: 需要处理这种内在痛苦以降低风险
atoms.evidence_excerpt: one of the feelings that is the source of intense suffering and a greater risk of both self-destructive and hetero-destructive actions is feeling bad, feeling destroyed from within.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述这种感受与风险的关系。

atoms.claim: 当心智化丧失时，会出现碎片感、连贯性丧失和对自己生活的能动感丧失。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗需恢复心智化以重建连贯性和能动感
atoms.evidence_excerpt: When mentalizing is lost there is a feeling of fragmentation, loss of coherence and loss of the feeling of agency over one’s life.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述心智化丧失的体验。

atoms.claim: 暴力可以被理解为对抗灾难性焦虑的盾牌，是一种重新获得对灾难性体验控制的幻觉，而不仅仅是无法以其他方式处理的不适的排出。
therapeutic_implications: 需要理解暴力的防御功能，而非仅视为行为问题
atoms.evidence_excerpt: This situation stimulates violent actions, a violence that can be understood as a shield against these catastrophic anxieties, as a kind of illusion of regaining control over catastrophic experiences and not only as an evacuation of discomfort that cannot be processed in another way.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述暴力的防御功能。

atoms.claim: 当一个人没有心智化时，我们不应强迫他们心智化，因为他们无法倾听我们。
therapeutic_implications: 表明我们站在他们一边
通过言语和非言语方式验证他们的情绪状态
表明我们与他们同在并支持他们
不要用心智化来应对非心智化
表明支持并验证情绪状态
response_constraints: 不能以心智化来应对非心智化
避免直接要求心智化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: When someone is not mentalizing, we should not force them to mentalize, because they cannot listen to us. We can’t address non-mentalizing with mentalizing.

atoms.claim: 在情绪失调时，积极尝试将注意力转移到冲突较少的领域，以降低破坏性行为的风险。
therapeutic_implications: 主动转移注意力焦点
将患者从触发情绪风暴和失调的源头移开
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In situations of emotional dysregulation like this moment with Andrew, it is important to find ways to stop and actively try to focus on less conflictive areas to diminish the risk of destructive behaviours.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 通过共同注意和情感调节建立认知信任
atoms.canonical_name_en: build epistemic trust through joint attention and affect regulation
atoms.claim: 通过共同注意和情感调节建立认知信任，是帮助重新建立心智化过程的第一步。
therapeutic_implications: 通过共同注意和情感调节建立认知信任
atoms.evidence_excerpt: This has to do with the idea of building epistemic trust through joint attention and affect regulation (Midgley, Ensink, Lindqvist, Malberg, & Muller, 2017), as the first step in the process of helping re-establish mentalizing.

atoms.claim: 在非心智化时，治疗师有主动角色，尤其是在已知的青少年或家庭模式中。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师主动中断非心智化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: This technical aspect is also connected to interrupting non-mentalizing. The therapist has an active role here, especially if it is a known pattern of the young person or family.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 心智化姿态的四条稳固腿
atoms.canonical_name_en: four sturdy legs of the mentalizing stance
atoms.claim: 心智化姿态定义为一张有四条稳固腿的桌子，支撑和促进治疗过程：明确的好奇心、终止非心智化、保持心智化不同维度之间的平衡、突出患者心智化的时刻。
therapeutic_implications: 明确的好奇心
终止非心智化
保持心智化维度平衡
突出心智化时刻
atoms.evidence_excerpt: I will introduce some technical aspects of the mentalizing stance defined as a table with four sturdy legs that support and facilitate the therapeutic process. These are: curiosity made explicit, terminating non-mentalizing, holding the balance between the different dimensions of mentalizing – as described in previous chapters – and highlighting the moments in which the patient mentalizes.

atoms.claim: 明确的好奇心是心智化姿态的支柱之一，因为对于青少年群体，假装知道他们的感受是最糟糕的。
therapeutic_implications: 表达对青少年心理状态的好奇
保持谦逊和不知的姿态
response_constraints: 不要假装知道青少年的感受
检查所说内容是否与青少年相关
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Curiosity made explicit is another of the legs of the mentalizing stance, because, when working with this group of adolescents, there is nothing worse than pretending that we know what it is to be in their shoes.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述，针对青少年群体。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 通过感官层面恢复心智化
atoms.claim: 在情绪风暴后，可以通过共享的感官体验（如炎热、蚊子）来刺激心智化，先展示自己的思维过程，再邀请青少年心智化。
therapeutic_implications: 从感官层面开始
先表达自己的感受
邀请青少年分享体验
response_constraints: 避免直接讨论核心冲突
atoms.evidence_excerpt: After a while, I try to stimulate mentalizing in another area that I think will be much more tolerable, and I opt for the sensory level we are both sharing, mentioning how hot it still is, and appreciating the shade.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述，用于青少年。

atoms.claim: 当青少年情绪失调时，治疗师应通过言语和非言语方式验证其情绪状态，表明支持并陪伴。
therapeutic_implications: 言语和非言语验证
表明陪伴和可用性
response_constraints: 不要试图立即解决问题
atoms.evidence_excerpt: we must indicate that we are by their side, validate their emotional state by both verbal and non-verbal means, showing that we are with them and that we support them.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述，适用于青少年。

atoms.claim: 治疗师绝不应在未检查青少年是否认为所说内容与他们相关的情况下，对他们说任何话。
therapeutic_implications: 在陈述后询问青少年的看法
response_constraints: 不要假设相关性
atoms.evidence_excerpt: We should never say anything to an adolescent without checking whether they believe that what we have told them is relevant to them at that time or not.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述，针对青少年。

atoms.claim: 好奇明确化是心智化立场的支柱之一，因为与青少年工作时，假装知道他们的感受是最糟糕的。
clinical_signals: 青少年表现出愤怒或绝望
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应表达自己的思考过程，并明确对青少年心理状态的好奇
response_constraints: 避免假装知道青少年的感受
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Curiosity made explicit is another of the legs of the mentalizing stance, because, when working with this group of adolescents, there is nothing worse than pretending that we know what it is to be in their shoes.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述好奇明确化是心智化立场的一部分，并指出与青少年工作时假装知道其感受是最糟糕的。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 从感觉层面开始心智化
atoms.claim: 对于高风险青少年，应从最原始的感觉层面开始心智化，即心智化与治疗师共享的新情感体验。
clinical_signals: 青少年被情绪淹没，无法心智化
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应注意到并命名当前情境，从感觉层面刺激心智化
response_constraints: 给予时间，从心理发展过程停滞的地方开始
atoms.evidence_excerpt: For this reason, what we consider as the main goal is the need to give ourselves time to try to develop mentalizing in areas where it can be more tolerable. This can be achieved more easily if we start where their psychic developmental process was detained, starting from the most primitive level: mentalizing the sensory level.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确建议从感觉层面开始心智化，作为处理高风险青少年的策略。

atoms.claim: 治疗师应干预以验证并检查自己对青少年情感体验的理解。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应验证并检查自己的理解
atoms.evidence_excerpt: I intervene validating and checking what I am understanding.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述治疗师验证并检查理解。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 青少年心智化工作的核心概念：认识论信任
atoms.claim: 认识论信任是理解治疗工作的基本概念，在青少年心智化治疗中至关重要。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应促进认识论信任
atoms.evidence_excerpt: A fundamental concept to understand therapeutic work is epistemic trust (Fonagy & Allison, 2014), described in detail in other chapters of this book.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确提及认识论信任是理解治疗工作的基本概念。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 从感觉层面开始心智化
atoms.claim: 如果从心理发展过程停滞的地方开始，即从最原始的感觉层面开始心智化，更容易发展心智化。
clinical_signals: 患者处于被情绪淹没、完全无法心智化的状态
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师需注意并命名正在发生的事情，以刺激从该发展水平的心智化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: This can be achieved more easily if we start where their psychic developmental process was detained, starting from the most primitive level: mentalizing the sensory level.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确说明从最原始的感觉层面开始更容易发展心智化。

atoms.claim: 心智化情感是情感调节过程中的一个重要技术立场，旨在促进对情感的重新评估，而不仅仅是调节。
clinical_signals: 患者能够发展出刚刚描述的情绪
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师促进对情感体验的反思——识别、加工和表达情感——以发展出患者能够表达的新意义
atoms.evidence_excerpt: We can refer to the concept of mentalized affectivity (Jurist, 2005), as an important one that underpins a technical stance in the process of affect regulation where we try to facilitate a revaluing of affects, and not just modulating (Fonagy, Gergely, Jurist, & Target, 2002).
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确引用心智化情感概念，并说明其技术立场。

atoms.claim: 治疗师通过验证和检查自己的理解来干预。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师验证并检查自己是否理解正确
atoms.evidence_excerpt: I intervene validating and checking what I am understanding.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确描述治疗师验证并检查理解。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 帮助患者理解他人情绪反应的原因
atoms.canonical_name_en: helping patient understand reasons for others' emotional reactions
atoms.claim: 治疗师帮助患者理解他人为何因患者的话语而生气。
clinical_signals: 患者对他人情绪反应感到困惑
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师询问患者是否能理解他人为何生气
atoms.evidence_excerpt: T: Right, so she got angry. But, can you understand why she got angry over what you said?
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文中治疗师直接询问患者是否能理解他人为何生气。

atoms.claim: 当患者表现出对治疗师想法的真诚好奇时，治疗师可以示范如何以不同方式表达相同信息。
clinical_signals: 患者对治疗师的想法表现出真诚好奇
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师直接示范一种更温和的表达方式
atoms.evidence_excerpt: I think that Andrew is showing honest curiosity about what I might have in mind, he is interested in my way of expressing this. So I think it is important to respond.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文中治疗师认为患者表现出真诚好奇，因此认为回应很重要，并随后示范了表达方式。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 突出和重视有效的心智化
atoms.claim: 治疗师通过关注此时此地，检测、突出和重视有效的心智化，来强化心智化立场。
clinical_signals: 患者表现出有效的心智化
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应明确肯定患者的心智化表现，并对比其之前非心智化的状态
atoms.evidence_excerpt: We do it by focusing on the here and now, detecting, highlighting and valuing effective mentalizing: “I really like the way of thinking that you are being capable of showing right now. Look at how different it is from the way you were thinking just five minutes ago when you seemed so certain about what you were saying about such a person… instead, now you are wondering about how that person might feel when you do something like what you had done. Do you see the difference?”.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确描述了治疗师通过聚焦此时此地、检测、突出和重视有效心智化的干预方式。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 在患者表现出好奇时提供示范
atoms.canonical_name_en: providing a model when the patient shows curiosity
atoms.claim: 当患者对治疗师的想法表现出真诚的好奇时，治疗师直接回应并提供示范是重要的。
clinical_signals: 患者表现出对治疗师表达方式的真诚好奇
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师可以示范如何以不伤害他人的方式表达相同信息
atoms.evidence_excerpt: I think that Andrew is showing honest curiosity about what I might have in mind, he is interested in my way of expressing this. So I think it is important to respond.
atoms.extraction_notes: 治疗师明确认为当患者表现出好奇时，回应是重要的。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 帮助患者找到不同的表达方式
atoms.canonical_name_en: helping the patient find alternative ways of saying things
atoms.claim: 治疗师帮助患者找到不同的方式表达相同信息，以想象不会伤害他人。
clinical_signals: 患者以可能伤害他人的方式表达
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师引导患者思考如何换一种方式表达，并想象对方的感受
atoms.evidence_excerpt: And on how sometimes we can find different ways of saying the same thing, sort of giving the same message but in a different way… in a way that we can imagine won’t hurt the other person so much… you know, when we’ve been talking about putting yourself in the other person’s shoes.
atoms.extraction_notes: 治疗师明确提及帮助患者找到不同的表达方式，并想象不伤害他人。

atoms.claim: 患者能够识别在不同情境中引发他人拒绝的关系模式。
clinical_signals: 患者自发将当前情境与过去类似情境联系起来
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师可以强调患者这种识别模式的能力
atoms.evidence_excerpt: We see in the sequence how Andrew has been able to identify a relational pattern in which he elicits rejection from others in two different situations.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确描述患者识别了关系模式。

atoms.claim: 治疗师通过关注此时此地，检测、突出并重视有效的心智化。
clinical_signals: 来访者表现出有效的心智化
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应明确肯定和突出来访者有效的心智化表现
atoms.evidence_excerpt: We do it by focusing on the here and now, detecting, highlighting and valuing effective mentalizing
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确描述了这一技术步骤。

atoms.claim: 治疗师可以指出来访者当前的心智化方式与之前非心智化方式之间的差异。
clinical_signals: 来访者从非心智化转向心智化
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应帮助来访者看到两种思维方式的区别
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Look at how different it is from the way you were thinking just five minutes ago when you seemed so certain about what you were saying about such a person… instead, now you are wondering about how that person might feel when you do something like what you had done. Do you see the difference?
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文通过治疗师的话语展示了这一对比技术。

atoms.claim: 治疗师可以引导来访者思考如何以不同方式表达自己，以促进心智化。
clinical_signals: 来访者能够识别关系模式
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应鼓励来访者设想更有效的沟通方式
atoms.evidence_excerpt: So, can you think of another way you could have said this to the teacher?
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文中治疗师直接提问。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 治疗师作为心智化模型
atoms.claim: MBT方法要求治疗师将自己作为模型，使自己的内隐思维过程外显化，展示不完美、承认知识的局限，并对自己的和他人的心理状态保持好奇。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应公开反思自己的感受和想法，并询问他人的感受和想法
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The MBT approach implies offering ourselves as a model that makes our implicit thought processes explicit. In this way, we offer a model of someone who is not perfect, of someone who is aware of the fact that there are limits to our knowledge and is safe in acknowledging it: “I am curious because I know I do not know”.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确描述了这一立场。

atoms.claim: 治疗师应努力营造一种认识论信任的氛围，以恢复青少年的能动性和希望。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应通过展示好奇、承认无知、考虑不同视角来建立信任
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Above all, we try to promote an atmosphere of epistemic trust that restores the young person´s capacity for agency and hope.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确将认识论信任作为核心目标。

atoms.claim: 关系体验可以产生治疗效果，因为它有利于改变青少年对关系的可用性和心理态度，使他们更能接受周围已有的良性关系。
clinical_signals: 青少年对关系持负面预期
therapeutic_implications: 治疗关系本身可以促进青少年对关系的开放态度
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The relational experience can have a therapeutic effect because it favours a change in the adolescent’s availability and mental attitude towards relationships, so that they can be more open to being influenced by benign and benevolent relationships that they could already have in their surroundings, but were unable to see and benefit from.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确说明了关系体验的治疗作用。

atoms.claim: 关系体验可以产生治疗效果，因为它有利于改变青少年对关系的可用性和心理态度，使他们更能接受周围良性和善意的关系。
therapeutic_implications: 优先考虑改变临床团队自身的思维和网络
通过关系体验促进青少年的开放态度
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The relational experience can have a therapeutic effect because it favours a change in the adolescent’s availability and mental attitude towards relationships, so that they can be more open to being influenced by benign and benevolent relationships that they could already have in their surroundings, but were unable to see and benefit from.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述关系体验的治疗效果及其对青少年态度的影响。

atoms.claim: MBT方法意味着将自己作为一个模型，使我们的内隐思维过程外显化，展示一个不完美、承认知识有限的人。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应展示不完美和承认无知
外显化内隐思维过程
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The MBT approach implies offering ourselves as a model that makes our implicit thought processes explicit. In this way, we offer a model of someone who is not perfect, of someone who is aware of the fact that there are limits to our knowledge and is safe in acknowledging it: “I am curious because I know I do not know”.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述MBT中治疗师作为模型的做法。

atoms.claim: 治疗师提供对自己和他人心理状态的兴趣模型，包括反思感受和想法，并大声询问他人可能的感受和想法。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应外显化对心理状态的好奇
促进对他人心理状态的反思
atoms.evidence_excerpt: We also offer a model of interest in one’s own and others’ mental states, making reflections on how we might feel or what we think about a certain situation and asking ourselves out loud how the other person might feel and think.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述治疗师作为心理状态兴趣的模型。

atoms.claim: 我们努力促进一种认识论信任的氛围，恢复青少年的能动性和希望。
therapeutic_implications: 促进认识论信任
恢复青少年的能动性和希望
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Above all, we try to promote an atmosphere of epistemic trust that restores the young person´s capacity for agency and hope.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述促进认识论信任的目标。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 心理化失败导致适应不良行为
atoms.canonical_name_en: failure of mentalization leading to maladaptive behaviours
atoms.claim: MBT-A认为适应不良行为（如自伤、暴力、物质滥用）是心理化失败影响情绪调节能力的结果。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗应针对心理化失败以改善情绪调节
atoms.evidence_excerpt: MBT-A considers these maladaptive behaviours to be the result of the failure of mentalization impacting on the young person’s capacity to regulate affect
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述因果关系。

atoms.claim: MBT-A认为适应不良行为是心智化失败的结果，影响了青少年调节情感的能力。
therapeutic_implications: MBT-A旨在发展青少年对自己和他人心理状态的意识，增强心智化能力
atoms.evidence_excerpt: MBT-A considers these maladaptive behaviours to be the result of the failure of mentalization impacting on the young person’s capacity to regulate affect
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确将适应不良行为归因于心智化失败。

atoms.claim: 神经发育变化暂时损害了心智化能力，部分导致了心智化失败。
therapeutic_implications: MBT-A需考虑神经发育因素
atoms.evidence_excerpt: neurodevelopmental changes temporarily compromising mentalizing (Fonagy & Luyten, 2009).
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确提及神经发育变化暂时损害心智化。

atoms.claim: MBT-A治疗师需要身心俱在，舒适地注意、命名、处理和表达自己的情感状态，同时对他人的状态保持良性好奇。
clinical_signals: 青少年难以解读面部情绪表达
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师需示范反思性思考
response_constraints: 治疗师需表达自己的感知和体验
atoms.evidence_excerpt: MBT-A therapists need to be present in mind, body and soul. Recognising that adolescents can struggle to read the emotional expression on faces (Tahmasebi et al., 2012) therapists need to feel comfortable noticing, naming, processing and expressing their own affective states whilst being benignly curious about others.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述治疗师的心智化立场。

atoms.claim: 非防御性地使用幽默是强大的工具，能减轻紧张并增强成员间的联结。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师可适当使用幽默
response_constraints: 非防御性使用
atoms.evidence_excerpt: When used non-defensively, humour is a powerful tool, surprising the minds of others, reducing tension and increasing the bond amongst members.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述幽默的使用及其效果。

atoms.claim: 治疗师验证积极的心智化尝试，有助于建立有韧性的团体氛围。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应肯定青少年的心智化努力
atoms.evidence_excerpt: However big or small, therapists validate positive mentalizing attempts, helping to build a resilient group atmosphere
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确提及验证积极心智化尝试。

atoms.claim: 应避免长时间沉默，因为它们可能增加焦虑并损害心智化。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应主动打破沉默
主动打破沉默
降低焦虑
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Long silences are avoided as they are likely to raise anxiety and impair mentalizing.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明避免长时间沉默的原因。

atoms.claim: 非防御性地使用幽默可以让他人感到惊讶、降低紧张感并增强成员之间的联系。
therapeutic_implications: 使用幽默降低紧张感
增强团体凝聚力
response_constraints: 幽默必须是非防御性的
atoms.evidence_excerpt: When used non-defensively, humour is a powerful tool, surprising the minds of others, reducing tension and increasing the bond amongst members.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 验证积极的心智化尝试
atoms.claim: 治疗师验证积极的心智化尝试，有助于建立有韧性的团体氛围，并传达关心自己和他人重要性。
therapeutic_implications: 强化积极行为
建立团体韧性
atoms.evidence_excerpt: However big or small, therapists validate positive mentalizing attempts, helping to build a resilient group atmosphere and convey the importance of caring for oneself and others.

atoms.claim: 通过明确且具体的目标，并在团体开始前达成一致，来支持管理权威。
therapeutic_implications: 设定清晰目标
增强团体结构
response_constraints: 目标需在团体开始前达成一致
atoms.evidence_excerpt: ‘Managing authority’ (Karterud & Bateman, 2012) is supported by having clear and specific aims which are understood and agreed before the group commences.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 团体治疗师兼任个体治疗师
atoms.canonical_name_en: group therapists doubling as individual therapists
atoms.claim: 团体治疗师兼任参与者的个体治疗师，有助于建立连续性和凝聚力。
therapeutic_implications: 增强治疗连续性
增强团体凝聚力
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Group therapists double as participants’ individual therapists, which helps to build continuity and cohesion.

atoms.canonical_name_en: Remaining connected in moments of crisis
atoms.claim: 在危机时刻保持连接并寻求理解行为而非对其采取行动，对成功至关重要。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师需在危机中保持连接，努力理解行为而非控制
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Remaining connected in moments of crisis and seeking to understand behaviour and not act upon it is vital to success.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述在危机中保持连接和理解行为的重要性。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 治疗师对自身感受的觉察
atoms.claim: 治疗师需要觉察自己对患者的感受，并与同事和机构建立信任关系，以维持心智化。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师需建立信任关系，创造接纳、回应和心智化的氛围
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Being aware of our own feelings in response to our patients requires therapists to have trusting relationships with colleagues and the institutions within which we work.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述治疗师觉察自身感受并建立信任关系的必要性。

atoms.claim: 理想情况下，团体由一男一女两位治疗师带领，最多八名成员，每周在同一时间同一房间进行，缺席成员的椅子留在圈内以示铭记。
therapeutic_implications: 安排固定时间、地点和男女治疗师组合，保留缺席成员椅子
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Ideally, the two therapists will be a female-male couple with a maximum of eight members with the group taking place weekly at the same time and in the same room. The room is organised into a circle of chairs with absent members continuing to be held in mind by their chair remaining in the circle.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述团体设置和构成。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 团体治疗师兼任个体治疗师
atoms.canonical_name_en: Group therapists double as individual therapists
atoms.claim: 团体治疗师兼任参与者的个体治疗师，有助于建立连续性和凝聚力。
therapeutic_implications: 安排团体治疗师同时担任个体治疗师
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Group therapists double as participants’ individual therapists, which helps to build continuity and cohesion.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述双重角色对连续性和凝聚力的益处。

atoms.claim: 团体受益于拥有男性和女性参与者，以及多样化的新兴人格障碍类型，这提供了发展新视角和技能的机会。
therapeutic_implications: 招募不同性别和人格障碍类型的成员
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Groups benefit from having male and female participants with a diverse range of identified emerging personality disorders. This offers opportunities to develop new perspectives and skills;
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述多样性带来的益处。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 评估阶段建立心智化档案
atoms.canonical_name_en: Developing formulation and mentalizing profile during assessment
atoms.claim: 在评估阶段，治疗师需与青少年合作制定个案概念化和心智化档案，以支持其理解、动机和团体治疗参与。
therapeutic_implications: 评估阶段与青少年合作制定心智化档案
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It is essential that during the assessment phase therapists work collaboratively with the adolescent to develop a formulation and mentalizing profile that supports their understanding, motivation and participation in group treatment.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述评估阶段制定心智化档案的必要性。

atoms.claim: 停车技术是一种标记或注意到无法连接当下此刻的成员的方法，有助于管理唤醒、挑战非心智化时刻，并在有人被“停车”后尽快返回。
clinical_signals: 成员无法连接当下此刻
therapeutic_implications: 标记并暂时搁置无法参与的成员
尽快返回被停车的成员
response_constraints: 停车后应尽快返回
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The technique of ‘Parking’ is a way of marking or noticing someone who is not able to connect to what is happening in the here-and-now. It is helpful for managing arousal, challenging non-mentalizing moments and holding the group on a mentalizing trajectory when someone has been “parked” it is important to come back to them as soon as possible.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接描述停车技术及其目的和注意事项。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 招募其他成员帮助心智化
atoms.canonical_name_en: recruiting others into the mentalizing task
atoms.claim: 当一名成员无法表达时，治疗师可以招募其他成员帮助该成员进行心智化。
therapeutic_implications: 邀请其他成员帮助理解该成员的状态
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Kimberley says nothing and the therapist recruits others into the mentalizing task, helping Kimberley.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接描述治疗师招募其他成员帮助沉默的成员。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 标记并验证成员的感受
atoms.claim: 治疗师通过标记成员的感受（如羞耻感）并验证其合理性，可以降低成员的唤醒水平并促进连接。
therapeutic_implications: 标记感受
验证感受的合理性
降低唤醒
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Marking Kimberley’s rising affect the therapist answers, ‘No wonder you were having trouble being in the room, if you felt you were being criticised’. In validating Kimberley’s feelings of shame and sense of being wrong, the therapist gets alongside her, giving room for angry feelings but not agreeing it was her intention to leave Kimberley out. Kimberley’s arousal decreases and she makes eye contact.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接描述标记和验证感受后唤醒降低。

atoms.claim: 当成员无法连接时，治疗师可以暂停、搜索和倒带，以理解发生了什么导致成员感到“出局”。
therapeutic_implications: 暂停当前互动
搜索理解原因
倒带回顾
atoms.evidence_excerpt: ‘I can see you seem “out” Kimberley’, can we pause, search and rewind to try and understand what happened for you to feel “out”.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用治疗师的话。

atoms.claim: 治疗师通过匹配青少年的情感并好奇地探索其背后的原因，可以促进心智化。
therapeutic_implications: 匹配情感
好奇探索
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Matching Kelly’s affect the therapist wonders, ‘Wow! What is it about groups?’
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接描述治疗师匹配情感并好奇。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 肯定青少年的描述并分享治疗师自己的感受
atoms.canonical_name_en: affirming description and sharing own response
atoms.claim: 治疗师肯定青少年对自己体验的勇敢描述，同时分享自己的感受（如悲伤），可以促进心智化。
clinical_signals: 青少年描述保护性行为
therapeutic_implications: 肯定描述
分享治疗师感受
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The therapist affirms Kelly’s brave description of how she experiences herself with others whilst also noticing her own response to this. ‘I can see how you feel you’re protecting yourself from this “infection”. But when you were explaining this to me, I felt sad.’
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接描述肯定和分享感受。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 在评估阶段共同制定心智化档案
atoms.canonical_name_en: developing a formulation and mentalizing profile collaboratively
atoms.claim: 在评估阶段，治疗师与青少年合作制定一个心智化档案，以支持其理解、动机和参与团体治疗。
therapeutic_implications: 合作制定心智化档案
支持理解、动机和参与
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It is essential that during the assessment phase therapists work collaboratively with the adolescent to develop a formulation and mentalizing profile that supports their understanding, motivation and participation in group treatment.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接描述评估阶段合作制定心智化档案。

atoms.claim: 停车技术是一种标记或注意到无法连接当下此时此地的成员的方法，有助于管理唤醒、挑战非心智化时刻，并使小组保持在心智化轨道上。
clinical_signals: 成员无法连接当下此时此地
therapeutic_implications: 标记并暂时搁置无法连接的成员
尽快回到该成员
response_constraints: 使用非指责的方式
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The technique of ‘Parking’ is a way of marking or noticing someone who is not able to connect to what is happening in the here-and-now. It is helpful for managing arousal, challenging non-mentalizing moments and holding the group on a mentalizing trajectory when someone has been “parked” it is important to come back to them as soon as possible.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了停车技术的定义和用途。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 招募他人参与心智化任务
atoms.canonical_name_en: recruiting others into the mentalizing task
atoms.claim: 当一名成员无法连接时，治疗师可以招募其他小组成员帮助该成员心智化。
therapeutic_implications: 邀请其他成员提供观察和帮助
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Kimberley says nothing and the therapist recruits others into the mentalizing task, helping Kimberley.
atoms.extraction_notes: 示例中明确展示了招募他人的技术。

atoms.claim: 验证成员的羞耻感和被否定感，治疗师站在成员一边，为愤怒情绪留出空间，但不认同其意图。
therapeutic_implications: 验证感受
降低唤醒
促进眼神接触
response_constraints: 不认同意图
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In validating Kimberley’s feelings of shame and sense of being wrong, the therapist gets alongside her, giving room for angry feelings but not agreeing it was her intention to leave Kimberley out. Kimberley’s arousal decreases and she makes eye contact.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了验证感受及其效果。

atoms.claim: 三角化是邀请小组中的另一个人就他人描述的问题或他人之间的互动给出自己的观点，要么从自己的视角，要么从对他人视角的理解出发。
therapeutic_implications: 邀请其他成员提供观点
atoms.evidence_excerpt: This is working towards triangulation, ‘asking another person in the group to give his view on the problems described by others or on the interaction between others, either from his own perspective or from his understanding of their perspective’ (Bateman, Kongerslev, & Bo, 2019).
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确引用了三角化的定义。

atoms.claim: 治疗师使用自我，反思自己的心智化崩溃，明确表达对自己的理解。
clinical_signals: 治疗师自身心智化崩溃
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师反思并表达自我理解
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Here, therapist use of self enables the therapist to reflect on her own mentalizing breakdown making explicit her understanding of herself.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了治疗师使用自我的概念。

atoms.claim: 表达性活动可整合到小组结构中，以适应小组的心智化能力，用于促进对心理状态的思考。
therapeutic_implications: 使用猜测游戏、讨论视频片段、角色扮演和艺术创作等创造性干预
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Expressive activities have a long history of use in MBT models and can be integrated into the group structure to adapt to the group’s mentalizing abilities. Guessing games, discussing video clips, role-plays and artmaking are but a few ways in which creative interventions have been employed to promote thinking about mental states.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了表达性活动的用途和例子。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 早期心理教育小组中的表达性活动
atoms.canonical_name_en: expressive activities in early psychoeducation groups
atoms.claim: 在早期心理教育小组中，表达性活动常用于阐明内隐和外显心智化的动态性质，以及我们如何容易基于行为做出假设。
therapeutic_implications: 使用表达性活动阐明心智化动态
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In early psychoeducation groups, these activities are often used to illuminate the dynamic nature of implicit and explicit mentalizing and how easily we can make assumptions based on behaviour.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确提到了早期心理教育小组中的使用。

atoms.claim: 以非指责的方式运用这些技术，能营造安全的团体环境，让成员在此时此地工作，并保持情感焦点，同时探索相关的人际困难。
therapeutic_implications: 营造安全的团体环境
促进此时此地的工作
维持情感焦点
探索人际困难
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Employed in a non-blaming manner, these techniques foster a safe group environment for members to work in the here-and-now and maintain an affective focus whilst exploring relevant interpersonal difficulties.

atoms.claim: 表达性活动在MBT模型中有着悠久的使用历史，可以整合到团体结构中，以适应团体的心智化能力。
therapeutic_implications: 适应团体的心智化能力
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Expressive activities have a long history of use in MBT models and can be integrated into the group structure to adapt to the group’s mentalizing abilities.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 表达性活动创造安全距离
atoms.claim: 表达性活动为探索情感创造了安全距离，否则这些情感可能会被体验为压倒性的。
therapeutic_implications: 为探索情感创造安全距离
防止情感被体验为压倒性
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Expressive activities create a safe distance for the exploration of feelings, which might otherwise be experienced as overwhelming.

atoms.claim: 治疗师使用自我使治疗师能够反思自己的心智化崩溃，并明确表达对自己的理解。
therapeutic_implications: 促进治疗师反思自身心智化崩溃
明确表达治疗师的自我理解
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Here, therapist use of self enables the therapist to reflect on her own mentalizing breakdown making explicit her understanding of herself.

atoms.claim: 三角化是指请团体中的另一个人就他人描述的问题或他人之间的互动给出自己的看法，可以从自己的视角或从对他人视角的理解出发。
therapeutic_implications: 促进多视角理解
atoms.evidence_excerpt: This is working towards triangulation, ‘asking another person in the group to give his view on the problems described by others or on the interaction between others, either from his own perspective or from his understanding of their perspective’ (Bateman, Kongerslev, & Bo, 2019).

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 温和忽略非心智化评论
atoms.claim: 治疗师温和地忽略最初的非心智化评论，然后询问团体成员对场景的想象。
therapeutic_implications: 避免直接对抗
引导团体转向心智化探索
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Gently ignoring the initial non-mentalizing comment therapist one asks, ‘What do people imagine is happening here?’

atoms.claim: 表达性活动为探索感受创造了安全距离，否则这些感受可能被体验为压倒性的。
clinical_signals: 感受可能被体验为压倒性的
therapeutic_implications: 使用表达性活动创造安全距离
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Expressive activities create a safe distance for the exploration of feelings, which might otherwise be experienced as overwhelming.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 表达性活动支持从内隐到外显的反思
atoms.canonical_name_en: expressive activities support movement from implicit to explicit reflection
atoms.claim: 表达性活动支持从内隐知道到外显反思的转变。
therapeutic_implications: 使用表达性活动促进从内隐到外显的反思
atoms.evidence_excerpt: with the expressive activity supporting the movement from implicit knowing to explicit reflection.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 表达性活动增强自我能动感
atoms.canonical_name_en: expressive activities enhance sense of self-agency
atoms.claim: 当外显心智化能力减弱时，使用纸、黏土或积木等表达性活动可以增强青少年的自我能动感。
therapeutic_implications: 使用表达性活动增强自我能动感
atoms.evidence_excerpt: When explicit mentalizing capacities are diminished, the opportunity to put on paper, use clay or building blocks to capture some of the young person’s thoughts and feelings, can empower the young person positively impacting on their sense of self-agency.

atoms.claim: 在假性模式中，成员看似共情地回应（如“我完全有同感”），但伴随冗长描述，缺乏情感或对感受层面的理解，导致空虚和无意义感。
clinical_signals: 过度使用言语创造情感距离
therapeutic_implications: 挑战非心智化而不进一步分裂认知和情感
从身体开始，注意感觉，在心智化感觉层面逐步建立心智化图景
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Such statements are often accompanied with lengthy descriptions which fail to capture any affect or make sense of what might be happening on a felt level. Missing is a genuine curiosity with excessive use of words creating an emotional distance leading to feelings of emptiness and meaninglessness.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 利用治疗师自身感受突破假性模式
atoms.canonical_name_en: using therapist's own feelings to break through pretend mode
atoms.claim: 治疗师利用自身感受并在试图理解他人的背景下表达这些感受，可以帮助他人接触自己的感受并突破假性模式。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师表达自身感受以促进他人感受接触
atoms.evidence_excerpt: As a therapist using our own feelings and expressing these in the context of trying to understand another can enable others to get in touch with their own feelings and ‘breakthrough’ Pretend Mode.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 适当提高焦虑水平以突破假性模式
atoms.canonical_name_en: raising anxiety to break through pretend mode
atoms.claim: 有时可以通过提高一点焦虑和唤醒水平，将情绪状态带到前台，从而突破假性模式。
therapeutic_implications: 适当提高焦虑和唤醒水平
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Sometimes this can involve raising a bit of anxiety and heating up the arousal level to bring emotional states to the forefront (Muller & Midgley, 2020).

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 治疗师容忍被视为“可悲”以促进团体参与
atoms.canonical_name_en: therapists tolerate being seen as 'pathetic' to promote group engagement
atoms.claim: 在MBT-A团体中，治疗师可以容忍被视为“可悲”，并专注于他们的“场景”，使团体成员感到较少抑制并能够回应。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师容忍被视为可悲
专注于治疗师场景
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The therapists can tolerate looking ‘pathetic’ and with the focus on their ‘scene’, group members feel less inhibited and able to respond.

atoms.claim: 在假装模式中，成员看似共情地回应，但缺乏真正的好奇心，过度使用言语造成情感距离，导致空虚和无意义感。
clinical_signals: 成员说'哦，是的，我完全有同感'
冗长的描述但缺乏情感
therapeutic_implications: 挑战非心智化而不进一步分裂认知和情感
从身体开始，注意感觉，在感官层面心智化
通过注意和命名逐步建立心智化图景
治疗师使用自己的感受并表达出来以帮助他人接触感受
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Such statements are often accompanied with lengthy descriptions which fail to capture any affect or make sense of what might be happening on a felt level. Missing is a genuine curiosity with excessive use of words creating an emotional distance leading to feelings of emptiness and meaninglessness.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 在假装模式中提高唤醒水平
atoms.canonical_name_en: Raising arousal level in Pretend Mode
atoms.claim: 有时可以通过提高一点焦虑和加热唤醒水平来将情绪状态带到前台，从而突破假装模式。
therapeutic_implications: 提高焦虑和唤醒水平以将情绪状态带到前台
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Sometimes this can involve raising a bit of anxiety and heating up the arousal level to bring emotional states to the forefront (Muller & Midgley, 2020).

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 通过图像促进共同注意和好奇心
atoms.canonical_name_en: Using images to promote shared joint attention and curiosity
atoms.claim: 单独观看图像，促进对某物的共同注意，容纳强烈的情感和关系动力，鼓励成员对图像保持好奇。
therapeutic_implications: 观看图像以促进共同注意
鼓励对图像的好奇
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The images are viewed individually, promoting shared joint attention on something else, holding powerful feelings and relational dynamics. Eye contact increases and therapists encourage members to be curious about the images.

atoms.claim: 治疗师应紧贴青少年，提供共情验证，以激发好奇心和差异。
clinical_signals: 青少年处于心理等价模式
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师需要紧贴青少年，提供共情验证，以激发好奇心和差异
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The therapeutic task is to get right alongside the adolescent offering empathic validation in the hope of stimulating some curiosity and difference.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接描述治疗任务。

atoms.claim: 治疗师使用侧站技术，同时支持双方感受，并将焦点从他们身上转移到治疗师对互动的想象体验上。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师同时支持双方感受
将焦点从当事人转移到治疗师对互动的想象体验上
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Trying to regulate the growing arousal they use the technique of siding, whereby they side with the feelings of both Fatima and Rob whilst also taking the focus away from them and onto the therapist’s imagined experience of the interaction.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接描述侧站技术。

atoms.claim: 治疗师需要承受青少年的愤怒等情感，同时牢记青少年可能感到害怕且无法明确心智化。
clinical_signals: 青少年愤怒指责治疗师
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师承受青少年的情感
牢记青少年可能害怕且无法明确心智化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The therapist endured Fatima’s feelings of anger, holding in mind how Fatima was possibly frightened, unable to explicitly mentalize with the therapist she felt was at war with her.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接描述治疗师的态度。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 青少年群体中的心理等价模式
atoms.claim: 在青少年群体中，心理等价模式可能导致成员难以创造差异空间，并因害怕不同而附和。
clinical_signals: 成员难以创造差异空间
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师需帮助青少年注意这一模式
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The therapists have recognised this pattern of relating emerging in the group with members finding it difficult to create a space for difference, often agreeing with Fatima.
atoms.extraction_notes: 案例中描述青少年群体中的模式。

atoms.claim: 治疗师使用侧边技术，同时支持双方感受，并将焦点从他们身上转移到治疗师对互动的想象体验上。
therapeutic_implications: 通过支持双方感受并转移焦点来调节唤醒水平
保护双方成员
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Trying to regulate the growing arousal they use the technique of siding, whereby they side with the feelings of both Fatima and Rob whilst also taking the focus away from them and onto the therapist’s imagined experience of the interaction.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 在个体治疗中探索并承担责任
atoms.canonical_name_en: exploring and taking responsibility in individual session
atoms.claim: 当团体干预导致误解时，治疗师应在个体治疗中探索此事，并为自己在误解中的角色承担责任。
therapeutic_implications: 在个体治疗中探索事件
治疗师承认自己的责任
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The team agreed it was important to explore this with Fatima in her individual session and for the therapist to take responsibility for their part in the misunderstanding.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 忍受患者的愤怒并保持心智化
atoms.claim: 治疗师需要忍受患者的愤怒，同时保持心智化，理解患者可能感到害怕但无法明确表达。
clinical_signals: 患者将治疗师比作批评性父母
therapeutic_implications: 忍受愤怒
保持心智化
理解患者潜在的恐惧
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The therapist endured Fatima’s feelings of anger, holding in mind how Fatima was possibly frightened, unable to explicitly mentalize with the therapist she felt was at war with her.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 鼓励暂停并澄清听到的内容
atoms.canonical_name_en: encouraging pause and clarifying what was heard
atoms.claim: 当患者准备离开时，治疗师鼓励暂停，并请患者澄清听到他人说了什么。
therapeutic_implications: 鼓励暂停
要求澄清听到的内容
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The therapist encourages Kelly to pause, looking as though she is about to leave, ‘Whoa, wait Kelly, please I’d like you to stay… what is it you’ve heard Tamara say?’

atoms.claim: 青少年在目的论模式中，情绪难以识别，感觉与想法混淆，行动不假思索以改变难以忍受的内在状态。
therapeutic_implications: 关注潜在情绪状态
区分感觉与想法
反思人际体验
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Often emotions are hard to recognise, feelings are confused with thoughts, and actions occur without thinking in an attempt to shift intolerable internal states.

atoms.claim: 治疗师可以通过提问（如“然后呢？”）来挑战青少年关于治疗应无限延长的目的论要求，从而促进心智化。
clinical_signals: 青少年要求具体行动（如延长治疗时间）
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师可以分享困境并邀请小组讨论
使用温和的挑战来探索潜在感受
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Taking a risk one of the therapists playfully challenges, ‘And then what?’
atoms.extraction_notes: 案例中治疗师通过提问挑战目的论要求。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 治疗结束时的非心智化模式重现
atoms.canonical_name_en: re-emergence of non-mentalizing patterns at ending
atoms.claim: 在治疗结束时，随着新形成的依恋纽带因分离和告别过程而受到压力，早期非心智化模式很可能重新出现。
therapeutic_implications: 需要给予足够时间处理结束
让离开的个体和剩余组员考虑各种感受
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The re-emergence of earlier non-mentalizing patterns are likely as newly formed attachment bonds are strained under the process of separating and saying goodbye.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述治疗结束时非心智化模式重现。

atoms.claim: 结束治疗可能是一个困难和情绪化的经历，团体可能表达低落情绪和悲伤，开始哀悼成员的离开。
therapeutic_implications: 需要给予足够时间处理结束过程
让离开者和剩余成员考虑各种感受
atoms.evidence_excerpt: ending therapy can be a difficult and emotive experience. It is not uncommon for the group to express low mood and feelings of sadness, as they begin to mourn the loss of a group member.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述结束治疗的情绪反应。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 结束治疗中的非心智化模式重现
atoms.canonical_name_en: re-emergence of non-mentalizing patterns in ending therapy
atoms.claim: 在结束治疗过程中，随着新形成的依恋纽带因分离和告别而紧张，早期非心智化模式可能重现。
therapeutic_implications: 需要识别并处理非心智化模式
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The re-emergence of earlier non-mentalizing patterns are likely as newly formed attachment bonds are strained under the process of separating and saying goodbye.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明非心智化模式重现的原因。

atoms.claim: 支持离开的成员反思他们在团体中的时间，要求他们给其他成员写一张卡片，卡片留在团体治疗室，供剩余和新成员阅读。
therapeutic_implications: 促进反思
提供表达性活动
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In supporting leaving members to reflect on their time in the group, they are asked to write a card to their fellow group members. These cards remain in the group therapy room, enabling remaining and new members to read the goodbye messages of the previous group members.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述告别卡片的使用方法。

atoms.claim: 告别卡片等表达性活动可以刺激患者反思他们的治疗过程。
therapeutic_implications: 使用表达性活动促进反思
atoms.evidence_excerpt: This chapter concludes with the goodbye letter 19-year-old Annju wrote at the end of treatment, which describes how this expressive activity can stimulate patient reflection on their therapeutic process.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明表达性活动的作用。

atoms.claim: 在青少年团体中，结束治疗时团体可能表达低落情绪和悲伤，非心智化模式可能重现。
therapeutic_implications: 给予足够时间处理结束
讨论感受
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It is not uncommon for the group to express low mood and feelings of sadness, as they begin to mourn the loss of a group member. The re-emergence of earlier non-mentalizing patterns are likely as newly formed attachment bonds are strained under the process of separating and saying goodbye.
atoms.extraction_notes: 内容明确针对青少年团体。

atoms.claim: 认识论信任是通过青少年体验到被看见、被理解（即被准确心智化）而赢得的。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Research into Epistemic Trust suggests that this is ‘won’ when the young person experiences themselves as being seen (re-cognised) and understood; mentalized accurately, as it were.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确陈述了认识论信任的获得条件。

atoms.claim: 一般精神病理学因子（P因子）可能是个体认识论信任适应性差的代理指标。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Ideas about the General Psychopathology Factor (“P-Factor”, Caspi et al., 2014) have led to the proposal that this transdiagnostic approach to the risk of chronicity and treatment resistance in an individual may in fact be a proxy measure for this disposition; one of poor or low adaptability of a person’s Epistemic Trust.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文提出P因子可能是认识论信任适应性差的代理指标，属于强烈暗示。

atoms.claim: 那些常被服务描述为“难以接触”的青少年，实际上可能更应被描述为“服务不足”：他们得到的帮助（通常是大剂量、复杂且昂贵的）很少被体验为有帮助，他们的拒绝在某种意义上是有目的且适应性的。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The vignette above is a typical example of the ‘dis-integration’ of the care system around those challenging young people, who are frequently described as “hard to reach” by services, although in truth they might better be described as “under-served”: the help that is offered to them (often in large, complex, and expensive ‘doses’) is rarely experienced as helpful, and their rejection of it is, in that sense at least, purposeful and adaptive.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确将“难以接触”重新定义为“服务不足”，并指出拒绝帮助是有目的且适应性的。

atoms.claim: 对于认识论过度警觉的青少年，帮助之门对专业帮助者紧闭，却对毒品贩子、帮派头目等黑暗社会代表敞开，这些黑暗角色似乎更容易被他们不加批判地理解和接受。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Paradoxically, while the doors to help seem firmly closed to professional helpers, they can appear frustratingly (or worryingly) open to the representatives of the darker side of society: drug dealers, gang leaders, delinquent peers and adults who might want to exploit them. Something about these darker characters (who the young person may, in truth, identify as their existing network of ‘help’) seems much easier for them to understand and accept uncritically.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确描述了这一悖论。

atoms.claim: 认知信任在青少年体验到被看见、被理解（即被准确心智化）时被“赢得”。
clinical_signals: 青少年对帮助持高度警惕
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师需要准确心智化青少年，以建立认知信任
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Research into Epistemic Trust suggests that this is ‘won’ when the young person experiences themselves as being seen (re-cognised) and understood; mentalized accurately, as it were.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述认知信任如何被赢得。

atoms.claim: AMBIT是一种系统性的方法，旨在围绕困境青少年及其家庭发展和调整帮助系统，使其更有帮助、更被使用、更有效。
clinical_signals: 青少年问题复杂、高风险、低参与度
therapeutic_implications: 服务应关注青少年对帮助本身的关系
促进多机构协作
atoms.evidence_excerpt: AMBIT is less a concrete (teleological) organisational model and more a systematic approach to the development and adaptation of systems of help around troubled adolescents and their families so that these can be experienced as more helpful, and thus be better used and more effective
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接描述AMBIT的本质。

atoms.claim: 这些青少年可能有多重精神科诊断、学校问题、社交问题、反社会问题，并涉及多种服务，如警察、毒品服务、医疗、社会关怀等。
therapeutic_implications: 需要协调多系统合作
atoms.evidence_excerpt: These young people may have had several psychiatric classifications, problems at school, social problems (peer group relationships) and antisocial problems (gangs and offending), so that police and drug services, or acute medical services who are called upon to address their self-injurious behaviours, are often a part of the mix along with social care, educational inclusion services, and forensic or youth offending services.
atoms.extraction_notes: 描述青少年问题的复杂性。

atoms.claim: 帮助系统本身的复杂性可能加剧青少年的复杂性和停滞状态。
clinical_signals: 多机构介入但效果不佳
therapeutic_implications: 需要减少系统复杂性
促进服务间一致性
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Paradoxically, the very complexity of these helping systems can amplify and indeed exacerbate the complexity and stasis.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述系统复杂性的负面影响。

atoms.claim: AMBIT影响下的服务可能将其更基本的任务视为能够解决来访者的慢性认识论警觉——解决来访者与帮助本身的关系。
therapeutic_implications: 服务需关注来访者与帮助的关系
建立认识论信任
atoms.evidence_excerpt: an AMBIT-influenced service may see its more fundamental task as being able to address this chronic Epistemic Hypervigilance in their clients – to address their clients’ relationship to help itself.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述AMBIT服务的基本任务

atoms.claim: 认识论信任不尊重专业角色、权威或培训——年轻人可能更容易与低薪、系统上被忽视的寄宿护理人员建立认识论信任，而不是与昂贵的、高资质的治疗师。
clinical_signals: 与某些工作者建立信任困难
therapeutic_implications: 重视非专业关系中的信任建立
降低对专业角色的依赖
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Epistemic Trust shows no respect for a professional role, authority, or training – a young person may find it much easier to develop some epistemic trust in a low paid, systemically-overlooked residential care worker than in an expensive, highly qualified therapist with multiple degrees and diplomas!
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述认识论信任的特点

atoms.claim: 在压力下，工作者变得目的论化，权力斗争常常被暗中或有时公开地演绎。
therapeutic_implications: 支持工作者保持心智化
减少跨机构冲突
atoms.evidence_excerpt: They become teleological, and power struggles are often enacted, covertly or sometimes overtly.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述工作者在压力下进入目的论模式

atoms.claim: AMBIT是一套系统应用的原则和方法，旨在帮助工作人员更容易识别服务系统何时解体（停止相互心智化），并拥有干预工具以恢复心智化。
therapeutic_implications: 使用AMBIT工具恢复心智化
系统层面的干预
atoms.evidence_excerpt: AMBIT can best be described as a set of principles and methods applied systemically that stimulate awareness of the above problems and help staff working with these kinds of clients to recognise more easily when and where the service systems dis-integrate (stop mentalizing each other), and then have tools to intervene to restore mentalizing.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述AMBIT的定义和功能

atoms.claim: 大多数这些年轻人有依恋系统受损的历史；他们很少拥有安全依恋模型来支持与专业人员建立帮助性治疗关系。
therapeutic_implications: 需要特别关注依恋问题
建立信任需耐心
atoms.evidence_excerpt: most of these young people have a history in which their attachment systems have been compromised; they rarely have a model of secure attachment that they can use to support the task of building a helping therapeutic relationship with a professional.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述青少年依恋系统受损

atoms.claim: 如果儿童的依恋系统是紊乱的，心智化能力的发展尤其受到抑制。
therapeutic_implications: 早期干预依恋问题
促进心智化发展
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The development of mentalizing capacity (see Chapter 1) is inhibited particularly if a child’s attachment system is disorganised (Fonagy & Target, 2005).
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述依恋紊乱对心智化发展的影响

atoms.claim: 我们在不可避免的压力条件下工作，尽管我们尽力心智化，但这种能力变得脆弱。
therapeutic_implications: 支持工作者应对压力
提供心智化支持
atoms.evidence_excerpt: we work in conditions where stress is inevitable, and where despite our best efforts to mentalize, this capacity is rendered fragile.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述工作者心智化能力的脆弱性

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 心智化能力的社会依赖性
atoms.claim: 心智化能力是个人社会联结程度的衡量标准，至少与个体或二元现象同等重要。
therapeutic_implications: 干预应关注增强个体的社会网络，而不仅仅是个体或二元关系
atoms.evidence_excerpt: mentalizing capacity as a measure of a person’s social connectedness (at least as much as it is an individual or dyadic phenomenon).
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确将心智化能力定义为社会联结的衡量标准。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 社会网络对心智化的支持
atoms.canonical_name_en: network of benign minds supporting mentalizing
atoms.claim: 母亲能够心智化其哭闹的婴儿，前提是她至少拥有一个其他心智网络的概念，这些心智能够、愿意或确实将她的心智放在心上。
therapeutic_implications: 工作者需要获得支持性网络以维持自身心智化能力
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The mother can only mentalize her screaming infant insofar as she has at least the idea of a network of other minds that can, would, or do hold her own mind in mind: her own mother, her partner, her friend, the health visitor, etc.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文以母亲为例说明心智化依赖于支持性网络。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 社会稀疏化与潜在脆弱性
atoms.claim: 潜在脆弱性随着社会稀疏化而直接增加，个体发现越来越难以接触到良性的、具有心智化的心智。
therapeutic_implications: 干预应致力于防止或逆转社会稀疏化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: a latent vulnerability that increases in direct relation to “social thinning” (McCrory, 2019), so that across time an individual, through neurodevelopmental vulnerability, trauma, or symptomatic illness, finds they have less and less access to benign and mentalizing minds.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确将潜在脆弱性与社会稀疏化联系起来。

atoms.claim: AMBIT是一种团队方法，尽管它强调可能产生认识信任的强个体关键关系。
therapeutic_implications: 干预应基于团队，同时培养关键个体关系
atoms.evidence_excerpt: AMBIT is a team approach, even though it emphasises strong individual “key” relationships where epistemic trust may arise.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确将AMBIT描述为团队方法。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 认识信任与专业角色无关
